### D492. The mainnet demo binds every Sodax deposit's spoke `to` to the signing address's own hub wallet
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-09; the swap's output bound too and its minimum shown, approved by the owner 2026-11-09 · Built on `fix/demo-swap-hub-wallet`, not merged, not deployed (`packages/core/src/mainnet-demo.ts` `checkSodaxHubCalls`, `checkSpokeHubWallet`, `checkSwapIntent`, `ownRecipient`, `DemoSwap`, `DemoRoute`; `packages/web/src/vault/signing.ts`; `packages/web/src/auth/approve-page.ts`) · Amends D429 point 3 and closes the destination part of the spec's R5, with a row of "Superseded or amended".
- Decision: every Sodax spoke deposit the demo signs, on Base and on Stellar (a swap's two hub calls, a bridge's four, an empty-data deposit, native or token), is refused unless its spoke `to` is exactly the signing address's own hub wallet (20 bytes). Same offline derivation as D476 (`sodaxHubWalletOf`, keyed by the chain the deposit is on). The check sits first in `checkSodaxHubCalls`, before the `data` is read, and a call without the spoke side is refused. `assessMainnetDemo` runs it in the vault before any popup and in the popup's own read of the bytes (`'shown'` mode needs only the signing address), so a wrong `to` gets the cap line and no value there. 
- Decision, a swap's intent (`checkSwapIntent`, on the `createIntent` hub call), read from `EvmSolverService.constructCreateIntentData` and `encodeAddress`:
  - `creator` must be the signing address's own hub wallet (the SDK sets `creatorHubWalletAddress`, the spoke `to` above).
  - `srcChain` must be the deposit chain's relay id, `srcAddress` the signing address encoded as the SDK does (20 bytes on Base, the 44-byte SCV_ADDRESS XDR on Stellar).
  - `dstChain` must be 30 (Base) or 27 (Stellar), and `dstAddress` canonical for that chain and equal to the session's own address on it, compared in the encoded form, as a bridge's recipient (`{ wallets }` in the vault). The popup holds only the signing chain's address, so `'shown'` reads the recipient without binding it, as for a bridge. A swap within one chain (Base to Base) is allowed, to the user's own wallet there. No `wallets` and no `'shown'`: refused.
  - `solver` must be the zero address (any solver). The SDK defaults to it and the sample passes it. A named solver could be the page's own, and it alone would fill the intent at the minimum output.
  - `data` must be empty. The SDK's `composeIntentData` gives `0x` with no partner fee and no delivery hook. A fee envelope carries a fee amount and a receiver, so a page could otherwise route part or all of the input to itself. This also refuses a swap with a partner fee or a delivery hook (a hook also replaces `dstAddress`).
  - `allowPartialFill` must be false: the SDK passes the caller's value and the sample always sends false, and otherwise the shown minimum wouldn't be a total. Refused as `mainnet_demo_unknown_call`.
  - `deadline` must be non-zero and at most one hour ahead of the server-corrected time (the same clock the rest of the check uses; the popup's own clock in the popup). The sample sets now + 10 minutes (`DEADLINE_SECONDS`) and the SDK's default offset is 5 minutes (`DEFAULT_DEADLINE_OFFSET`), so an hour leaves 50 minutes for a page clock running ahead. A deadline of 0 is Sodax's limit order, which has no expiry; with an unfillable minimum it would lock the funds, and the demo won't sign a cancel. Refused as `mainnet_demo_unknown_call`. A deadline already past isn't refused: that intent can't be filled and doesn't lock anything for longer.
  - `outputToken` must be the hub asset of an asset the demo lists on the destination chain (ETH, USDC, EURC on Base; XLM, USDC, EURC on Stellar), which is exactly what the sample's six tokens resolve to.
  - Refusal reasons: a wrong hub wallet, recipient, creator, source address or chain is the new `mainnet_demo_wrong_destination` (4100, before any popup; the launcher says `Refused: this sends funds to a wallet that isn’t yours (mainnet demo)`), so the user isn't told Hana "can't tell how much" it moves. A wrong solver, data or output asset stays `mainnet_demo_unknown_call`. Older SDKs pass `data.reason` through unchanged.
- Decision, the popup: below the value line, `Swap on Sodax. Recipient on Stellar: G…`, from the popup's own decoding of the bytes through the same function, shown only once its checks pass (hub wallet, creator, source, destination form, solver, data, output asset). No protocol change, as for D476.
- Decision, the popup's minimum: below the recipient line, `Minimum you receive: 1.234 USDC`, the intent's `minOutputAmount` as plain text, from the popup's own decoding and only once its checks pass. It changes nothing the vault accepts: no new refusal. The decimals and symbol are the pinned list's (`MAINNET_DEMO`: ETH 18, USDC and EURC 6 on Base; XLM, USDC and EURC 7 on Stellar), for the asset whose hub asset is the intent's `outputToken`, so a value is shown only for a listed asset. Confirmed from `@sodax/sdk` 2.2.0: each spoke token's entry carries `decimals` and its `hubAsset`; `getQuote` says `quoted_amount` is in the destination token's smallest unit; `constructCreateIntentData` passes `minOutputAmount` through with no scaling for any token. Cross-checked read-only on Sonic (`eth_call` through `rpc.soniclabs.com`, 2026-11-09): the Soda vaults' `tokenInfo` gives ETH 18, Base USDC 6, XLM 7, Stellar USDC 7. EURC rests on the SDK alone: its `vault` in the SDK's config is the hub asset itself and `tokenInfo` on it reverts. The hub assets' own `decimals()` answer 0 for all six, so they say nothing about the units.
- Why: the popup names no recipient for a swap or a plain deposit, so a compromised page on the allowed app could send up to $9.99 to another hub wallet and the user had nothing to see. D476 closed this for bridges only; the derivation was already offline and needed nothing new.
- What the SDK does, confirmed from `@sodax/sdk` 2.2.0's code: `createIntent` (`index.mjs` ~31371, ~31411) sets `to` to `getUserHubWalletAddress(walletAddress, srcChainKey)`, with `walletAddress` the source address on both Base and Stellar, and the spoke deposit passes `to` through unchanged (`EvmSpokeService.deposit`, `StellarSpokeService.buildDepositCall`, which pass the 20 bytes as given). `createBridgeIntent` does the same (`to: hubWallet`, ~36256). The sample's only Sodax deposits are those two; its Stellar trustline and ERC-20 approve aren't deposits. Run with fetch blocked (no `api.sodax.com`) and only the hub-wallet read stubbed, the SDK's own Base swap passes `assessMainnetDemo`.
- What it refuses that was signable before: a deposit whose `to` is not the signer's own hub wallet, including an empty-data deposit funding someone else's hub wallet; a swap delivered to someone else or to another chain; a swap with a partner fee, a delivery hook or a named solver; a swap into an asset the demo doesn't list. No SDK path the sample uses does any of these: all 18 cross-chain pairs of its six tokens, built by the SDK's own encoder offline, pass in both vault and popup modes. Sodax's DEX deposit with a `dst` override (~38590, `to` the recipient's hub wallet) was already refused by the hub-call shape, and isn't used here.
- Not enforced: the intent's `minOutputAmount` (shown in the popup, above), and not bound: its `intentId`, and an input amount below the approval (the difference stays in the user's own hub wallet). These are the swap's terms, not where it goes. A byte-by-byte run over the SDK's swap calldata (2026-11-09) shows only these fields, the deposit amount's low bytes and a deadline inside its limit stay accepted. The one that matters: a compromised page can set the minimum output to almost nothing, so a filler could take the whole deposit for dust. The popup now shows the minimum, so the user can see it before approving, and it is bounded by the $9.99 cap per transaction. Hana's prices are ceilings, so a floor check would need a separate decision.
- A factory upgrade that changes the derivation now refuses every Sodax deposit, not only bridges, until the formula is reviewed and rebuilt (fail closed; nothing is signed). The upgrade risk is D476's.

- Note, 2026-11-09: only the vault applies the deadline's one-hour limit. The popup uses the device's clock, which could disagree and hide a swap's recipient and minimum, so it applies only the non-zero check.

### D493. The watchdog pins the exit list and pages on the hourly counter; an unpinned client in force pauses
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built: `apps/watchdog/src/run.ts` `exitClients`,
  `apps/watchdog/src/pins.ts` `parseExitPins`, `packages/env/src/schema.ts` `watchdog.pinnedExitClients`,
  `exitAlertPerHour` · For D468, D487 · Reads the design's "critical diff, plus a pinned expected value" (section 2) and
  "a watchdog pin mismatch is then critical and triggers a pause" (section 4)
- Decision: the lists (`exit_clients`, `pending_exit_clients`) go in the watchdog's critical diff, as the design says, and
  the manifest pins the expected list (`watchdog.pinnedExitClients`; `EXIT_PINS`). A client on chain not in the pins is
  critical (`exit_client_unpinned`): pending, alert only (it isn't in force, and the council removes it free, D483); in
  force, the watchdog pauses (design section 4), as it does for an unpinned active issuer key. A pinned client on neither
  list is a warning (`exit_client_missing`), since it is true both before the client is proposed and after an emergency
  removal (D483). The counter isn't a diffable value, so it pages by threshold instead: `exit_window.current` or `previous`
  at or above `watchdog.exitAlertPerHour` (default 20, provisional; the contract never refuses) is critical
  `exit_volume_high`, and so are the two hours together at 1.5 times that level, rounded up (30 by default), when neither
  reached it alone (`exit_volume_high:combined:<hour>`, a burst split across the hour boundary: H6's security review,
  2026-11-09). Absent pins = nothing pinned (as `pinnedIssuerKeys.email`, D190): set them before `set_exit_clients`.
  Unreadable pins page `pins_invalid:exit` and never pause, but every client in force still raises
  `exit_client_unpinned:in_force` (title `not paused: EXIT_PINS is unreadable`), so an already open alert doesn't
  auto-resolve while the pins can't be read.
- Options: pause on any mismatch (a pending unpinned client would stop every login for a mistake the council can undo for
  free); no pause at all (an unpinned client in force reaches every scope).
- Rejected: diffing the counter (it changes on every exit by design; it would page each one).
- Known limits of the alarm (H6's security review, 2026-11-09; not changed in code): (a) it catches bursts, not a slow
  harvest paced under it: with the default level, 14 sessions an hour reach neither 20 in an hour nor 30 across two, over 300
  a day with no page. The `exit_session_opened` events are the record for anything slower. (b) Anyone with a Google account
  can move the counter by opening sessions on their own identity (one count per session, no per-identity limit, since a
  refusing cap could be burned to lock users out of the rescue, D487): that can page every hour or keep the windows high
  enough to mask a real burst, so neither a loud nor a quiet counter proves anything alone. The alert's playbook says to
  read the events before acting. **The level needs raising once real traffic is known** (20 is provisional).

### D494. The exit state: an hourly window of current and previous, a retired pending client, the audience-shape rule by name, and no v2 migration
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built: `contracts/hana-signer/src/exit.rs`, `registry.rs`
  `assert_client_shape`, `migrate.rs` · For D468, D474, D487 · Fills in the design's section 1
- Decision: (1) `exit_window` stores `{window_start_ms, current, previous}` (the hour before, read once per watchdog run, so
  a burst straddling an hour boundary shows) and `get_config` shows it rolled to now; an older window reads as zero.
  (2) `set_exit_clients` retires a client dropped while still pending as well as one in force: a pending entry reserved the
  client publicly, and a mistyped client can be replaced by a new one (design section 1 says "removed"; the marker
  `RETIRED_EXIT` matches `RETIRED_SHARED`). (3) The audience-shape rule is `SELF_ISSUABLE.contains(provider)` (the constant,
  not the on-chain `self_issued` mark), so it holds even before `mark_self_issued`. (4) `migrate` keeps only v3 → v4 (and
  v4 → v4): every env is confirmed v3 (`docs/operations.md`; sandbox-dev since 2026-11-03), so the v2 path and layout
  copy are dropped as the design proposed.
  (5, added by H6's security review, 2026-11-09) The API reads the exit list for the email route too: `homeAudienceRoute` admits
  the audience `hana-home` only while `("email", "hana-home")` is in force on the list (from the cached `get_config`, so a
  removal lingers up to 60 s on an isolate, as for Google), so an emergency removal (D483) stops email Home as well. An older
  contract, an empty list and a pending entry all read as absent and refuse: `get_config` can't tell "never listed" from
  "removed", and the playbook's emergency call is `{"clients":[]}`, so an empty list must not pass.
- Options: a single window counter (a straddling burst splits; the two-window read still needs a combined level to see a split
  burst, D493); retiring only in-force clients (a pending client would be claimable the moment it is dropped).

## Hana Home H2: the app list (branch `feat/hana-home-h2`), 2026-11-09

### D500. `GET /v1/home/apps` is bounded per request; rows beyond the budget answer `coverage: 'unknown'`
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built: `apps/api/src/home/apps.ts`, `apps/api/src/views.ts`; `docs/api.md` · Source: the plan's H2, D417, D462, D466
- Decision: one route reads two sources, the list (`scopes.first_session_at`, D462) and the overlay (the wallet directory, by the verified `(provider, sub)`, D466), with no chain transaction. An answer has at most 30 of the user's own scopes (first page only) and 15 listed scopes a page, in `scope_id` order with a cursor. Coverage reads `get_scope` through a 60 s per-isolate cache (a missing scope 10 s) and may make at most 16 reads a request, own rows first, five at a time, stopping at the first failure; a row with no read answers `coverage: 'unknown'` and the page asks for it by `?scopeId=`. A search scans `apps`, so it has its own window of 10 a minute per Home key, on top of `homeGate`'s 30 a minute per IP and 60 per Home key.
- Why: the free plan's 10 ms CPU and 50 subrequests (D417) forbid a chain read per listed scope, and a failing RPC multiplies a read by its fallbacks: 16 reads stopped at the first failure stays under 50 even with every endpoint down. `first_session_at` costs a D1 read, not a chain read, and the listing keeps working if a chain read fails.
- Options: a chain read per scope (over budget); coverage only on an app's own page (no badge in the list, F2); a cron-maintained coverage table (no new cron, D417).
- Corrected 2026-11-09 (H2's security review): a badge can be stale for up to about 70 s, not 60: the 60 s copy is filled from `getScope`'s own 10 s view. Stated in `docs/api.md` and `docs/security.md`.
- Amended 2026-11-09 (same review): the overlay reads `status = 'active'` only, no longer `statusAt`'s promotion of a `pending` row past `effective_at`. A cancel's directory sync is best effort, so a `pending` row alone could show a cancelled link's owner the victim's wallet. A genuine matured member is not locked out: the app stays listed (`mine: false`), its key is reachable (H3's chain read), and its next login writes `active` (`syncAfterLogin`, and H3's `POST /v1/home/login` must do the same). Residual: an `unlink` whose sync fails stays `mine` until the next sync of that account.
- Limits: a badge can be up to about 70 s stale; a user with more than 30 scopes sees only the 30 most recently seen as "your apps" (the others stay reachable by the list).
- Address impact: none. Nothing here reads or changes how a path or key is derived.

### D501. Coverage values and order; `exit` added, `sharedLoginEndsAtMs` and `liveDevices` left out
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built: `apps/api/src/home/coverage.ts` · Amends the spec's `/v1/home/apps` shape (D98, D480, D490)
- Decision: for a Google identity, in order: `shared` (shared login on and a shared Google client in force), `hana_client` (a client the chain lists in the scope and `hana_held_clients` records, D503), `exit` (an exit Google client in force), `partner_client` (a partner's own client, no exit client in force; best effort), `none`. For an email identity: `email` (the scope's email client), `exit` (the Home audience on the exit list), `none`. A scope the chain doesn't have is `none`. `googleClientId` is the client Home should sign in with. Among several partner clients, the app's `google_web_client_id` is preferred. The spec's `sharedLoginEndsAtMs` is dropped: D480 made turn-offs immediate, so nothing is ever pending. `liveDevices` waits for H9's `/devices`, which reads shares by `path_hash` (no index on that column until H4).
- Why (D490 and the `hana_client` reading): a Hana-held client is the scope's normal route, so the exit counter (D487) stays a signal of real exits; a partner-held client isn't Hana's, so where the exit client exists Home uses it rather than a client whose redirect list Hana can't see.
- To confirm: D490 read literally ("shared login off" → exit) would send an Enterprise scope's users through the exit client even with a Hana-held client. This build keeps them on the Hana-held client and the exit client for the rest.
- Address impact: none. `aud` never enters the path.

### D502. The quieter listing: `scopes.home_quiet`, reachable by whole name, link or the user's own overlay
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built: migration 0016, `apps/api/src/home/apps.ts`, `admin home:listing` · Implements D98 item 8
- Decision: `scopes.home_quiet` (0/1, staff-set, `admin home:listing`). A quiet scope is left out of the list pages, and found by a search for an app's whole name (ASCII case-insensitive), by its `scopeId` or `appId` (the partner's link), and always in its own users' "your apps" (D466), since a user's own wallets are never hidden from them. An ordinary scope is found by any part of an app's name. Search covers app names only.
- To confirm: D98 item 8 said a quiet app is "shown after the user searches for the app or opens the partner's link", and read literally that hides it from its own users too. This build shows it to them. Also: whether "searches for the app" should mean the whole name (built, so a search can't enumerate quiet apps) or any part of it.
- Rejected: a quiet flag per app (the listing is by scope, D462); removing a quiet scope from the list entirely (D98: never removal).
- Amended 2026-11-09 (H2's security review): a quiet scope is no longer found by `?scopeId=` except by its own users. Scope ids are sequential (`s` + base36), so any Google account could walk them and read quiet partners' names, origins and logos. The partner's link is now `?appId=` only: app ids are `app_` + base58 of 12 CSPRNG bytes (`newId('app')` in console-core, `newAppId` in the CLI, 96 bits), not enumerable; only someone who knows the link or the whole app name finds one.

### D503. `hana_held_clients` and `admin home:client:add`: recorded only for a client the chain already lists
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built: migration 0016, `scripts/lib/admin-home.ts`, `apps/api/src/home/coverage.ts` · Implements the spec's `hana_held_clients (provider, aud, scope_id, added_at)`
- Decision: `admin home:client:add --scope --client [--yes]` records a Google client Hana holds, only after `get_scope` lists that client in that scope (a typo or a client in another scope is refused; a row for another scope is refused, not moved). Testnet only. Coverage counts a row only while the chain still lists the client in the scope, so a stale row changes nothing. `admin home:listing` and `home:client:add` write only D1, with no `app_changes` row: they aren't app settings a partner sees, and neither changes access to anything.
- Limit: no `home:client:remove` in this batch; a row for a client Hana no longer holds (a partner taking over the project) is removed by a D1 statement until a removal command is needed.

## Hana Home H4: consents on the server (branch `feat/hana-home-h4`), 2026-11-09

### D510. A 'none'-mode consent's replay check is its own row, kept until the consent expires
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h4`
  (`apps/api/src/vault/consent-store.ts` `pruneConsents`) · Amends the Home spec's "revoked more than 1 h ago" for rows
  with no share
- Context: the H1 message layout (`utf8("consent") ‖ consentId ‖ policyId ‖ expiresAtMs ‖ parentOrigin`, with
  `shareId` 0×16 and `counter` 0 in 'none' mode) has no nonce and no counter. A share counter makes a 'session'-mode
  message single use for good. In 'none' mode only `consent_id` (the PRIMARY KEY) stops a repeat, and the spec's prune
  would have removed it an hour after a revoke while the signed message could still pass `expiresAtMs > now`, so a
  captured register could have re-created a consent the user had stopped.
- Decision: the hourly prune deletes a consent past `expires_at`, or a `share_id IS NOT NULL` consent revoked over an
  hour ago. A revoked 'none'-mode row stays until its `expires_at` (at most the session's end).
- Options: (a) this; (b) a limiter marker per consent (one more Durable Object call on every register, and a marker held
  for up to 24 h); (c) a nonce in the layout (changes H1's frozen vectors, for no gain over (a)).
- Why (a): no new write, no new call, and the row still lives no longer than a session plus an hour, which is the
  privacy promise. Narrow-only either way: a replay could only have made a row read `active`, never let the vault sign
  without its sealed consent.
- Amended 2026-11-09 (H4's security review): the per-share window (10/min, the session key in 'none' mode) is spent only after the signature verifies, in both request functions, so an unsigned request can't burn a user's window. The per-IP limit stays first, before the body, so signature checks are capped.

### D511. `GET /v1/app` leaves `consent` out when it can't read it; `'unknown'` means the row isn't there
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h4` (`handlers.ts`)
- Decision: `consent` appears only on the vault's own read (`Origin: VAULT_ORIGIN`, `x-hana-consent`). `'unknown'` means
  this app has no such consent (or a malformed id, answered without a D1 read). A failed D1 read leaves the field out
  (and logs `consent_status_unavailable`), never `'unknown'`.
- Why: the spec has `'unknown'` clear the local consent, so a D1 blip must not read as one. H5: a missing `consent` is
  "no fresh answer": no auto-sign (popup) and the local consent stays.

### D512. The device label is the vault's word, shape-checked and never a reason to refuse
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h4` (`vault/endpoints.ts`
  `DEVICE_LABEL_RE`) · Carries out D98 item 10
- Decision: `deviceLabel` is optional on `POST /v1/vault/shares`, unsigned (the create-share signature doesn't cover
  it), at most 40 characters of letters, digits and ` .()/_-`, starting with a letter or digit. Anything else is stored as
  null and the share is still made. Any other extra key is still `400 bad_request`.
- Why: no login should fail over a cosmetic label, and a coarse allow-list of shapes keeps a label from being a
  fingerprint or markup. Older vaults send none. Rejected: a fixed list of browsers and systems (each new one would
  need an API deploy).

### D513. A consent's server-side details: the share is the expiry bound, and a dead share's revoke says so
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h4` (`vault/consents.ts`)
- Decision: in 'session' mode `expiresAtMs` must be after now and at most the share's capped end (`min(abs_expires_at,
  created_at + session_ttl_ms)`), not the chain's session expiry (no chain read). So H5 clamps a consent's end to the share's
  absolute end. A device's revoke of a consent whose share is dead answers `410 share_revoked` or `share_expired`, and
  `revoked_by = 'share'` is left for H9's Home sign-out: the status read already treats such a consent as `'revoked'`
  from the share row. `/v1/vault/consents*` count in the share's 10/min window, in 'none' mode under the session key.
- Amended 2026-11-09 (H4's security review): a 'none'-mode register makes at most one `get_session` read (`checkChainSession`'s `singleRead`, no retry loop): a fresh keypair used to cost about 7 reads over 2 s against a budget of one. A session the chain doesn't show yet answers `503 session_not_visible` with `retry-after: 1` rather than `410 session_ended`, so a just-created session behind a lagging node recovers on the vault's retry (H5) and nothing ends the session. A session key can hold at most 20 rows (`CONSENT_MAX_PER_SESSION_KEY`, `429 too_many_consents`, read through the `path_hash` index, no new index): one register writes several rows, so without a bound a single session key could spend most of D1's free daily writes at 10/min. A user registers once per Allow, so the cap is safe; the count isn't atomic with the insert, bounded by the 10/min window.
## Hana Home H3: the derive (branch `feat/hana-home-h3`), 2026-11-09

Decided during the build and its security review; confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 (D540–D543 decided then). Not merged, not deployed.

### D544. A Home derive is refused when there is nothing to rescue
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`home/login.ts`, `session-standing.ts` `opened`) · From H3's re-review
- Decision: `POST /v1/home/login` answers `404 home_no_wallet` ("no wallet for this sign-in in that app") when `get_identity` shows `status own` and `opened` false and links are open (`links_open`), before any limit is spent and before anything is relayed. A confirmed member isn't refused, and nothing is refused while links aren't open (the view isn't read then). It uses the view the standing already reads: no extra chain read.
- Why: every derive marks the identity `opened` on chain, permanently (`note_opened`, `links.rs`, from `derive_with`), and an opened identity can't be linked. A user whose wallet is under email who opened that app in Home with an unlinked Google account would lose that Google account's link for good.
- Downside (accepted): on sandbox-dev, wallets from before contract v3 have no `opened` record, so those are refused until they log in normally once. Mainnet starts on v3.

### D545. Accepted risk: throwaway accounts with one partner login can use up a day's Home ceiling
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10
- Decision: about 25 throwaway accounts that each do one partner login count as known (D527, D540) and can use up the day's ceiling at their own 20 a day. That is a one-day outage of Home, with the 80% alert (D541) and no funds at risk. Accepted; revisit if it is ever seen.
- Alternatives: a 7-day minimum record age before counting as known was considered and declined, because it would penalise genuine new users.

### D540. Identities with no directory row share 20% of the daily ceiling
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-09** · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`home_usage.unrecorded`, `countHomeDerive`, `homeUnrecordedCeiling`) · From H3's security review (M2)
- Decision: a derive by an identity with no `active` directory row and no confirmed link counts in a separate counter, in the same atomic statement as the day's total, and stops at 20% of the ceiling (rounded down, at least 1, always leaving one for people with records; a ceiling of 1 gives them none). A ceiling of 0 stops everything.
- Why: about 25 accounts could otherwise burn the whole day's ceiling and lock out the rescue route; now throwaway accounts only spend their own share.
- Trade-off (accepted): a real owner with no row, which includes the purged-scope shutdown case Home exists for, falls in the smaller share and can be crowded out there until the next UTC day.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (D544): the chain's `opened` also counts as known, which is safe only because D544 refuses an unopened identity (otherwise one derive would promote a stranger), so a purged-scope owner gets the larger share. What's left in the 20%: with links open, every derive that reaches the count is a member, has a row or is `opened`, so the share is empty. It applies only where links aren't open (a contract before v3, or before `accept_unrecorded_wallets`), where `opened` isn't read.

### D541. 80% of the daily ceiling writes a `home_budget_high` security event (amends D523)
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-09** · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (migration 0018, `noteBudgetHigh`, playbook `home-budget-high`)
- Decision: when a day's derives reach 80% of the ceiling the API writes one `security_events` row of kind `home_budget_high` (a fixed id per day; counts only, no `sub`, path or scope), shown in the admin's Security & monitoring and emailed by its existing feed. No new cron (D417). It replaces D523's log line.
- Note 2026-11-10: filling the 20% share (D540) raises no alert of its own. Accepted: with links open that share is empty, and where it applies the derives also count in the total, so real demand still reaches the 80% alert; a refused stranger costs nothing.

### D542. The Home relayer key's allowance is 5 NEAR
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-09** · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`deploy-contract`, the watchdog's default thresholds 1 / 0.2 NEAR) · Amends D98 item 11's 2 NEAR
- Decision: `--home-relayer-allowance` defaults to 5 NEAR, so one key covers about the 500-a-day ceiling at 100 Tgas prepaid each; the relayer account should hold about 5 NEAR extra.

### D543. `uid-erase` lists the scopes where the user has only a Home derive
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: found while checking H3, built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`scripts/lib/uid-erase.ts` `homeEventScopes`)
- Decision: a stranger's derive leaves a `key_exported` row (internal id, no app) and no directory row (D527). `uid-erase` already deletes it when run for that scope, because the internal id is recomputed from the identity, but it listed other scopes only from the directories, so an erasure could miss the scope. It now also reports the scopes holding such a row of these identities, by recomputing the internal id per scope, in batches of 500 ids.
- Residual: a member's Home derive in another scope is recorded under that scope's root, which this run can't compute; it is found from the directory row the derive writes. If that scope's directory sync also failed, it can be missed.

### D520. A Home derive's `key_exported` row names no app: `user_events.app_id` is nullable for `key_exported` only
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (migration 0018, `apps/api/src/mainnet-demo.ts` `recordKeyExport`, `home/login.ts`) · Closes the build plan's open item 4
- Decision: Home's derive records `key_exported` (D430) with `chain` null and `app_id` NULL. Migration 0018 rebuilds `user_events` so `app_id` may be NULL, for `key_exported` only (a new CHECK; `mainnet_signature` still needs an app). The admin's Users screen shows "Hana Home" for it.
- Why: a Home derive is per scope and has no app. Naming one of the scope's apps would be a false record: 0016's backfill read `app_id` as proof that an app had a login (`user_events WHERE app_id = apps.id`, and D462 lets strangers see only apps with a recorded login), so such a row would have marked an unreleased app as launched had it existed at that migration; the admin's Users screen shows it as the app the user exported from; retention (D433) and `uid-erase` key on `scope_id`/`user_id`, so they are unaffected either way. NULL matches no `app_id = apps.id`, nothing reads the column as an app it isn't, and D462's own write path is `markFirstLogin`, which Home never calls.
- Alternatives: (a) the scope's app (no migration, but a false attribution for a suspended app's scope, and a scope with several apps has no right answer; recommended against); (b) a sentinel such as `'home'` (no rebuild, but a column that lies about being an app id, and a dead link in the admin); (c) a `kind` of its own (a CHECK rebuild as well, and two kinds for one thing).
- Trade-off: a table rebuild in 0018 (all rows copied, ids kept; a migration test covers it).

### D521. Home's limits are counted last, right before the relay, not after the standing read
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`home/login.ts`) · Deviates from `docs/hana-home-spec.md`'s order ("Home limits; counter hold; `checkClientScope`…")
- Decision: the per-wallet, per-user and daily limits come after every check that a request can fail (scope, session key, signature, BLS shape), as `appQuota` does (D100). Per-IP stays first (in the gate). A refused request spends nothing; on a refusal by a later window the earlier windows are taken back; a relay that certainly never ran gives back what it took.
- Why: the spec's order (limits before the chain checks) would let a request that can't succeed use up the user's 3-per-hour, for no gain: nothing is relayed either way, and the chain reads that order would save are already bounded by the per-IP hour. The user's windows are counted per identity (`sha256(provider#sub)`), the per-wallet one per path, so a linked account's two identities share the wallet window; only a user's own tokens can spend them.
- Confirmed: the deviation from the spec's listed order.

### D522. A standing the chain didn't confirm fails closed on a Home derive
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3`
- Decision: `sessionStanding` fails open for partner logins (it only saves gas). `POST /v1/home/login` answers `502 near_unavailable` when the standing isn't confirmed: the per-wallet limit needs the real path (a member's root), and a guessed path would let a member's derives count in a different bucket.
- Alternatives: fail open as a partner login does (the path limit becomes guessable from a failed RPC). Not recommended.

### D523. The daily ceiling lives in D1 `home_usage` (one row a day), counted atomically; 80% is a log line for now
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (migration 0018, `home/login.ts` `countHomeDerive`, `homeDerivesPerDay`) · D98 item 11, D85
- Decision: one statement (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE derives < ?`) both counts and refuses at the ceiling, so concurrent isolates can't overshoot; the ceiling is `HOME_DERIVES_PER_DAY` (default 500). D1 failing refuses the derive (fail closed). Reaching 80% writes a `warn` log line `home_derives_high` once a day (the first request to cross it).
- Why not the rate limiter object: this count is the budget H11's statement reads; it should be queryable and survive DO eviction. A `security_events` kind would make the alert an email, but needs another rebuild (`security_events` CHECK) and admin work: left out of H3, raised here.
- Confirmed with a real alert: the log line is replaced by a `security_events` kind, D541.

### D524. A Home session is one use, `key_index` 0, at most 20 minutes, and carries no link
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`toHomeLogin`)
- Decision: `POST /v1/home/login` refuses anything but `keyIndex = 0`, `maxUses = 1`, `expiresAtMs ≤ now + 20 min` and refuses `linkJwt`, `linkImmediate` and `exportChain`. The spec already says the export session is one use and 15 minutes; this makes the API enforce it, with the Home identity's 5-minute margin.
- Why: `key_index` is part of the path, so an open index would give a fresh per-wallet window for each one (D59's bound dodged). One use and a short expiry stop a Home session being replayed through `/v1/derive` past Home's limits. Together these keep Home inside the exit client's on-chain caps (D486: 30 minutes, 3 uses, no link) without a check per route.
- Alternatives: enforce only the on-chain caps, and only for exit tokens (weaker, and two rules). Not recommended.
- Corrected 2026-11-09 (H3's security review, L5): "one use" holds for derives only. A used Home session stays live on chain until it expires (at most 20 minutes), and its key's holder can still call the routes that only ask for a live session of an active app in that scope: `POST /v1/identity/token`, `/v1/wallets/record`, the email-sharing calls, `/v1/mainnet-demo/events`, `/v1/vault/consents` ('none' mode) and `POST /v1/vault/shares`. Each also needs the app's publishable key, an allowed parent origin and the session key's signature, and a suspended or deleted app answers none of them. Nothing can derive again (`session_exhausted`). It isn't closed: a used-up session is exactly what a 'session'-mode partner login leaves (a share requires `used === max_uses`), the chain has no Home marker, and a marker of our own would add a read to every partner call. The key lives only in the Home page's memory, and its holder already has the user's key.

### D525. The server admits an exit client for any registered scope; D490's "only where the normal route is gone" stays Home's choice
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`checkHomeClientScope`)
- Decision: `POST /v1/home/login` accepts an exit client in force for any scope the chain has, exactly as the contract does; `homeCoverage` (D501) on the page chooses when to use it. Partner logins keep `checkClientScope`, closed to exit clients.
- Why: D490 says "this is Home's choice" and the coverage decision needs 60 s-cached views; a server-side refusal would reject legitimate exits in the window where a scope has just turned shared login off. Compromise of the page is already the single trust root (D468's analysis).
- Confirmed by the user: keep admitting exit tokens wherever the contract accepts them. The review's proposal to refuse one where the scope's normal route is up was considered and declined: the rescue route should have as few ways to fail as possible, and the only cost is a possible false alert on the exit counter.

### D527. A Home derive writes a directory row only for a user the directory or the chain already knows
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`home/login.ts` `holdsActiveRow`) · From H3's security review (M1) · Narrows how D500 is met
- Decision: after a derive, `syncAfterLogin` runs only when the standing is a confirmed linked member, or the directory already holds this identity as `active` in the scope. Otherwise no `end_users` or identity row is written and no Support ID is returned. `key_exported` is still recorded.
- Why: a derive permanently records the identity as `opened` on chain. Since D544 only someone who already had `opened` (or a member) reaches a derive where links are open, but `opened` alone doesn't prove a wallet anyone should list: a stranger can still get it with a direct contract call or one partner login. Before D544 anyone with an exit or shared token could derive in any registered, sequentially numbered scope. A written row made them `mine`, which shows every app of the scope, reopening the unreleased-app exposure D462 closed, and added a row to the partner's user list. D500 only needs the member case. A row marked `unlinked` or `cancelled` doesn't count, so a derive can't bring it back.
- Trade-off: a real wallet owner with no row (a purged scope, a lost record) doesn't regain `mine` from a derive; they find the app by search, as the spec's purge case already says.

### D528. `ckd_failed` gives back the wallet's window and keeps the per-user and daily counts
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` · From H3's security review (L1)
- Decision: a derive that fails in the MPC after the session was committed gives back its per-wallet hour. The per-user windows and the day's `home_usage` stay counted, since gas was spent.
- Why: a Home session is one use, so D486's retry in the same session doesn't exist; three MPC failures would otherwise lock the wallet for an hour with no key delivered. A client can force this outcome with a mismatched app key (the pairing precheck is off on the free plan), so only the wallet window comes back: the user's 10 an hour and 20 a day still bound it, and no key is released.

### D529. `homeDerivesPerDay` in the manifest; 0 is a kill switch
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`packages/env`, `gen-wrangler.ts`, `homeDerivesPerDay`) · From H3's security review (L6)
- Decision: the manifest's optional `homeDerivesPerDay` (integer, 0 or more) becomes the var `HOME_DERIVES_PER_DAY`. `0` means no Home derive at all (429 `home_busy`, nothing relayed or counted), not the default. Absent or malformed: 500.
- Why: operators need one place to set it, and a stop that doesn't need a code change.

### D526. The Home pool is kept out of the usage ledger and the nonce check until H11; the watchdog goes in after the key
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h3` (`relayer-config.ts`, `apps/api/src/changes/admin.ts` unchanged, `apps/watchdog/src/relayer.ts`)
- Decision: `AdminRpc.relayerKeys` keeps listing the session and owner pools only, and `/v1/home/login` writes no usage event, so the daily nonce check and settlement don't see Home keys or relays until H11 adds the statement line. The watchdog does watch the pool (allowance thresholds, `relayer_pool_empty:home`); deploying it before the Home key exists would page, so it goes last.
- H11 must add the Home keys here when it adds the ledger rows. Readiness row 7.4a holds it before mainnet (H3's security review, L4).
- Done on `feat/hana-home-h11`, 2026-11-10 (D585, D590, D591; not merged).

## A late `relayed` signal ends the close grace (branch `test/flake-fixes`), 2026-11-09

### D495. A popup's `relayed` signal the vault takes after the watch read `closed` turns the close grace off
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: decided while fixing a flaky test, confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built: `packages/web/src/vault/login.ts` `notePopup` · Amends D347, D400
- Decision: when the vault takes `relayed` from the popup it answered, it clears a grace already running for that close and forgets the close (`popupGone`), so the login goes on waiting for the answer (5-minute limit only).
- Why: the popup posts `relayed` after its answer's write and closes after the ack, or after 150 ms without one (D400). A busy vault can run its `closed` poll before it gets the message posted earlier. The watch then starts the 1 s grace, and `relayed` used to change nothing: if the relay read took longer than the grace (a slow network, a stalled frame), a finished login ended in `login_cancelled`. Found reading the popup lifecycle for the flaky `popup-close` test; that test's own flake was the harness running the grace as a 1 ms real timer, not this.
- Options: leave it (the 1 s grace covers almost every case, but the vault then knows the close wasn't the user's and cancels anyway); read `relayed` before `closed` in the poll (the browser orders the two tasks, not the page).
- Safety: `relayed` is taken only from the popup the vault answered, on `authOrigin` (as before D495), and the popup could already make the close moot by sending it first. A window that says `relayed` and writes nothing waits for the 5-minute limit, as it does when the signal arrives first.

## Hana Home H5: the vault's side of device consents (branch `feat/hana-home-h5`), 2026-11-09

### D530. A consent that can't be recorded is refused as an error, with `data.granted: false`
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts` `askConsent`, `errors.ts` `consentNotRecorded`) · Carries out D98 item 13
- Decision: on Allow the vault makes a random 128-bit `consentId`, registers the consent, and stores it only on the 201. A failure stores nothing. `hana_requestAutoApprove` then answers a port error `api_unavailable` with `data: {granted: false, reason: 'consent_not_recorded'}`; a covered request goes on to the approval popup, and the launcher says it couldn't be turned on.
- Options: (a) this; (b) answer the result `{granted: false}` with no error, as the spec's sentence reads.
- Why (a): the port carries a result or an error, not both, and the SDK's result validator takes only known keys, so `{granted: false}` plus a code can't be sent; a plain `{granted: false}` means the user said no, and a partner's fallback would treat an outage as a refusal (`D98` wants it refused, not retried silently). The error's `data` keeps the spec's `granted: false` for a caller that reads it. **Differs from the spec's wording; recommendation: (a).**

### D531. A consent stored before H5 is dropped at its first read; the user is asked again
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`withConsent`, `consentActive`; `legacy-consent.test.ts`)
- Decision: a consent with no `consentId` (a vault before this one, granted in a tab or sealed in the record) never auto-signs. It is dropped from the record at its first read; `hana_autoApproveStatus` reads null and the user sees the consent screen again at the next covered request, which registers normally.
- Options: (a) this; (b) keep it and register it silently on the user's behalf at the next signature; (c) keep honouring it until it expires.
- Why (a): the fail-safe. Registering without the user's Allow would give the server a record the user never agreed to create, on a consent that may predate the current policy; honouring it leaves it unrevocable from another device, the very thing H5 closes. Rows are only for consents actually granted against the server. Cost: every user with an open or persisted auto-approve is asked once more (only partner tabs that had it).
- Limit, stated: an old vault build still open in a tab keeps its old behaviour until the tab reloads, and may write a consent with no id; a current vault drops it at its first read.

### D532. Outage, race and read rules for the status read
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09, with H5's security review's amendment · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`confirmConsent`, `tryAutoSign`, `applyServedConsent`, `policyFresh`) · Amends D465's mechanics, within its 10 s
- Decision: auto-signing needs an `'active'` answer asked (`at` = when sent) within `POLICY_FRESH_MS` for the consent read under the lock; the register's 201 counts. `'revoked'` and `'unknown'` clear the consent, and that request goes to the popup with no consent screen. A failed read, a read with no `consent` field, or a value of another shape is no answer: no auto-sign, the consent stays, the request goes to the popup with no consent screen, and auto-signing resumes when a read answers `'active'`. Answers apply only to the consent named when the read was sent, and, for the same consent id, an answer asked earlier never overrides one asked later. A consent's answer is aged by the larger of the corrected clock and a monotonic timer (H5's review): the corrected clock stands still after a device clock goes back, and a monotonic timer may stop while the device sleeps. The auto-approve policy's own 10 s check is aged the same way (`policyFresh`); raw signing's and the mainnet demo's checks stay on the corrected clock.
- Race chosen: the id doesn't exist before the 201, so a read can't land before the register for that consent; the local write happens after the register, so `'unknown'` can't mean "not registered yet". A read asked before a newer grant can't clear the newer consent (compared by id).
- Why: D511 said a missing field must not clear; a failed read must behave the same, or an outage would clear a valid consent; and an outage must not keep a revoked one signing, which the freshness rule prevents: it only stops auto-signing for the outage (the popup still works), bounded to the outage, by re-reading on the next request. Limit: an `'active'` read can precede a revocation by up to 10 s (D465's design), and `GET /v1/app` failing shows extra popups for as long as it lasts.

### D533. After a failed register, a covered request doesn't re-offer the consent screen for 60 s
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`CONSENT_ASK_AGAIN_MS`)
- Decision: a covered request within 60 s of a failed register goes straight to the approval popup. `hana_requestAutoApprove`, an explicit request, still shows the screen. Otherwise, while the API is down, every covered request would show two popups.
- Options: (a) this; (b) no cooldown. **Recommendation: (a).** Not user-visible beyond avoiding the double popup.

### D534. Which revoke paths reach the API
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09, with H5's security review's condition and limit · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`revokeAutoApprove`, `revokeDormantConsent`, `logout`) · Amends the spec's "logout and a new login send the revoke" for `'session'` mode
- Decision: `hana_revokeAutoApprove` and "Stop auto-approving" clear locally first, then revoke best effort, only for a consent this tab holds (D510: no server call otherwise). A dormant tab deletes its sealed consent from the record without unlocking and tells the API when it knows the id (its last known consent), and `'none'`-mode logout and new login send the revoke. `'session'`-mode logout and new login send no separate consent call: revoking the share already ends the consent server-side (D513's status read), and an extra signed call under the counter adds only an API round trip and a window for the logout's revoke to fail on a stale counter. The local copy is cleared first in every path.
- Why: the share's revoke is the session mode's stronger signal: one call kills the consent and the share. Rejected: sending both (twice the calls, no change in what can sign).
- Condition on H9: after a `'session'`-mode logout or new login the row's `revoked_at` stays NULL, so Home must derive "active" from the share's liveness (as `consentStatus` does), never from `revoked_at` alone.
- Limit: a dormant tab that never read its consent can delete it locally but can't tell the API, because the id is sealed and it has no key. The row reads `active` until the share or the consent ends. It can't sign: the local consent is gone.

### D535. A consent's end is clamped to the share's absolute end; `session_not_visible` is retried three times
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`askConsent`, `registerConsent`, `CONSENT_NOT_VISIBLE_RETRIES`, `CONSENT_RETRY_*`) · Carries out D513
- Decision: the end an Allow agrees to is the minimum of `now + maxConsentMs`, the session's expiry and the share's absolute end as the API last said it (create or unlock), so the register doesn't fail `bad_expiry` on the typical session. `503 session_not_visible` is retried 3 times (`none` mode only, in practice), waiting `Retry-After` bounded to 1–5 s, then fails closed. A stale counter retries once with `expected`.
- Why: D513 asked for the clamp; a bounded retry covers a lagging node without holding the user's request open for long.
- Amended 2026-11-09 (H5's security review; confirmed by the user 2026-11-09): the API's cap also has `created_at + session_ttl_ms`, which the vault can't compute. A reload or wake is already right (unlock returns the capped end), so the gap is an app lowering its TTL while a tab is open. `400 bad_expiry` now carries `maxExpiresAtMs` when the end was past the cap; the vault keeps it, this Allow still fails closed (the user agreed to a stated end, so it isn't silently shortened), and the next Allow shows and asks for the capped end. Needs the API deployed before the vault for the fix to apply; a vault on an older API just fails closed as before.

### D536. Parallel requests in a session with no record are serialised, so the daily limits bind
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`withConsent`, `Session.consentQueue`) · Found by H5's security review; predates H5
- Decision: `withConsent`'s path with no record or lock (`'none'` mode, or no storage) runs one at a time per session. Before, parallel covered requests each read the counters before the previous write, so all signed and the count rose by one, past `perDayCount` and `maxValueWeiPerDay`.
- Options: (a) an in-memory queue per session; (b) the per-app Web Lock here too. **Recommendation: (a):** it adds no dependency to a mode that has never needed the lock.

### D537. A 410 on register ends the session, as a touch's does
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`askConsent`) · Found by H5's security review
- Decision: a `410` from `POST /v1/vault/consents` deletes the record, tells other tabs and ends the session (port error `4900`), instead of failing closed into a session that can't register. The exception is a session with no share that gets `reason: 'unknown_share'` (a `'session'` app whose share was never made, or an app switched from `'none'` to `'session'` while the tab is open): the API answers 410 for that, while the session is fine in memory, so it fails closed as any other register.

### D538. `hana_requestAutoApprove` doesn't report a consent it can't confirm as granted
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h5` (`requestAutoApprove`) · Found by H5's security review
- Decision: with a local consent whose status can't be confirmed, it answers `api_unavailable` with `data: {granted: false, reason: 'consent_unconfirmed'}`, shows no consent screen, and keeps the consent. A dormant session still answers from its last known consent without a read: it must not wake for a status answer (D112), and signing re-checks.

### D539. An auto-signature doesn't refresh the share's idle timer
- Date 2026-11-09 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-09 · No code change: `tryAutoSign` never calls `maybeTouch` · Found by H5's security review · Keeps D55
- Decision: only a signature a person approved in a popup slides the share's server `idle_until` (D55). So a session that only auto-signs reaches its idle limit: the consent's status reads `'revoked'`, auto-signing stops, and the session ends.
- Options: (a) this; (b) touch after an auto-signature (one line, at most once per 10 minutes).
- Why (a): with (b), a page driving covered requests with no one present could keep a share alive up to its absolute end, bounded only by the policy's limits and the consent's end. The in-memory idle limit is a separate timer, and any signing request already restarts it. Cost of (a): an app that only auto-signs has its users sign in again at the idle limit.

## Hana Home H11: billing and the Home keys' visibility (branch `feat/hana-home-h11`), 2026-11-10

D585–D599 were **confirmed by the user on 2026-11-10**, with D605 (the review's open finding, left uncapped for now).
D595–D599 are the fixes from the batch's independent review (no Critical or High). One thing stays open: who pays for a
suspended app's Home logins (D586's `suspended` line, built as "Hana pays"), to be discussed with the user's colleagues.

### D585. A Home derive that reaches the relay is one `home_login` usage event: a scope, no app, no uid
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`apps/api/src/usage/event.ts`, `home/login.ts`, `packages/console-core/src/usage-event.ts`, Neon `0008_home_logins.sql`) · Ends D526's "no usage event"
- Decision: `POST /v1/home/login` opens its event right before the relay, after every check and limit passed, and closes it with the response, as every captured endpoint does (`relayed`, `near_tx`, the Home key and its nonce from the relay result). The event's endpoint is `home_login`, its `app_id` is null (a Home derive names a scope, as an owner action does), and it carries no uid. A request refused before the relay writes no event.
- Why not D221's "every answer past the gate": Home has no app gate, so "the gate" is only the Home identity. Events for every refusal would put a stranger's failed attempts (`home_no_wallet`, `rate_limited`) into a partner's failure counts, though they cost no gas and the partner can do nothing about them. The request log still has each one. The nonce check and settlement need exactly the relayed ones, and those are all recorded, the failed ones included (`contract_rejected`, `ckd_failed`, a timeout).
- Why no uid: a uid counts an app's users (`usage.app_users` is keyed by app), and a Home derive belongs to no app. So a Home login adds nothing to MAU or new users. It also keeps the path out of the usage code entirely.
- Options: (a) this; (b) an event per answer past the Home gate; (c) reuse `login` with a null app (it would mix into login counts and latency percentiles).

### D586. Who pays for a Home derive is one table, `HOME_PAYER`, applied when the event is written
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 (the `suspended` line is D461's note and stays open: still to be discussed with the user's colleagues, build plan open item 5) · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`apps/api/src/home/billing.ts`, `usage/record.ts`)
- Decision: the event's `org_id` is the org that pays. `HOME_PAYER` in `apps/api/src/home/billing.ts` is the whole rule: `active` → the scope's org (`scopes.org_id`), `suspended` → Hana, `gone` → Hana. Changing who pays for a suspended app is changing that one line and its test; the ledger, reports, statements and settlement only ever see the org.
- What the three words mean for a scope (a Home derive names no app): `active` when at least one app of the scope that isn't deleted is running; `suspended` when the scope has apps that aren't deleted and every one of them is suspended, whoever suspended it (Hana, the org or the partner); `gone` when every app is deleted or the hot DB has no row for the scope.
- When it is applied: once, after the response, by one hot-DB read, and only when usage capture is on. If that read fails, Hana pays (a partner is never billed on a guess; `usage_org_unavailable`).
- Limits: the rule isn't retroactive. Events already written keep their org, so changing the suspended rule later changes billing from that deploy on; moving older events would be a statement by hand. An app suspended between the derive and the write a few milliseconds later is billed by its state at the write.
- Options for a scope with one running and one suspended app: (a) the partner pays while any app runs (built); (b) Hana pays as soon as any app is suspended. (a) because the users of the running app are the likelier ones to derive.

### D587. What a partner sees: a "Hana Home logins" line per scope, with a count, gas and cost, and nothing about who
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (Neon `0008_home_logins.sql` `usage.org_report`, `packages/console-core/src/reports.ts`, `types.ts`, `apps/admin/src/statement.ts`, the console's Usage page, the admin's reports table)
- Decision: a scope's Home logins are a report row of their own (`kind: 'home'`, no app), apart from the scope's owner actions, carrying only the gas of those logins. `usage.org_report` gains `kind` (`app`, `scope`, `home`) and `home_logins` (the ok ones). The statement shows the row as **Hana Home logins, scope `<id>`** with its count, Tgas, NEAR and USD; the summary has a "Hana Home logins" total and a one-line note. The CSV gains two columns, appended after `as_of` so no existing column moves: `row_kind`, then `home_logins` (changed after the review; first built in the middle). The partner console's Usage page and the admin's reports table show the same row and a "Home logins" column.
- What the partner doesn't see in the report or the statement: any user identifier, a per-user count, or which sign-in method was used. Failure codes of relayed attempts are listed, as for logins. Corrected after the review (D595): the partner's ledger CSV did name each Home event's transaction, whose public arguments carry the user's ID token; it no longer does. The chain itself still shows a scope's Home derives to anyone, so "nothing about who" is true of what Hana hands a partner, not of what a partner can find.
- A statement without a Home line renders exactly as before (no column, no summary line, no note), and totals stored before this change still parse.
- An app filter leaves Home rows out, as it leaves owner actions out: neither has an app.

### D588. The price of a Home login is its gas, like a login's; no fee of its own
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built: nothing new (the existing billing rule applies to the new rows)
- Decision: a Home login is billed exactly as every other relayed event: its settled gas at the day's NEAR/USD rate (about 38–40 Tgas, roughly $0.02 at the spec's figures). Relayed-then-rejected gas isn't billed (D91); gas of a relay that errored after the broadcast is (D324), as for a login. There is no per-login fee and no free allowance.
- Options: (a) gas only (built); (b) gas plus a fixed fee per Home login; (c) Hana absorbs Home gas up to a monthly allowance per org. (a) because D461 called the line cheap and the ledger bills only gas today; (b) and (c) would be the first non-gas price in the ledger and need the service contract's wording first (readiness 9.9).

### D589. Hana's own org in the ledger is the manifest's `hanaOrgId`, else `org_legacy`
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`packages/env/src/schema.ts` `hanaOrgId`, `apps/api/scripts/gen-wrangler.ts` → var `HANA_ORG_ID`, `apps/api/src/home/billing.ts` `hanaOrgId`)
- Decision: D461's "Hana's internal org" is an org of kind `internal` that staff create in the admin console, named in the env's manifest as `hanaOrgId`. `gen` writes it as the API var `HANA_ORG_ID`. Without it (sandbox-dev today) the events Hana pays for go to `org_legacy`, which no partner can read and no statement bills.
- Why not a fixed id: org ids are generated, and an internal org lets staff read Hana's own Home usage in the admin like any org's.
- For the user: create the internal org and add its id to `envs/<env>.json` before turning capture on, so Hana's Home usage isn't mixed with legacy scopes' rows.

### D590. Settlement holds a Home derive to the Home pool, and every other event to the other pools
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`apps/admin/src/settlement.ts` `poolMatches`, `ledger.ts` `settlementQueue`) · Extends D321's check 2
- Decision: besides D321's three checks (a unique transaction; a pool key; the transaction at FINAL signed by the relayer account with that key at that nonce, to the signer contract), a `home_login` event must carry a key of the Home pool, and no other event may carry one. A mismatch is `signer_mismatch` with `wrongPool` in the alert, refused without a chain read, never billed.
- Why: the API relays Home derives from the Home pool only and nothing else from it. An event that crosses the pools wasn't written by the relay it claims, which is the case D321 exists for (a leaked writer credential attaching a real transaction to an org).
- Consequence: an API from before this batch lists no Home keys, so a Home event settled against it is refused, not billed. Deploy the API before the admin Worker.

### D591. Row 7.4a: the Home keys are in `AdminRpc.relayerKeys`, the nonce check and the status page; one more call a day
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`apps/api/src/changes/admin.ts` `relayerKeys`, `apps/admin/src/ledger-cron.ts`, `status.ts` tile `home-pool`) · Closes D526
- Decision: `relayerKeys` lists the Home pool's public keys, tagged `home`. The daily nonce check reads each one (D323's rules unchanged), so a Home key whose nonce moved with no ledger row is `nonce_unexplained` and emailed. System status has a "Home pool keys" tile: the keys on chain and their lowest allowance against the watchdog's thresholds, a warning when the API holds a Home key the relayer account lacks, and "not measured" in an env with no Home key at all.
- Budget (D380): one `view_access_key` more at the 00:30 UTC run, so 3 instead of 2 with one key per pool, and never more than 3 in a run however many keys a pool has (D598). No new cron trigger (D417). In the measured worst case (every job due at once) the run still makes exactly 40 calls; the link-rate check, which needs two, waits for the next run 15 minutes later.
- With usage capture off (sandbox-dev): changed after the review, see D596. The check records baselines and raises no alert while the API says capture is off.

### D592. Neon migration 0008: the `app_id` rule found by what it says, the report dropped and created again
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built: `apps/api/migrations-usage/0008_home_logins.sql`, `apps/api/test-usage/ledger.test.ts`, `reports.test.ts`
- Decision: 0008 widens `events_endpoint_check` and `record_event` for `home_login`; replaces the `app_id` rule (null exactly for owner actions and Home derives) under the name `events_app_id_check`, finding 0001's unnamed constraint by its definition and failing unless there is exactly one; and drops and recreates `usage.org_report` with the two new columns and the same grants. No row changes.
- Deploy order: 0008, then the API, then the admin Worker and the console. Before 0008 the ledger refuses a Home event (`usage_write_rejected`, the derive itself unaffected) and the API reads the old report without `kind` correctly. After 0008 an older API or admin Worker reads the new report correctly too, since no Home row exists until the new API writes one.

### D593. A statement's totals stay version 1: `homeLogins` and the `home` row are optional additions
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built: `packages/console-core/src/reports.ts` (`statementTotalRow`, `statementView`)
- Decision: `usage.statements.totals` keeps `v: 1`. `homeLogins` is optional on a row and on the sum, and `kind` gains `home`, so statements already stored parse and render unchanged. A new statement stores `homeLogins` only when it has a Home line, so one without is byte for byte the old shape and an API from before this batch still reads it; one with a Home line needs the new API (deploy the API before the admin Worker).
- Why not `v: 2`: nothing about an existing field changed, and a second version would need both renderers kept for 7 years of locked files.

### D594. The Home pool's first-day ledger gap is accepted: derives made before capture is on are never billed
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built: nothing
- Decision: Home derives relayed before H11 is deployed with capture on have no ledger row and are never billed to anyone. No backfill from chain.
- Why: they are testnet derives on sandbox-dev, there are few, and a backfilled event would have to guess who paid.

### D595. A partner's ledger rows don't point at a Home derive's transaction; staff's do (review M2)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (Neon `0008_home_logins.sql` `usage.org_ledger`, `usage.org_ledger_full`; `apps/admin/src/ledger.ts`) · Corrects D587
- Found by the independent review: D587 said a partner sees nothing about who, but `ConsoleRpc.ledger` returned each Home event's request id, exact time and `near_tx`, and that transaction's public arguments carry the user's ID token.
- Decision: `usage.org_ledger`, the function the API's writer role reads for partners, returns a `home_login` row with no `near_tx`, with the UTC day (00:00:00.000) in place of the time, and with a row id `home_` + 32 hex characters of a SHA-256 of the request id and time, so the id is stable and unique for paging and is no key into Hana's logs. Scope, outcome, gas status and gas stay, so the partner's CSV still sums to the statement. Every other row is unchanged. The writer role can no longer read the full rows at all: they are `usage.org_ledger_full`, granted to the admin role only, which staff use to reconcile a statement against the chain.
- What is true after this, and what isn't: Hana's reports, statements and ledger give a partner no pointer from a Home login to a person. But the chain does, to anyone: a Home derive is a public transaction from the Home relayer key whose arguments hold the scope id and the ID token, as every login's does. A partner who wants to know which of its users left through Home can read that from chain without Hana, and a row's exact gas would be enough to match it. H11 doesn't change that; it is the standing property of ID tokens in public call arguments.
- Options for the request id and time: (a) drop both for partners, keep the day (built); (b) keep them (a support reference, but a second key to the same transaction by timestamp); (c) drop Home rows from the partner's ledger altogether (the CSV would no longer reconcile with the statement).

### D596. With usage capture off the nonce check records baselines and raises no alert; deploy-check requires capture on a production network (review M3)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`apps/api/src/changes/admin.ts` `relayerPools`, `apps/admin/src/nonce-check.ts`, `status.ts` tile `nonce-check`, `ops.nonce_checks.reason` in Neon 0008, `scripts/lib/deploy-check.ts`) · Amends D323 and D591
- Found by the review: with capture off, any day a relayer key's nonce moved ended in a `nonce_unexplained` email, for Home keys after this batch and already for session and owner keys.
- Decision: `AdminRpc.relayerKeys` also answers `capture` (the API has `USAGE_DB`). While it is false the check still reads each key but records its nonce as explained with reason `capture_off` and alerts nobody; System status shows "Relayer nonce check: not measured". The first check after capture is back on is a fresh baseline (`capture_on`), because the nonces that moved meanwhile have no rows and never will; from the next check D323's rules apply. An API that doesn't send the flag is judged as before.
- `deploy-check`: the API's `GET /v1/health` now says `usageCapture`. On a production network (anything but testnet) capture off, or an API that doesn't say, fails the check; on testnet it is a note.
- Limit: while capture is off the check sees nothing, by design, so a relayer key used outside the API goes unnoticed by it. The watchdog's allowance and balance alerts still apply. That is why a production env can't pass deploy-check without capture.

### D597. `hanaOrgId` must be an internal org, checked at deploy and again when a statement is built (review M4)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`scripts/lib/deploy-check.ts`, `apps/admin/src/statement.ts` `StatementRefused`, `statements.ts`) · Extends D589
- Found by the review: the id was checked by shape only, so a partner's org id there would have put every Home derive Hana pays for on that partner.
- Decision: `deploy-check <env> --d1` reads the org's `kind` from the console's D1 and fails unless the org exists and is `internal`; on a production network a manifest without `hanaOrgId` fails too. Independently, a statement refuses a Home line whose scope isn't one of the statement's org's own apps' scopes, unless the org is internal: nothing is written and staff are told which scope.
- Why both: the deploy check catches the mistake before an event is written; the statement check is the one that can't be skipped.

### D598. The nonce check reads at most three keys a run; pools are read one by one; a key belongs to one pool (review L1, L2, L6)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built on `feat/hana-home-h11` (`apps/admin/src/nonce-check.ts`, `ledger-cron.ts`, `apps/api/src/relayer-config.ts` `poolsSharingAKey`, `relayer-pool.ts`, `changes/admin.ts`) · Amends D323, D380's table and D591
- Decision:
  - The check is no longer one burst at 00:30 UTC. Its day starts at 00:30; each 15-minute run reads at most three keys not yet tried that day (`ops.state` `nonce_check.day`), and later runs finish the round. A key is tried once a day whatever the outcome. With one key per pool nothing changes (three reads at 00:30); with more keys the other jobs keep their calls. An unexplained key's email goes out in the run that read it.
  - `relayerKeys` reads each pool on its own: a secret that doesn't parse loses only that pool's keys (`unreadablePools`, logged by the admin every run as `relayer_pool_unreadable`), so a malformed `HOME_RELAYER_KEYS` can't stop the check and settlement for logins.
  - One key in two pools is refused: neither pool relays (`503 relayer_unconfigured`) or lists a key until the secrets are fixed. Settlement tells a Home derive from everything else by its key's pool (D590), so a shared key would make that ambiguous.
- Trade-off: with more than three keys the last ones are read up to an hour or so after 00:30 instead of at once.

### D599. Migration 0008 waits at most 5 s for its lock and has no down path; refusals are final, so the API is deployed first (review L3, L4)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built: `apps/api/migrations-usage/0008_home_logins.sql` (`SET LOCAL lock_timeout`), `docs/operations.md` "Hana Home billing: deploy" · Extends D592
- Decision: 0008 sets `lock_timeout` to 5 s, so it fails cleanly instead of queueing behind a long statement with every writer behind it; run it again. `ADD CONSTRAINT … NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE` works on a partitioned table (tried on Postgres 18 in PGlite; not tried on Neon), but each migration file is one transaction and the first lock is held to the commit, so it would gain nothing and isn't used.
- No down path: the schema after 0008 accepts everything the older one did. To go back, deploy the older API and leave the schema.
- Order and why: 0008, the API, then the admin Worker. A settlement refusal is final (the event has its row and is never read again), so an admin Worker that settles a Home event against an API listing no Home key would refuse it for good. For the same reason a key is removed from a pool's secret only once nothing it signed is left to settle; there is no list of recently rotated keys (D321's trade-off stands).
- Not built: keeping a rotated-out key accepted by settlement for 24 h. It would need a list of retired public keys beside the pool secrets; proposed as a follow-up if rotations become routine.

### D605. A partner's Home line stays uncapped for now; to settle before mainnet (review M1)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: confirmed by the user 2026-11-10 · Built: nothing (no change) · Source: H11's independent review, M1; `docs/security.md` "Open: a partner's Home line can be run up by strangers"; `docs/mainnet-readiness.md` 1.20
- Decision: while an app is active its org pays for every Home login in its scope (D461, D586), with no cap and no alert on the partner's side, for now. The question is settled before mainnet.
- The exposure: anyone can make one ordinary login in a partner's app and then derive through Home up to 20 times a day per Google account, until the env's daily ceiling (500 by default). At about $0.02 each that is about $10 a day, about $300 a month, for the whole env.
- Options put to the user: (a) Hana pays for every Home login, no partner line (one line in `HOME_PAYER`; reverses D461); (b) the partner is billed up to N per scope per day and Hana pays the rest, never refusing a derive (about a day's work: a per-scope daily counter in D1); (c) a monthly allowance or cap per org (2–3 days: it changes the one billing rule and the statement's billed figures).
- Chosen: none yet. (b) was the recommended alternative and was declined for now.
- Why it can wait: testnet only, usage capture is off on sandbox-dev, and no statement has been issued to a partner.

  isolate, not globally (one refresh per isolate per 5 min, per 60 s while failing), so traffic reaching many isolates
  spends more of the key's quota; exhaustion only falls back to the keyless source and then the fixed table. Accepted
  for the sandbox demo; a global slot from `RATE_LIMITER` is the fix if a shared key's quota ever suffers.
### D275. The admin console's Users screen reads the user directory through a read-only, self-auditing RPC on the issuer
- Date 2026-11-04 · Status: **confirmed by the user** (2026-11-05, with the amendments below) · Source: D269 ("the
  admin console's Users page later (batch C)") · Written: `docs/batch-c-spec.md` "Users and Support ID" (data path,
  Users screen, what partners never see, tests, Q26); build plan C8b · Built: branch `feat/batch-c-8b` (C8b; not
  merged, not deployed; the build's own readings D388–D392)
- **Amendments by the user (2026-11-05)**, otherwise as recommended below:
  - **The support-ticket reference is required to open a single user's detail** (`get`, and any call that returns
    one identity's full record), and **optional for list and search views** (`search`, list pages). Every call is
    still audited in `email_admin_audit`, with the ticket when given and never an address in the audit row.
  - **The per-staff budget as proposed, provisional**: at most 500 identities an hour and 2 000 a day per staff email;
    past that the call answers `rate_limited` and the security alias is emailed (the admin Worker's existing alert and
    email path, under its call-budget rules, D380). The numbers are named constants (console-core
    `DIRECTORY_ROWS_PER_HOUR`, `DIRECTORY_ROWS_PER_DAY`).
  - **The admin screen also shows the user's wallets, User ID (`u1_…`), Support ID and internal `hu_…`** from the wallet
    directory through the API's AdminRpc (admins see email and wallets, D310), joined by provider and sub.
  - Confirmed as recommended: `DirectoryRpc` with no route, bound only by the admin Worker as `ISSUER`; read-only
    methods (`search`, `get`, `auditSince`; `byUid` not built: D346 dropped the uid it would read); the source test;
    the issuer's own JWT check as the actor; the audit row in the same D1 batch as the read; issuer migration 0003; the
    search filters and the detail's fields; "chain unavailable", never a guess; the unverified-claim warning and
    never a default target; no CSV export; nothing for partners, with tests that enforce it.
- Recommendation:
  - **Data path.** The issuer exports `DirectoryRpc`, a `WorkerEntrypoint` with no route that only the admin Worker
