    binds (`ISSUER`). It has read methods only (`search`, `get`, `auditSince`; `byUid` with D276). A source test
    holds the module to `SELECT`s on `user_emails` and `user_email_apps` and forbids imports of the signer, key,
    challenge and mail modules.
  - **The issuer checks the staff member.** Each call carries the staff request's Access JWT, which the issuer
    verifies itself (admin application `aud`, team domain, staff list) and uses as the actor. Each call also writes
    its `email_admin_audit` row in the same D1 batch as the read, with a required ticket and no address in it.
    Issuer migration 0003 adds the actions and a `detail` column.
  - **Budget.** Each staff email gets at most 500 identities an hour and 2 000 a day (provisional). Past that, the
    call answers `rate_limited` and the security alias is emailed.
  - **Features**:
    - Search by address (exact, or a substring of at least 3 characters), provider, app, sub and "unverified only".
    - The detail shows the address, provider, sub, verified and hosted flags, first and last seen, and the apps. It
      also shows the on-chain path per scope, and for a linked member the account root, read live with
      `get_identity` and `get_account`. A failed read shows "chain unavailable", never a guessed path.
    - Unverified Google claims carry the CLI's warning and are never a match's default target.
  - **No CSV export.** Bulk reads stay with `admin user:list --json`.
  - **Partners get nothing.** No binding in the console, no `ConsoleRpc` field, no SDK or `/v1` field, nothing in
    the partner feed.
- Why: the issuer is the directory's only writer (D269), so a narrow read entrypoint keeps it so. Checking the JWT at
  the issuer means a compromised admin Worker reads only what staff requests let it read, and those reads are
  audited where the data lives. This is D251's direction (a narrow RPC instead of a broad D1 binding).
- Main trade-off: more code in the Worker that holds the signing keys and `K_sub` (mitigated: no route, the source
  test, additive methods), and the issuer must deploy before the screen.
- Alternatives:
  - (a) **An issuer D1 binding in the admin Worker.** Simplest, but D1 bindings are read-write and cover the whole
    database. A bug or compromise there could write `email_hints` (which automatic linking reads, D266),
    `email_suppressions` or the audit, and read with no audit row. Not recommended.
  - (b) **Move the directory into a D1 of its own, bound to both Workers.** This keeps the hints out of the admin
    Worker's reach. The admin Worker could still rewrite rows and mislead support, reads go unaudited, and there are
    two writers. Cheap now (0002 isn't applied on sandbox-dev), but not recommended.
  - (c) **The admin Worker calls the issuer's Access-protected HTTP routes.** This puts an address-serving route on
    the public internet. Not recommended.
  - (d) **A CSV export**, capped (e.g. 1 000 rows), audited and emailed to the alias. Useful for partner-wide
    analysis, but one click takes out a slice of the directory. Not recommended for batch C; the CLI covers one-off
    needs.
- Also: the batch C spec's Support ID line ("no email or Google account") and "Hana stores contact details only for
  partner members, security contacts and billing contacts" were rewritten. They now read as statements about
  partners and about whom Hana contacts, consistent with D269.

### D276. Support ID: the uid's first 40 bits; staff resolve it through the directory's stored uid; errors by request ID
- Date 2026-11-04 · Status: **confirmed by the user** (2026-11-05: "yes go ahead with C15"), **as amended by D346 and
  below** (the 2026-11-05 amendment; built in C15, D394–D397) · Source: build plan C15's open question (D144:
  confirmed, built from data Hana already keeps), made consistent with D269 · Written: `docs/batch-c-spec.md`
  "Support ID lookup", Q27; build plan C15
- Recommendation:
  - **The code** is `HANA-XXXX-XXXX`: the Crockford base32 of the uid's first 5 bytes. The secret is
    `USER_ID_KEY` through the uid (`hana-id/uid/v1`), so there is no new secret, domain string or table. It is per
    scope and per account (a linked member shows its root's code).
  - **Where it is shown.** The API returns `supportId` with the session (`/v1/login`, `/v1/sessions`). The vault
    exposes it in `hana_status` (so partners' diagnostics carry it) and in the popup's account view.
  - **Code → user.** The issuer fills a `uid` column in `user_email_apps` after each directory write, from a new
    API entrypoint `IssuerRpc.uid` (bound only by the issuer; the entrypoint D251 plans), off the answer's path.
    Staff reach that column only through `DirectoryRpc.byUid`, with a staff JWT. Without a directory row, the
    fallback is the ledger only (`app_users` by uid prefix). Every match is listed (40 bits: rare collisions,
    resolved by the app the partner names).
  - **Address → user** is the Users search; the detail shows the code.
  - **What a lookup shows**:
    - Logins and sessions: the ledger's ok `login`, `session` and `derive` events by uid, with live vault shares
      from `AdminRpc.userShares`.
    - Errors: by the request IDs the partner sends, since the ledger keeps uids only on ok events, by design.
    - The app's `app_changes`.
    - Not consents: they live only in the vault's browser storage.
  - **Partner side**: the code only, no address or sub, and no partner lookup in batch C.
  - **Retention**: nothing new but the `uid` column (kept with its directory row) and audit rows (5 years). A code
    resolves while the ledger holds the uid (24 months after the month, D90). Directory rows have no expiry under
    D269. An erasure request deletes them with a new CLI `user:erase`, so `DirectoryRpc` stays read-only.
  - **Migrations**: the Neon one adds `app_users (uid)` and `events (uid, at)` indexes, at the next free number
    (0004 and 0005 are taken).
- Why: D144 (no dedicated support table) holds, and the uid is already the ledger's key. Storing it beside the
  address makes code → user a single indexed read instead of recomputing every directory row's uid at the API. The
  key stays in the API only. A compromised issuer gains uids it can't join to anything (it can't read the ledger).
  A compromised admin Worker can't compute uids without a staff JWT.
- Main trade-off: the partner page sees a stable per-scope pseudonym (40 bits of the uid; no more than the identity
  token's `sub` gives). The issuer also gains a call into the API, best effort and off the hot path, so a lost call
  leaves the code unresolvable to a user until the next login.
- Alternatives:
  - (a) **A separate `SUPPORT_ID_KEY`** (HMAC of the uid). It adds a secret and still needs a stored code or a
    scan. Not recommended.
  - (b) **The code from the identity token's `sub`** (`IDENTITY_SUB_KEY`). Partners could map it themselves, but
    it is a second pseudonym that the ledger doesn't use, and it needs its own index. Not recommended.
  - (c) **No stored uid.** Recompute the uid at lookup for each directory row of the app through an
    `AdminRpc.uid`. That costs O(users of the app) per lookup and lets the admin Worker compute uids on its own.
    Not recommended.
  - (d) **uids on post-verification error events**, so errors list per user. It means a migration of the ledger's
    CHECK and more per-user data. Not recommended; request IDs cover support.
  - (e) **An org-scoped lookup in the partner console** (the org's ledger rows for a code, no address). Deferred.
- Amends in text only: D96's "it reveals no email or Google account" now holds for partners; staff reach the
  directory (D269). `docs/email-login-spec.md` ("Support ID lookups show … never a `sub` or address") and
  `docs/hana-home-spec.md` "Support ID" still say otherwise. They are to be aligned once this is confirmed.
- **Amended 2026-11-04 by D346 (confirmed by the user): the code's derivation.** The code is now the Crockford base32
  of the first 5 bytes of the identity token's `sub` HMAC (`IDENTITY_SUB_KEY`, the 16 bytes `u1_…` encodes), no
  longer of the uid: alternative (b) above, taken so the partner's one id (the `sub`) and its Support ID are the same
  user's, and a partner can compute the code from the `sub` it stores. The format `HANA-XXXX-XXXX` is unchanged.
  Code → user is `end_users.support_code` in the hot DB (D312, built), then `end_users.user_id` (the uid, `hu_…`) for
  the ledger; the issuer's `uid` column and `IssuerRpc.uid` above are no longer needed for it, and the ledger-only
  fallback (a uid prefix) is gone: a user with no directory row since the deploy has no resolvable code.
  "Where it is shown" still stands as planned and is not built: neither `/v1/login`, `/v1/sessions`, `hana_status`
  nor the popup carries a Support ID yet.
- **Amended 2026-11-05 (confirmed by the user, "yes go ahead with C15"; built on `feat/batch-c-15`, D394–D397):** the
  design C15 builds, replacing the recommendation above where they differ:
  1. **Code → user** is the wallet directory: `end_users.support_code` (indexed), or `token_sub` / `user_id` when staff
     hold the User ID or the internal id. No `uid` column in the issuer (`user_email_apps.uid`), no `IssuerRpc.uid`,
     no `DirectoryRpc.byUid`. Where an email is shown, the join is by provider and sub (`end_user_identities` → the
     issuer's `user_emails`), as `user:find --user` and the C8b screen do. Every match is listed (40-bit collisions;
     the partner's app tells them apart). The code is taken in any case, with or without `HANA-` and dashes
     (console-core `parseSupportId`, the CLI's parser).
  2. **What a lookup shows**: the user's ids, identities and wallets (the directory); the scope's apps; the ledger's
     ok `login`, `session` and `derive` events by uid (Neon; the indexes are 0007's, D362, so no migration); the vault
     shares that haven't expired (`AdminRpc.userShares`, built, and the lookup's own read); errors by the request IDs
     the partner gives (the ledger keeps uids only on ok events, by design); the apps' `app_changes`. Not consents.
  3. **Where users see it**: `supportId` beside the session in the `/v1/login` and `/v1/sessions` answers (additive),
     the same derivation as the stored code (D395); the vault's `hana_status` (`hana.supportId`, for SDK 0.2.0 or
     later, D393) and the approval popup's account line (the popup's only account view).
  4. **Partners**: the code only (their Users page shows it, D310); no partner lookup in batch C; no address or sub.
  5. **Erasure**: `uid-erase` (D361) removes everything the lookup reads for the account (its directory rows, so the
     code resolves to nothing, and its uids in the ledger; `scripts/test/uid-erase.test.ts`); no `user:erase`. Vault
     shares and app changes aren't per-user records the erasure keeps: shares expire within a day and the lookup
     reaches them only through the directory row.

## Dev env email limits, 2026-11-04

### D340. Dev envs (`local*`, `sandbox*`) get higher per-mailbox and per-IP email code limits; production keeps D198's
- Date 2026-11-04 · Status: confirmed by the user (2026-11-04: "yes raise limits for dev environments please, as we
  will be testing a lot and testnet don't really cost us money anyway") · Built on `fix/dev-email-limits` · Amends D198
  (its numbers are now production's)
- Decision: the email issuer picks its limit set from `ENV_NAME` with `isDevEnv` (`@hana-id/env`: `local*`,
  `sandbox*`), once per request (`limitsFor` in `apps/email-issuer/src/limits.ts`). Every other name gets production's,
  which are exactly D198's. Dev values (production in brackets):
  - per (mailbox, requester) code mails: 20 per 15 min (3), 100 a day (10);
  - per mailbox code mails: 30 per 15 min (10), 200 a day (30);
  - challenges per mailbox a UTC day: 250 (35); live challenges at once: 20 (5), chosen so one tester's abandoned
    starts never meet the live cap before the per-requester 15-min code limit;
  - wrong codes per (mailbox, requester): 30 an hour (10) before the 1 h lock;
  - failed checks per mailbox a UTC day: ceiling 100 (25), backstop 80 (18), owner slot 17 (4), ticket slot 3 (3). The
    ceiling stays the sum of its three slots, so the owner slot still works past the backstop, and the requester lock
    (30) still trips before the backstop (80);
  - per IP: `start` 30 per 10 min (10) and 300 a day (50); `resend` 30 per 10 min (10); `verify` 90 per 10 min (30).
- Unchanged in every env: the aggregate prefix limits, the recipient-domain cap (it protects Hana's sending
  reputation), the ticket and grant allowances (the grant slot too), the google-match and google-record limits, the
  webhook and staff limits, the budget and its pools, `confirm`'s per-IP bound (production's 10 per 10 min: a staff
  unsuppress's mailed link, not the login flow), and each challenge's own 5 attempts and 2 resends.
- How it applies to existing counters: the mailbox object gets the set with every call (none: production's). Its
  counters are keyed by window name and start, never by max, and both sets use the same names and windows, so a
  sandbox-dev mailbox over production's numbers but under the dev ones passes at once, with no reset. A requester's
  wrong-code lock is keyed by the max that set it (production's keeps its `lock:<ip>` key), so a lock set at
  production's 10 doesn't hold under the dev set.
- Why: sandbox-dev is testnet, used by Hana's own testers many times a day; D198's numbers were sized against an
  attacker on a mainnet mailbox and blocked repeat testing. The name rule (not a manifest flag) means no setting can turn
  them on in a production env, as for the other dev-only privileges.
- Main trade-off: on a dev env, a 6-digit code can be guessed with 100 failed checks a day instead of 25 (≈ 3.7% a year
  instead of ≈ 0.9%). Testnet accounts hold no real funds.
- Alternatives: (a) a manifest field for the limits: it could be set in a production env by mistake. Not recommended.
  (b) Resetting the counters on sandbox-dev (rotating K_rl): a one-off that also drops device tickets and recurs at the
  next busy day. Not recommended.
- Amended 2026-11-04 (same day, `fix/dev-ticket-limits`): a ticketed start (a device that signed in before) never
  falls back to the code limits, so its own allowance (production 3 a day per address, 9 per mailbox) blocked the
  user's testing first; dev envs raise it to 100 and 300. Production unchanged.

## A cancel on Google's sign-in screen (branch `fix/google-cancel-back-to-chooser`), 2026-11-04

### D341. Cancelling Google's sign-in screen goes back to Hana's method chooser; closing the popup there is `login_cancelled`
- Date 2026-11-04 · Status: confirmed by the user (2026-11-04: "yes" to "the popup goes back to Hana's method chooser
  … the partner app gets `login_cancelled`, … `google_error` stays for real Google failures") · Built on
  `fix/google-cancel-back-to-chooser` (`packages/web/src/auth/callback-page.ts` `goBack`, `toSlot`;
  `auth/email-page.ts` `showChooser`, `restartGoogle`, `chooseEmail`, `onPageHide`; `auth/login-storage.ts`
  `slot`, `back`, `offer`, `cancelled`; `auth/login-page.ts` (the record-only login's email context);
  `vault/login.ts` `readRelay`; `auth/google.ts` `GOOGLE_CANCEL`, `GOOGLE_CANCELLED_RELAY_ERROR`) · Source: the user's
  report (Cancel on Google's screen showed "Sign-in stopped … Code: google_error" at `/login/email#…`) · Amends D264,
  D270 and D273 (a cancel ended the Google login with `google_error`, `access_denied`)
- Decision:
  - Under token_first, when Google answers `error=access_denied` to the login's first request (from the chooser, from
    `/login` directly, or from case B's Google step on `/login/email`) or to D273's interactive retry, the callback
    relays nothing. The vault's wait goes on under the login's own 5-minute limit (`LOGIN_PENDING_MS`). The popup goes
    back to the screen the Google step came from, on `/login/email#<relayId>`: Hana's method chooser with the line
    "Google sign-in was cancelled." and the app's methods (Continue with Google; Continue with email when the app
    offers it: a Google-only app's chooser has Google only), or case B's own choices (Link and continue when the
    issuer offered it, Sign in with Google, Cancel) with the same line.
  - Google again is a fresh attempt: a new random OAuth `state` whose login entry names the login's relay slot
    (`slot`), with the login's nonce and the same binding checks; the ID leg reuses that attempt's state. The cancelled
    attempt's state never finds an entry again. Between the two, the login's keys are parked under the slot
    (`cancelled`, never usable by a Google answer: refused as an expired sign-in) and the email page takes them into
    memory on load. Case B's Google step always uses such a fresh state under token_first. After a cancelled D273
    retry, Google again is that retry once more (the same account, `login_hint`, no chooser): slot 1 already holds
    that account's access token and a relay slot takes one write.
  - Email from the chooser is the email step in place (the login's entry back under its slot).
  - Closing the popup on that screen (`pagehide` when the page didn't navigate on itself) writes `{error:
    'google_cancelled'}`, encrypted when the screen was shown and sent with `keepalive`, to the login's slot; the vault
    ends the login with `login_cancelled` (only in a login with the follow-up key, the token_first ones). The keys are
    zeroed and the email context dropped, so a reload shows an expired sign-in. Case B's Cancel there relays
    `email_cancelled` as before (`login_cancelled`).
  - `google_error` stays for Google's real failures: any other error code, `invalid_response`, the tokeninfo stops,
    `google_account_mismatch`, a second failure of the D273 retry, the silent ID request's errors (no screen was
    shown). A cancel is still relayed as `access_denied` (`google_error`) where there is no screen to go back to: no
    email context stored, a login without the follow-up key (an env without an email issuer, batch B's request), and
    the record-only fallback's openid request when tokeninfo couldn't answer.
- Why: the user cancelling Google's screen is a choice, not a failure. Ending the login with a stop screen and a
  code made them start again from the app; Hana's own chooser lets them pick again in the same window. A partner's
  "cancelled" handling is `login_cancelled`, the code a close or `cancelLogin()` already gives.
- Main trade-off: the close relies on `pagehide` (every desktop browser fires it on close, and the e2e checks it in
  Chromium, Firefox and WebKit); where it doesn't fire (a crashed or killed browser, some mobile cases) the partner
  gets the login's `login_timeout` after 5 minutes, as before for any abandoned popup.
- Alternatives: (a) relay the cancel and let the vault end the login with `login_cancelled` at once: the user loses
  the chance to pick again in the window. Not recommended. (b) Reuse the login's slot as the OAuth `state` for every
  attempt: simpler, but a cancelled attempt's state would find an entry again. Not recommended. (c) A Cancel button
  on the chooser: not asked; the original chooser has none and closing the window is the way out. Not done.
- The login's limit still applies: the screen stops at the email step's deadline (`EMAIL_STEP_LIMIT_MS`, 15 s before
  the vault's), and Google or email picked after it starts nothing. Once the vault has ended the login (its limit, a
  newer login, `cancelLogin()`), its reads of the slot have stopped (`fix/abandoned-login-freeze`'s abort-aware
  `readSlot`), so a late `google_cancelled` lands in a slot nobody reads.
- Not changed then: closing the popup at other points (the email step, Google's own page, the follow-up screens) left
  the vault waiting until its limit (`login_timeout`, `data.stage: 'pending'`). Amended the same day by D347 (any close
  while the login waits on the popup is `login_cancelled`) and D348 (a `method: 'google'` login comes back to Google
  only).

### D347. Closing the login popup at any point ends the login within seconds with `login_cancelled`
- Date 2026-11-04 · Status: confirmed by the user (2026-11-04, "yes") · Built on `fix/google-cancel-back-to-chooser`
  (`packages/web/src/vault/login.ts` `PopupTask.watchPopup`, `popupWait`, `POPUP_WATCH`; `vault/vault.ts`;
  `auth/callback-page.ts` `signalVault`; `auth/login-page.ts`, `auth/email-page.ts` `tellVault`; core `hana:auth-progress`
  stages `relayed` and `back`) · Amends D341 ("closing the popup at other points still leaves the vault waiting") and
  the partner guide's "An unfinished login" (a closed popup was `login_timeout` after 5 minutes)
- The signal: the vault's own handle on the popup window (the hello's `event.source`, partner and vault mode alike),
  read every 250 ms. It stays valid across the popup's navigations because Hana's auth pages send no
  Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and Google's sign-in pages send it report-only (checked with `curl` on 2026-11-04 for the
  authorization endpoint, the identifier and account-chooser pages: `cross-origin-opener-policy-report-only:
  same-origin`; only Google's OAuth error page enforces `same-origin`). `pagehide` alone can't be the signal (it fires
  on every navigation, and no Hana code runs on Google's page); the SDK's handle isn't used after the popup connected,
  as before.
- Decision:
  - The popup tells the vault what the handle can't: every Hana page posts `hana:auth-progress` `google` before it
    navigates to Google; the callback posts `back` as it loads (it still has its opener, so that trip switched no
    browsing context group); a page that closes itself after relaying (the callback, the email step) posts `relayed`
    first. The callback doesn't know the vault frame's name, so it posts to the opener and each of its frames with
    `vaultOrigin` as the target origin; the vault takes the signal only from the popup it answered.
  - A close while the login waits on the popup (its first slot, a follow-up screen's answer, a link task's slots) ends
    it after a 1 s grace with `login_cancelled`, `data.reason: 'popup_closed'`: the login aborts (the freeze fix's
    abort-aware relay reads stop), its keys are dropped, and a later write to its slots is never read. The grace lets
    an answer the popup wrote just before it closed itself win even if `relayed` was lost.
  - A close while the vault works alone (google-match, the chain) lets the login finish; a later wait on the popup
    then ends at once.
  - A close within 8 s of a `google` signal, before `back`, is taken for an IdP's COOP switching the popup's browsing
    context group (the opener's handle then reads closed while the window is open: the spec makes the two
    indistinguishable). The watch stops for the rest of that login, which falls back to its 5-minute limit and to
    D341's own close report on the screen after a cancel.
- Why: Privy-like behaviour; a closed popup is the user's cancel, and a partner waiting 5 minutes for `login_timeout`
  can't tell the user anything meanwhile.
- Main trade-off: a user who closes the popup within 8 s of reaching Google's page gets the 5-minute
  `login_timeout`, not `login_cancelled`. The alternative is a false cancel of every login if Google starts enforcing
  COOP on its sign-in pages (it reports violations today). If Google switches to an enforcing policy on a later page
  (after the 8 s), a login would be cancelled while the user is still at Google: the watch's assumption to recheck
  before each release, with `coop-canary <env>` (D386; it replaced `curl -sI` on the authorization URL).
- Alternatives: (a) the SDK polling its own handle after connect: the same handle semantics, with one more hop. Not
  done. (b) The popup reporting its own close on every page (`pagehide` with a pre-encrypted relay write, as D341's
  screen does): it can't cover Google's page, and slot writes are single use. Kept only for D341's screen. (c) A
  heartbeat through the API: no Hana code runs on Google's page either. Not recommended.
- Amended 2026-11-05 by D398: a close within the 8 s still stops the watch, but the login then waits 90 s for the
  popup's answer and ends with `login_cancelled` (`popup_closed`) without one, rather than waiting for its 5-minute
  limit.
- Amended 2026-11-05 by D400: a page that posts `google` or `relayed` navigates or closes only once the vault acked
  it (`hana:auth-progress-ack`), or after 150 ms; Chromium delivered a signal posted in the navigation's own task with
  a null `event.source`, which the vault can't take.

### D348. After a cancel, a login the partner restricted to Google comes back to Google only
- Date 2026-11-04 · Status: confirmed by the user (2026-11-04, "yes") · Built on `fix/google-cancel-back-to-chooser`
  (`packages/web/src/auth/email-storage.ts` `EmailContext.method`, `auth/login-page.ts`, `auth/email-page.ts`
  `showChooser`) · Amends D341 (its chooser offered the app's methods whatever the partner asked)
- Decision: `/login` keeps the method the partner named (`hana.login({method})`) in the email context. When a login
  started with `method: 'google'` is cancelled on Google's screen, the screen it goes back to offers **Continue with
  Google** only, even in an app with email login; **Continue with email** appears only when the partner didn't
  restrict the method. Closing the popup there is `login_cancelled` as before.
- Why: a partner that names Google has its own sign-in choices (often a separate email button); offering email in
  Hana's popup would override that choice.
- Alternatives: (a) the app's full chooser (D341 as built): it ignores the partner's `method`. Not recommended.


### D550. Hana Home's page (H7) lists apps and addresses from the API and derives nothing
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/web/src/auth/home-page.ts`, `home-api.ts`, `entries/home.ts` · Source: the plan's H7; `docs/hana-home-spec.md` "Wallets and export" ("Viewing needs no chain transaction and no re-auth")
- Decision: `/home` signs the user in with Google and shows what `GET /v1/home/apps` answers: their apps first, each with whether Hana can still open the wallet, the addresses on record and the Support ID where the API gives one. It never calls `POST /v1/home/login`: the first derive belongs to export (H8). An app with no address on record says so and offers nothing more until H8.
- The Home sign-in itself uses the shared Google client through `/login?mode=home` and `/login/callback` (the spec's "Identity" step 3). With no shared Google client in force the page says sign-in isn't available: signing in to Home through the exit client needs `/home/callback` (D491), which arrives with the per-app sign-in (H8) or email (H10).
- Why: the spec says viewing needs no chain transaction; a derive marks an identity `opened` on chain for good (D544) and spends the daily ceiling, so it shouldn't happen just to look.
- Seams left: the app page's `home-app-extras` element (export in H8, devices in H9), `SIGN_IN_METHODS` (email in H10), and the page's sentences for the derive's refusals (`home_no_wallet`, `home_busy`, `home_account_mismatch`, `link_pending`), already written and tested.
- Address impact: none. No path, key rule or derivation is read or changed.
- Note, 2026-11-10 (H10, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10): the open point is settled by D618: with no shared client in force Home signs in through the exit client and `/home/callback`.

### D551. `/home`'s policy lists the API and Google's JWKS only; the NEAR RPC joins with the derive
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/pages/host.ts` (`authPageDirectives`, `AUTH_PAGE_PATHS`, `AUTH_LOGO_PATHS`), `packages/web/src/auth/pages.ts`
- Decision: `/home` is served with the base policy plus `frame-ancestors 'none'; connect-src {apiUrl} https://www.googleapis.com`, and the files origin in `img-src` (app logos). The spec's list also names `{rpc}` and `{rpcFallback}`; H7 reads no chain, so they are left out until H8 needs them for `get_scope` and `get_identity`.
- Why: a page gets only the origins it uses. Adding two origins later is one line in each of the two lists, which a test keeps equal.
- Address impact: none.

### D552. `/login?mode=home` takes its own message, `hana:home-params`, only from a same-origin opener at `/home`
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7` (the condition of H1's review); **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (the new message) · Built: `packages/core/src/protocol.ts` (`hana:home-params`), `packages/web/src/auth/login-page.ts` (`checkHome`)
- Decision: the Home sign-in child is `/login?mode=home`. It accepts only `hana:home-params` (`signer`, `clientId`, the Home public key, its end, the salt, the nonce, the relay slot and key), only with `event.origin === authOrigin`, `event.source === window.opener` and `opener.location.pathname === '/home'`. It recomputes `homeNonce` from the message's own key, end and salt for the pinned signer and stops on any difference, so it never sends Google a nonce it can't account for. It goes to Google with `scope=openid`, the account chooser and no `max_age`. The mode takes no `hana:auth-params`, and the partner, vault and export modes take no `hana:home-params`: no other opener can get a token with a Home nonce through Hana's pages.
- Options: reuse `hana:auth-params` with a flag (its session fields would be dummies, and a flag could be set by the vault); a separate page (another route and policy for the same steps).
- Address impact: none.

### D553. Hana Home's sign-in ends after 15 minutes: a warning 2 minutes before, the screen kept, nothing fetched, a new key at each sign-in
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (the 2 minutes and the same-account rule) · Built: `home-page.ts` (`HOME_EXPIRY_WARN_MS`, `checkSession`, `signedIn`) · Implements the spec's "Expiry" (D424's rules for Home) and the plan's "One `hk` per sign-in"
- Decision: the page tells the end from the identity's own `expiresAtMs` (timers, and a check whenever the page is shown or focused and before every request) and from any 401. Two minutes before, a notice says so and offers "Sign in again". At the end the key and token are dropped; everything on screen stays; a click that needs the API sends nothing and the notice asks for a new sign-in. The page never sends a request again by itself, after an error or after a new sign-in. A new sign-in always makes a new key. If it is for the same Google account (the `sub`, compared in memory), the screen stays exactly as it was and nothing is fetched until the user acts; for another account the screen is cleared and that account's list is loaded.
- Why: "lose nothing" and "never retry" together mean the user, not the page, decides what is asked again; comparing the account stops one person's list staying on screen under another's sign-in.
- Memory only: the key, token and `sub` are never written to storage, a URL or a log; a reload signs out.
- Address impact: none.

### D554. Hana Home's wording: availability badges, app states, refusals
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts` (`COVERAGE_TEXT`, `homeProblem`)
- Decision:
  - Availability, from the API's coverage: `shared`, `hana_client`, `exit` and `email` read "Available" ("Hana can open this wallet for you, even if the app stops running."); `partner_client` "May stop working" (it works only while the app keeps its own Google sign-in); `none` "Not available" (with "If the app still runs, use the app itself."); `unknown` "Not checked yet", checked once when the app's page is opened or on "Check now" (a user's own app by `?scopeId=`, another by `?appId=`, D502).
  - App states: `suspended` "Paused", `deleted` "Closed", a test app "Test app". Sections: "Your apps", "Find an app", "Other apps that use Hana".
  - Refusals read as fixed sentences picked by the API's code, never the API's own message, with the code and the request ID beneath: `home_no_wallet` "There is no wallet for this sign-in in that app." (D544); `home_busy` "Hana Home has reached its limit for today. Try again tomorrow."; `rate_limited` and any other 429 "Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again."; every 5xx and a network failure "Hana Home is not reachable right now. Nothing on screen was lost. Try again in a moment."; every 401 ends the sign-in (D553).
- Why: plain words, no internal terms (scope, coverage, derive); one place to change them.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (H7's security review, D559): the availability words changed. "Available… Hana can open this wallet for you" showed on apps where the user has no wallet, and promised an action the page doesn't offer yet.
- Address impact: none.

### D555. The partner's link to Hana Home is `/home?appId=app_…`
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts` (`linkedAppId`) · For D502 ("found … by its `appId` (the partner's link)")
- Decision: `/home?appId=<app id>` (exactly that one parameter, of the app id's form) opens that app's page after sign-in, with one `GET /v1/home/apps?appId=` read. Anything else in the query is ignored. The page never changes its own URL.
- Why: an app id is public and can't be walked (D502); nothing of the user's is in the link.
- Address impact: none.

### D556. Hana Home links a Stellar address to StellarExpert; an EVM address gets no explorer link
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts` (`STELLAR_ACCOUNT_URL`)
- Decision: beside the copy button, a Stellar address links to its StellarExpert account page for the env's network (a fixed URL of Hana's choosing with the address appended, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). An EVM address has only the copy button: it is the same address on every EVM chain, so no one explorer is right for it. The spec's F3 says "copy and explorer links" without naming chains.
- Options: an EVM link to one default chain (which one is a product choice); a list of chains (long, and most would be empty).
- Address impact: none.

### D557. A partner's app name is never a heading on Hana Home, is held to the display-safety rule and cut to 60 characters; a linked app that isn't the user's doesn't open
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-api.ts` (`homeAppName`, `HOME_NAME_SHOWN`, `HOME_UNNAMED_APP`), `home-page.ts` (`appPage`, `loadFirst`) · From H7's independent security review (medium) · Amends D555
- Problem: `/home?appId=` made a partner's own words the landing heading on the auth origin. A partner could name its app "Hana security notice: wallet locked, restore at …" and send users the link.
- Decision:
  - A name is shown only if it passes `isDisplaySafeLine` (no control, direction-changing or invisible character) and is 1 to 200 characters; otherwise Hana's stand-in "Unnamed app" takes its place. The app stays listed: a user's wallet is never hidden by its app's name.
  - A shown name is cut to 60 characters and "…". The full name is nowhere in the page, including the "View …" button's label.
  - An app's page has fixed Hana headings ("App details", "App" or "Apps that share one wallet"); the name is a value inside the neutral box under them.
  - `/home?appId=` opens an app's page only when the app is the user's own (`mine`). For any other app the user lands on their own list, with the linked app below it under "The app from your link" and Hana's notice that it has no wallet on record for them there and that the name and address are the app's own.
- Left as is: names and origins still show in the list's cards, as text, in the neutral box that marks partner content on every auth page.
- Address impact: none.

### D558. `/home` sends `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin-allow-popups`, and answers its sign-in child only at `/login?mode=home`
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/pages/host.ts` (`AUTH_PAGE_HEADERS`), `home-page.ts` (`childAtLogin`) · From H7's security review (two low findings)
- Decision: `/home` alone among the auth pages sends COOP `same-origin-allow-popups`: a page on another origin that opened it keeps no handle (it can't navigate the window or watch it), and the sign-in child Home opens itself keeps its opener. The other auth pages still send no COOP: the partner page or the vault opens them and must reach them. Home also answers its child's hello only while the child's address reads as `/login?mode=home` on this origin, the mirror of the child's check of Home (D552); a window whose address can't be read gets no answer.
- Checked: the sign-in works with the header in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (`apps/e2e/tests/home.spec.ts`), and a foreign opener's handle reads as closed.
- Address impact: none.

### D559. Hana Home's availability words say only what is true now; the account is compared by method and id; a request overtaken by a new sign-in shows nothing
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h7`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts` (`coverageText`, `signedIn`, `request`) · From H7's security review · Amends D553 and D554
- Decision:
  - Words (replacing D554's): for the user's own app, "Does this wallet depend on the app?" with "Stays reachable" (signing in to the wallet would still work through Hana if the app stopped running), "Depends on the app", "Out of reach", "Not checked yet". For an app where Hana knows no wallet of theirs, "Would a wallet here depend on the app?" with "Supported", "Depends on the app", "Out of reach", "Not checked yet", each saying Hana has no wallet on record for them there. No sentence says "available", "open", "export" or "move": the page offers none of those yet. H8 revisits the words when export exists.
  - A new sign-in is "the same account" only if both the sign-in method and its id match (ready for email in H10, where two methods' ids must never be taken for one person).
  - A request whose sign-in has ended or been replaced before it answered shows no problem and is not sent again; an answer for another account is thrown away.
- Address impact: none.

## Hana Home H8: key export in Home (branch `feat/hana-home-h8`), 2026-11-10

Built on `feat/hana-home-h8` (on top of H7), not merged, not deployed. Every decision here was **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (D575–D584 and, from the security review, D600–D604). No path, key rule or derivation changes in any of them.

### D575. Hana Home moves a wallet out from a collapsed section on the app's page; nothing in the address opens or starts it
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/web/src/auth/home-export.ts` (`startHomeExport`), `home-page.ts` (`moving`, `appPage`) · Source: the spec's "Wallets and export" and "Lock-in stance" (D41), H7's review ("`?appId=` must never preselect or start an export")
- Decision: an app's page ends with one collapsed button, "Move this wallet to another wallet app". Expanding it shows what it does and D430's warning; "Sign in again to continue" starts the per-app sign-in; then the wallet's two addresses, a choice of chain, the warning again with the typed `EXPORT`, and Show key / Copy key. Continue, Show key and Copy key sit behind the approval guard; a shown key hides after 60 s (D430).
- The section always starts collapsed. The page reads `?appId=` only to choose which app's page to open (D555, D557); no parameter expands the section, picks a chain or starts a sign-in, and each step needs a real click in the page.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (H8's security review, D600): the app a link named is not offered the move at all in that page load, the user's own included.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (D677, asked for by the user; confirmed by the user 2026-11-10): collapsed, the section is a heading, one sentence and a "Show how to move it" button, like the devices section, instead of one full-width button.
- The reveal is one module shared with the export window (`key-reveal.ts`: the guard over a screen's buttons, Show/Hide, Copy, the 60 s hide, the clipboard blank), so the safeguards can't drift apart. The export window's behaviour is unchanged, with one addition (D580: a shown key hides before printing).
- Address impact: none.

### D576. The section is offered for the user's own apps and for apps they found themselves; never for the app a link named
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts` (`homeExportRoute`, `HOME_EXPORT_OFF_TEXT`)
- Decision: the section offers the sign-in on an app that is the user's (`mine`), and on an app with no wallet on record that the user reached through their own list or search. That second case is the shutdown case Home exists for: a purged directory (the spec's "the user then finds the app by search, and a derive shows the addresses"). There the wording says Hana has no wallet on record and will look for one, and the API refuses with `home_no_wallet` when the chain shows none (D544), before anything is spent.
- The app a `/home?appId=` link named, when it isn't the user's, is never offered in that page load, however the user reaches its page: the section says to open Hana Home without the link and find the app by name. Amended 2026-11-10 (D600): the same holds when the linked app is the user's own.
- Options: (a) this; (b) the user's own apps only (simpler, but a user whose app shut down and was purged could never move the wallet, which is the point of Home; not recommended); (c) every app, the link's included (a partner's link would then lead straight to a key screen; not recommended).
- Address impact: none.

### D577. The per-app sign-in uses its own message, fixes one use and key index 0 in the child, asks Google to sign in again, and sends no `login_hint`
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/core/src/protocol.ts` (`hana:home-derive-params`), `login-page.ts` (`checkHomeDerive`), `home-export.ts` (`prepare`, `awaitToken`) · Deviates from the spec ("Home sends `login_hint`")
- Decision: to open one app's wallet, `/home` sends its child `/login?mode=home` the message `hana:home-derive-params` (signer, client, scope, session key, end, salt, nonce, relay slot and key). The child takes it only from a same-origin opener at `/home` (as D552), recomputes `sessionNonce` with `keyIndex 0` and `maxUses 1` written in the child itself, and goes to Google with `max_age=0`. No other mode takes the message.
- No `login_hint`: the hint would put the user's Google id in the child's address and the browser's history, and through a message. The page instead compares the token's account with Hana Home's sign-in before anything is sent; a different account reads "Sign in as the same account you used in Hana Home" (`home_account_mismatch`) and costs nothing. The API checks the same again.
- Options: send the hint as the spec says (one click fewer for a user with several Google accounts; the id in a URL). Not recommended.
- Address impact: none (`key_index` 0 is the address Home shows; the nonce layout is the existing `sessionNonce`).

### D578. H8 opens wallets through the shared client and an app's own Google client; the exit client's `/home/callback` is proposed for H10
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8` (the two routes); **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (where `/home/callback` goes) · Built: `home-export.ts` (`homeExportRoute`, `checkRoute`) · Source: D490, D491, D550, the plan's H8 ("decide with the spec whether signing in through the exit client belongs here or in H10"); the spec leaves the batch open
- Decision: H8 signs in for an app with coverage `shared` (Hana's shared client) or `hana_client` / `partner_client` (a Google client of the app itself), both through the existing `/login/callback`. Before answering the child, the page reads NEAR itself: `get_scope` with `allow_shared` and the client in `get_config().shared_clients`, or `scope_for_client('google', client) === scope`. A mismatch stops before Google (`not_covered`); an unreadable chain says so (`near_unreadable`).
- Coverage `exit` and `email` say "Hana Home can't move this wallet yet" and offer no sign-in. `/home/callback` (D491), which both the per-app sign-in through the exit client and Home's own sign-in without a shared client need (D550's open point), is proposed for **H10**.
- Why H10: it is a new page on the auth origin, the only one that receives exit tokens, with a new redirect URI and a deploy-checklist item; it deserves its own security review rather than a place inside "keys in memory". H10 already builds the email exit and changes the same child. Nothing links to `/home` before H12.
- Cost (to weigh): on an env with an exit client in force, coverage reports `exit` for every app whose normal route is gone, and for partner-held clients too (D490's order), so those wallets can't be moved out from Home until `/home/callback` exists. If H10 slips, do it as a small batch of its own before H12. D550's "no shared client in force means sign-in is unavailable" stays open until then.
- Address impact: none (`aud` never enters the path).
- Note, 2026-11-10 (H10, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10): built as proposed: `/home/callback` and the exit client for coverage `exit`, email codes for coverage `email` (D618, D624, D626).

### D579. Hana Home derives the vault's path: the identity's own, or its account root's only after both NEAR providers agree
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (the wording of the two refusals) · Built: `packages/web/src/auth/export-path.ts` (`exportPath`, shared with `export-page.ts`), `home-export.ts` · Implements D263 for Home
- Decision: the path comes from one function the export window and Hana Home share. `get_identity` names the identity or its root; a root's path is read again on `rpc` and `rpcFallback` separately and used only if both agree with the first view and show the root as an account root (`confirmPath`). The identity's own path takes no second opinion, as in the vault: only the MPC can answer for it, and the pairing check against the pinned key refuses anything else (a page told "own" while the chain derived the root shows nothing: `pairing_failed`).
- Refusals: the providers disagree, `path_disputed` ("NEAR providers disagree about which wallet this sign-in opens, so Hana Home opened nothing"); a provider didn't answer or the env has no second one, `path_unconfirmed`; a pending link, `link_pending`. Nothing is relayed in any of them.
- Test: `packages/web/test/auth/home-export.test.ts` "golden" holds Home to the frozen `derivation-v1.json` vectors (paths, secrets, addresses and export strings), for an own path and for a member reaching its root.
- Address impact: none. `pathIdentity` and the path string are unchanged; the function was moved, not rewritten, and the export window's tests pass unchanged.

### D580. The opened wallet's secret lives at most 5 minutes in the page and is erased on leaving; a chain key lives inside one Show or Copy
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts` (`HOME_PRK_LIFETIME_MS`, `wipeSecret`, `lock`, `chainSecret`), `key-reveal.ts` · D98 item 6, the spec's step 4
- Decision: after the derive the page holds PRK in one buffer for 5 minutes (a timer, and a check against the server-corrected clock every second and when the tab is shown again). It is zeroed at 5 minutes, on "Lock now", when the user goes back to the list, signs out, signs in as another account, and on `pagehide` (close, reload, or the back/forward cache). The CKD answer's secret is zeroed as soon as PRK is taken from it. A chain's private key is derived inside one Show or Copy and zeroed in the same call. Coming back to the app's page starts collapsed, and opening again needs a new sign-in.
- The 5 minutes run from the derive, not from Hana Home's sign-in: a wallet that is open stays open for its 5 minutes if Home's own 15 minutes end meanwhile (nothing new can be fetched). Option: lock when Home's sign-in ends (stricter, but a user reading the key would lose it mid-way). Not built.
- What can't be erased, as in the export window: the key's text while shown (one text node, replaced by dots on hide), a copy in the clipboard (blanked after 60 s and when the wallet locks, where the browser allows it), and the strings themselves until the engine collects them. A screenshot can't be prevented; the page says "Make sure nobody can see your screen". New for both pages: a shown key hides before printing (`beforeprint`), and the stylesheet blanks the box in print.
- Address impact: none.

### D581. Hana Home sends a derive once and never re-sends it
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts` (`resendableUntil: 0` to `loginOnChain`) · Applies D553 to `POST /v1/home/login`; deviates from the export window, which re-sends once
- Decision: the page sends `POST /v1/home/login` once per sign-in. An outcome it can't learn is looked up on NEAR (`get_session`, the transaction), as the login table does; anything else is a refusal with "Try again", which goes back to the first screen and a new Google sign-in.
- Why: D553 says Home never sends a request again by itself, and each derive spends the daily ceiling and the user's own windows.
- Cost: a passing `near_unavailable` or `relayer_busy` costs the user one more Google sign-in.
- Address impact: none.

### D582. Home shows the opened wallet's own addresses, says so when the record differs, and keeps them on the app's page where Hana had none
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts` (`mismatch`), `home-page.ts` (`opened`)
- Decision: once a wallet is open the section shows the two addresses worked out from its own key. If an address on record differs, a warning says the record is different and the ones shown are the wallet's own; the move goes on (the spec's "warns on a difference": a compromised API can show a wrong address in the list, never change the wallet). Where Hana had no address on record, the app's page then shows the opened wallet's addresses, marked as such, until the user signs out or reloads (public values, memory only).
- Option: stop on a difference (safer-looking, but it would let a wrong directory row block a user's exit). Not recommended.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (H8's security review, D601): a difference does stop the move on a linked member's path and when the answer was looked up on NEAR; the warning remains only on the identity's own path with the API's own answer.
- Address impact: none.

### D583. `/home`'s policy gains the two NEAR RPC origins: exactly the export window's list
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/web/src/auth/pages.ts` (`connectSources`), `apps/api/src/pages/host.ts` (`authPageDirectives`) · Completes D551
- Decision: `/home` is served with `connect-src {apiUrl} {rpc} {rpcFallback} https://www.googleapis.com`, the same origins as `/export` and nothing more (a test holds the two equal). The page reads NEAR only after the user presses "Sign in again to continue": listing and viewing still read no chain (a test fails on any read).
- Address impact: none.

### D584. Wording: the section, its refusals, and the availability sentence now that the move exists
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-problems.ts` (`PROBLEM_TEXT`, `DERIVE_RATE_LIMITED`), `home-export.ts`, `home-page.ts` (`coverageText`, `MOVE_WORDS`) · Revisits D559 as it asked
- Availability (final wording proposed): the badges stay "Stays reachable", "Depends on the app", "Out of reach", "Not checked yet" (and "Supported" for an app with no wallet on record). The sentence gains one clause only where this page offers the move for the user's own wallet: "You can also move it to another wallet app, further down this page." and, for an app's own Google sign-in, "To stop depending on it, you can move the wallet to another wallet app, further down this page." No badge says "export" or "available": the badge answers whether the wallet depends on the app, and the section says what can be done.
- Refusals use H7's sentences by code (`home_no_wallet`, `home_busy`, `home_account_mismatch`, `link_pending`, `not_covered`, the unreachable family), each with the code and the request ID. Added: `rate_limited` on a derive reads "This wallet was opened too many times. Wait an hour and try again." (H7's "wait a minute" is wrong for hourly and daily limits); `shared_login_disabled`, `unregistered_client` and `scope_mismatch` read as `not_covered`; `ckd_failed`, `pairing_failed`, `session_exists` and the token refusals each say that nothing was shown and to sign in again; a 401 ends Home's sign-in and says so.
- Section words: "Move this wallet to another wallet app" (the spec's label, never "export" in a heading), "Confirm it's you", "Opening your wallet", "Your wallet is open", "Your Stellar key" / "Your EVM key", "Wallet locked".
- Address impact: none.

### D600. The app a link named is never moved out in that page load, the user's own included
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts` (`linkScope`), `home-export.ts` (`homeExportRoute`) · From H8's independent security review (M1) · Amends D575 and D576
- Problem: `/home?appId=<an app the victim uses>` opened the user's own funded wallet's page, where the section was offered with no caution about the link. A phisher could send it with "press Move this wallet and paste the key here".
- Decision: for the app the page's link named, whether or not it is the user's, the section offers no sign-in in that page load, however the user gets to the app's page (the link, the list, a search, after signing in again). It says: "You came to this app through a link. Hana Home never moves a wallet out from a link, because a link can come from anyone. If you want to move this wallet, open Hana Home yourself, without the link, and find the app in your list or by its name." Addresses and the Support ID still show, and the availability sentence doesn't mention the move there.
- Cost: a user who followed an honest "Manage in Hana Home" link has to open Hana Home again without it to move that wallet. H12's own links should not carry `appId` if they are meant to lead to the move.
- Address impact: none.

### D601. A wallet that differs from the record is not shown on a linked path, or when the answer was looked up on NEAR
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts` (`awaitToken`: `linked`, `answered`), `home-problems.ts` (`address_mismatch`) · From H8's independent security review (M2) · Amends D582
- Problem: the pairing check proves a key is the MPC's for the path asked about. If both NEAR providers lie "member of root R", and the outcome is read back from the RPC by its transaction, R's owner can forge an answer that passes it; D582 only warned, so the user could import an attacker-held key. The export window stops there (`address_mismatch` against the vault's address).
- Decision: when an address on record differs from the opened wallet's, the page refuses with `address_mismatch` and zeroes the secret if the path is an account root's (a linked member), or if the result did not come in the API's own answer (it was recovered from NEAR). On the identity's own path with the API's own answer, D582's warning stays: only the MPC could have made that key.
- Limits: with no address on record there is nothing to compare (a purged scope). Against a compromised API the comparison has no value, since the API controls the record too; it is a check against a lying RPC, and a hint of a wrong directory row.
- Address impact: none.

### D602. A derive's limit sentence says how long the API asked to wait
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-api.ts` (`login`, `retryAfterS`), `home-problems.ts` (`deriveRateLimited`) · From H8's review (L2) · Amends D584
- Decision: on a `rate_limited` answer to `POST /v1/home/login` the page reads `retry-after` (the API exposes it) and says "This wallet was opened too many times. Try again in about N minutes." up to an hour, "in about N hours" beyond, and "Try again later." when the API gave no time. It replaces "Wait an hour", which was false for the daily limit.

### D603. The opened wallet's secret is erased when the tab is frozen
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts` (the `freeze` listener) · From H8's review (L3) · Amends D580
- Decision: a frozen background tab runs no timers, so the 5 minutes could pass with PRK still in memory. The page locks the wallet on the document's `freeze` event (as "Lock now"), besides the timer, the server-clock check and `pagehide`. A browser without the event falls back on the check made when the tab is shown again, before anything can be shown or copied.
- Option not built: lock after a short time hidden (it would also lock a user who switches to their wallet app to paste the key).

### D604. The per-app step is described as choosing the Google account again, not as proof that it's you
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h8`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts`, `login-page.ts` (`checkHomeDerive`) · From H8's review (L4) · Amends D584; the mechanism is unchanged
- Decision: the page no longer says "To be sure it's you" or "Confirm it's you". It says "First you choose your Google account again; it must be the account you used for Hana Home. Google may not ask for your password again.", and the step's heading is "Choose your Google account again".
- Why: Google sends no `auth_time` even with `max_age=0`, and with `prompt=select_account` the step can be one click. Whoever can use the user's Google session on the device can open every app's wallet from Home, where the export window reached one app's. `docs/security.md` states it. A real re-authentication is not available from Google's implicit flow today; whether Home needs another factor before mainnet is for the production-readiness check.

## User-testing fixes (branch `fix/testing-1110`), 2026-11-10

### D570. A watchdog channel with no credentials is recorded once per alert and held, not retried, and is not a delivery error
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built on `fix/testing-1110` (`apps/watchdog/src/alerts.ts` `deliverAlerts`, `store.ts`, migration `0003_unconfigured_channels.sql`; `apps/admin/src/monitoring.ts` `deliveriesLatest`) · Amends D85
- Found: on sandbox-dev Slack has no webhook. The sender answered `not configured` like a failed send, so Slack stayed in each alert's `pending_channels` and was tried again on every 5-minute run: forever for a critical alert (only warnings give up, after a day), resolved and acknowledged ones included. Each try wrote a `deliveries` row, `alert_delivery` reported `error` on every run (13 failed), and an alert's last 20 rows in the admin were all Slack's.
- Decision: the run asks the channel whether it is configured before sending. If not, the alert gets one `deliveries` row (`ok: false`, `not configured`) the first time, and the channel moves to a new column `alerts.unconfigured_channels` (held). Held channels are never tried while unconfigured, and later runs write nothing for them. `alert_delivery`'s `failed` counts only sends a configured channel refused or lost; the run that holds a channel says `N held (channel not configured)` in the check's detail and stays `ok`. The `channel_not_configured` warning stays the signal. A real failure (HTTP error, timeout, a throw) keeps its retries, and 15-minute re-sends on configured channels are unchanged. A run in which every channel is held is not counted as a round (`send_count`, `last_sent_at` unchanged), so the first real send is not marked "re-sent".
- Admin: an alert view also carries `deliveriesLatest`, the newest row of each channel out of all the watchdog served, shown above the last 20 rows, so one noisy channel can't hide the others.
- Why a column and not a lookup in `deliveries`: it costs no extra read, where a lookup would scan the rows the old code already wrote on every run (D1 bills rows read; sandbox-dev is on the free tier, D417).
- Deploy: the watchdog's migration 0003 before its Worker, and the admin Worker. Old `not configured` rows stay (history).
- Not changed, reported: resolving an alert stops nothing by itself. An outstanding first delivery of a resolved alert is still retried (critical: until it succeeds; warning: for a day), and a resolved critical alert is re-sent every 15 min until acknowledged. Event alerts are resolved at creation, so "never send a resolved alert" would silence every event; the ack is the stop. To decide separately whether a resolved, acknowledged critical alert's failing first delivery should give up after a day like a warning's.

### D571. When a held channel gets its credentials, only alerts still open are sent on it
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built on `fix/testing-1110` (`deliverAlerts` `open`, `Store.alertsToDeliver`)
- Decision: "open" is what the status endpoint already calls open: the condition still holds (`resolved_at` null), or the alert is critical and unacknowledged. For those, the run after the channel is configured sends it as a first delivery (not waiting for a 15-minute round, and also past a warning's one-day retry window). An alert that closed meanwhile (a resolved condition, a warning event, an acknowledged critical event) is never sent on that channel; it keeps its one `not configured` row.
- Why: a channel set up weeks later must not replay history into Slack or a pager, but someone should hear about what is wrong now.
- Alternatives: (a) send every held alert: a flood of stale alerts on the day a channel is added. Not recommended. (b) send none, only alerts raised afterwards: an unacknowledged critical alert would still reach the new channel at its next re-send, but an open warning condition never would. Not recommended.
- If a held channel's send then fails, it becomes an ordinary outstanding first delivery (retried, counted as failed).

### D572. Whether the launcher can be clicked travels in its own port event, `launcherKind`, and reaches partners as `launcher`'s `clickable`
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (a separate, new message: SDKs already released ignore it and keep working, new SDKs get the flag; putting `clickable` on the `ui` message was considered and declined because released SDKs reject unknown fields) · Built on `fix/testing-1110` (`packages/core/src/protocol.ts` `launcherKind`, `packages/web/src/vault/launcher.ts`, `vault.ts`, `client/client.ts`; `apps/smoke`, `apps/demo`)
- Found: every auto-sign ends with a 3-second "Signed by Hana under …" flash, announced with the same `ui {launcher: 'show'}` as a button the user must click. The SDK passed it on as `launcher {visible: true}`, so the smoke page counted a popup (an auto-signed request more than 3 s after the last was labelled "after the consent screen"), the demo page told the user to click, and the integration guide told partners the same.
- Decision: the vault sends `launcherKind {clickable}` just before each `ui` show (false for a flash, true for an intent); the SDK remembers it and emits `launcher {visible, label, clickable}` (`clickable` false when hidden; a show with no kind before it counts as a button). `visible` and `label` are unchanged.
- Why not a third field on `ui`: the SDK validates `ui` as exactly `{launcher, label}`, and 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 are with partners. They would drop a `ui` with another key, and with it the launcher itself: no login fallback, no approval, no export. A new event is dropped harmlessly by an older SDK (as `mainnetDemoPrices` was done). No version gate and no SDK version bump is needed.
- For the next SDK release notes (the repo keeps no changelog): the `launcher` event gains `clickable: boolean`; prompt a click only when `visible && clickable`.

### D573. The test-app note says what the mainnet demo signs when the demo is on; the consent screen names known chains and units
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (the user saw the after screenshot) · Built on `fix/testing-1110` (`packages/web/src/auth/approve-page.ts` `TEST_APP_DEMO_NOTE`, `render-consent.ts`, `auth.css`; `packages/core/src/networks.ts` `evmChainInfo`; the popup messages' `mainnetDemo`) · Amends D39's note for D428 apps
- Decision: the vault adds `mainnetDemo: true` to `hana:approve-request` and `hana:consent-request` for a test app whose demo is on as it last read it (a dev testnet build only; valid only with `testApp`). The popup, itself only in a dev testnet build, then shows: "Test app with Hana’s mainnet demo on: besides test networks, Hana ID signs real transactions on Base and Stellar’s public network here, up to $9.99 each. Those always ask you first and are never signed automatically. Other mainnets are refused. The keys are test keys that can be reset or lost, so keep only small amounts at this account." With the demo off the note is unchanged. A request for a demo mainnet keeps its red banner instead. The note appears on the approval and consent screens only; login, export and email sharing never had it.
- The flag is the vault's last read, not a fresh one: it changes only this sentence. Whether a mainnet request is signed is still decided by a fresh read (D428).
- Consent screen: an EVM chain is headed by Hana's own name for it with the number beside it ("Sepolia (testnet)  EVM chain 11155111"; "Base  EVM chain 8453"), from `TEST_EVM_CHAINS` plus a short list of mainnets in `@hana-id/core` (display only, it allows nothing); a chain Hana doesn't know stays "EVM chain <id>". Never a name from the policy. Native amounts carry the chain's coin ("0.001 ETH (1000000000000000 wei)"), or "0.001 of this chain’s native coin (… wei)" on an unknown chain.
- Layout bug fixed with it: the contract's short address had the class `address`, which is the email sharing sheet's block style (padding, border, margin), so as inline text its box covered the lines around it. The chip has its own class and is an inline-block that wraps whole; the sheet's rule is now `p.address`.
- Not changed: the approval popup's own "Chain ID <n>" rows still show the number only.

## Partner onboarding (branch `feat/partner-onboarding`), 2026-11-10

### D651. Onboarding: the admin console prepares the scope registration, one council command runs it
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built on `feat/partner-onboarding` (`apps/admin/public/app.js` `scopePanel`, `scopeRegisterPlan`; `apps/admin/src/scope-registration.ts`, `GET /api/me` `scopeRegistration`; `apps/admin/scripts/gen-wrangler.ts` `SCOPE_REGISTRATION`; `scripts/lib/admin-scope.ts` `registeredScopeId`, `owner-tx.ts` `castVoteTx`, `admin-owner.ts` `owner:vote`)
- Found (read-only investigation of `develop` 5bbd2a60): nothing in either portal registered a partner's scope on chain; "Create an app" needs one whose Google owners are owners of the organisation, staff couldn't see those owners' Google `sub`s, and `scope:register` didn't print the new scope id on the council path.
- Decision: the organisation page gets **Register a scope for this organisation**. It gathers the organisation's owners now (role owner, not disabled, a Google account recorded) and lists everyone else with why not yet (an owner invite not accepted, an owner still in the grant period, a disabled owner). Staff tick the owners (1–5, none ticked by default: D657) and get the exact commands for the env, a dry run and the one that sends (D658), always with Hana's shared login (`--allow-shared`; the partner's own client is added later with its proof: D656): on a dev env on testnet `… scope:register --allow-shared --owner-google <sub> … --member <first member> --approve-with <second member>` (both votes in one run), on another council env `--member <the member chosen by radio button>` (it prints the votes), for an account owner no `--member`. Problems block the command and say why; the no-shared-client env and an organisation without a security contact ("Create an app" needs one) are warnings. It sends nothing and holds no key; a Google `sub` is shown to staff and put in the command only, never in a URL or log.
- The manifest values the command needs (owner kind, owner, council members, whether the council's keys are on disk, shared client ids) reach the SPA as the admin Worker's `SCOPE_REGISTRATION` var through `GET /api/me`, each checked as a plain account or client id (they end up in a shell command); absent or malformed, the panel says it can't prepare the command.
- `scope:register` now prints `Registered scope: s…` and the next step on the council path too, from the `scope_registered` event in the passing vote's receipt logs (`sendTx` returns them with each receipt's executor); `owner:vote` prints it for the member whose vote passes a registration (D659).
- Not built: detecting the organisation's scopes on chain that have no app yet (D655). "Create an app"'s help points at the panel instead.
- An organisation that already has a live app gets the form behind one button. `apps/admin/test-spa/ux.test.ts` asserted the SPA never mentions `scope:register`; changed deliberately to: Legacy apps never shows it, and the SPA mentions it only in this panel.

### D652. Forms that need an on-chain owner say so instead; the partner guide says who can do what
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built on `feat/partner-onboarding` (`apps/console/web/src/pages/app/ChainOwner.tsx`, `Origins.tsx`, `Signing.tsx`; `docs/integration.md` section 1 "On-chain owners", sections 6, 9 and "Raw signing"; `packages/web/README.md`; the admin's "Propose origins" help)
- Decision: in the partner console, for an organisation owner who isn't an on-chain owner of the app's scope, the Origins add form, the policy editor and "Turn raw signing on" are replaced by one line: what needs an on-chain owner, who the on-chain owners are (members by address, NEAR accounts by id, anyone else as "a Google account outside your organisation"), and that an on-chain owner can add them from the scope page (the SetOwners proposal), or, when no organisation owner is on chain, to ask Hana. Read from the scope page's own route (one NEAR view per page, only for an owner of an active organisation; Signing reads it once for both panels); NEAR down shows the error with a retry, never the form. Kill switches (remove an origin, remove the policy, raw signing off) stay for every owner. These are every control whose write the API checks against the scope's on-chain owners (`confirmStepUp`: `origin.add`, `policy.set`, `raw_sign.on`); the scope page and Email login already used `youAreOnChainOwner`; settings, resume, keys, members and branding don't need it.
- The guide: section 1 gets "What Hana needs from you" and the order (owners accept the invite before the scope is registered; what they receive) and an "On-chain owners" paragraph (who can add origins and policies, how a later owner is added: SetOwners, the timelock, Execute); adding origins, the policy and raw signing name on-chain owners; "send Hana the client ID" is gone (D656: a partner's own client is added only with its proof).
- The staff "Propose origins" help no longer says "Full https:// origins": it states the origin rules (https with a real host name; on a test app in a dev env `http://localhost:<port>` and `http://localhost:*`), that a staff proposal always waits the full period, and that it is refused for one waiting period after the scope moved to the organisation.
- The sample partner repo (separate) should say the same: see the batch report's list.

### D653. A staff proposal of a localhost origin on a test app in a dev env could take effect when announced
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **declined for now, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Not built
- The security review's conditions, if it is ever built: testnet test apps only; keep the announcement (the email still goes out) and both guards (the dev-env and network checks, and the post-assignment refusal for every other origin); and know that it removes the cancel window for those origins if staff accounts are compromised (an attacker with staff access could add `http://localhost:*` with no time for the partner to cancel).
- Today `loopbackWaiver` (`apps/api/src/changes/lifecycle.ts`) applies only to a member's proposal; a staff proposal of `http://localhost:*` on a test app waits `appChangeDelayMs` and is refused for one delay after a scope assignment, like any staff proposal (spec "Staff proposals": no waiver except createApp's `no_session`).
- Proposal: extend the waiver to `proposed_by_kind = 'hana'` under the same conditions (loopback or the localhost wildcard, a test app, a dev env, a non-production network), and lift the post-assignment refusal for those origins only. It changes no authority (staff can already propose the origin; only the wait goes) and only in dev envs. Recommended only if partners keep needing staff to add localhost for them; with D652 an on-chain owner adds it themselves, at once.

### D654. A legacy scope owned only by NEAR accounts gets partner owners through a dev-env CLI command
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **declined for now, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Not built
- The security review's conditions, if it is ever built: refuse every non-dev env (as `scope:add-email-client` does), and require each `--owner-google` to be a current owner of the organisation the scope belongs to (read from the console, as "Create an app" does), so the command can't hand a scope to a stranger.
- Found: a scope whose owners are all `Owner::Near` (sandbox-dev's legacy `s1`, `s2`, "Smoke A/B") moves to an organisation freely, but then nobody in it is an on-chain owner, and the console's SetOwners needs an on-chain Google owner to sign. No tool proposes SetOwners as a NEAR owner.
- Proposal: `admin <env> scope:set-owners --scope <id> --owner-google <sub> … [--keep-near] [--yes]`, dev envs only like `scope:add-email-client` (whose `nearOwnerKey` it reuses): the scope's NEAR owner sends `propose_change(SetOwners, auth: Near)`, then, once due, `execute_change` (or prints when to re-run). Same authority as today (the NEAR owner's key already allows it); the timelock and the announcement on chain stay. Recommended for the two legacy scopes only; a partner scope should be registered with Google owners (D651).

### D655. Offering the organisation's registered scopes in "Create an app" waits for an index of scopes
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **declined for now, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Not built
- The security review's condition, if it is ever built: offer only a scope with at least one Google owner (and every Google owner an owner of the organisation), never a NEAR-only scope, which would otherwise move into any organisation that asks.
- The contract has no view listing scopes or their owners (`get_scope` by id only; ids are a counter), and the API's `scopes` table holds a scope only once it has an app. So "scopes of this organisation on chain without an app" is not one cached view call. Options: (a) probe `get_scope` upward from the highest id the API knows until `null` and keep those whose Google owners are all organisation owners (a few uncached views per open; a scope registered for another organisation in between is skipped); (b) record `scope_registered` events (the watchdog already reads the chain) into a table the admin reads; (c) a contract view (excluded: no contract change).
- Recommendation: none for now. Staff copy the id the command prints (D651); revisit (a) if typing it causes mistakes.

### D656. A new scope is registered with Hana's shared login only; a partner's own Google client is added with its proof
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: decided after the security review of `feat/partner-onboarding`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built on `feat/partner-onboarding` (`apps/admin/public/app.js` `scopeRegisterPlan`; `docs/integration.md` sections 1 and 6; `docs/operations.md` "Onboarding a partner on testnet")
- Found (review, MEDIUM): `admin_register_scope` takes `clients` with no client proof, where `register_scope` and `AddClient` require one. A partner could send Hana another partner's public client id; Hana would register it under the wrong scope, the real owner's registration would then be refused, and if that client ever listed this env's login callback, the wrong site would show its consent screen with those users' wallets in the wrong scope.
- Decision: the panel has no client-id field, and its commands always carry `--allow-shared` and never `--client`. The partner adds their own client from their console's scope page (`AddClient`, which takes a sign-in with that client: the proof that they control it, plus the contract's timelock) and can then turn shared login off there (`disable_shared_login`, refused while the scope has no client of its own). That is the safe route to a scope without shared login. The guide no longer offers "send Hana the client ID".
- Not changed: the CLI's `scope:register --client` stays for Hana's own test clients (operations "Google Cloud OAuth"); it is never used for a client a partner sends.

### D658. The panel shows a dry run and the command that sends, chooses the proposer by radio button, re-reads the members at each Copy, and offers only digit Google ids
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: decided after the security review; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built on `feat/partner-onboarding` (`scopeRegisterPlan`, `ownersStillCurrent`, `commandBlock`'s `beforeCopy`; `scripts/lib/admin-args.ts` `ownersFromArgs`)
- Two commands, each with its own Copy: the dry run (no `--yes`: prints the call, sends nothing), then the same with `--yes` (on a dev env it casts both votes). On a council env without keys on disk, a radio button per council member (none chosen at first) fills `--member`; no placeholder with shell characters. Each Copy reads `GET /api/orgs/:org` again and refuses (nothing copied) when a ticked owner was removed, made a viewer or disabled since the page was read; the page says when the owners were read.
