### D659. A scope id is read only from the signer's own receipts, and `owner:vote` only for the signer's scope registration
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: decided after the security review; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built on `feat/partner-onboarding` (`scripts/lib/near.ts` `receiptLogs`, `admin-scope.ts` `registeredScopeId`, `admin-owner.ts` `ownerVoteCmd`)
- Found (review, LOW): `owner:vote` read any `scope_registered` line in any receipt, for any owners, so a contract the call touched could make it print a scope id that isn't real.

## Hana Home H9: devices and revocation (branch `feat/hana-home-h9`), 2026-11-10

Built on `feat/hana-home-h9` (from `develop` with H7 and H8), not merged, not deployed. Every decision here was **confirmed by the user
2026-11-10** (D606–D615, and D661–D665 from H9's security review). No path, key rule or derivation changes in any of them; no migration, no cron.

### D606. Home's devices, consents and email sharing are the account root's, by the same rule as the app list
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/home/root.ts` (`scopeRoot`, `overlayRoots`) · Carries out the spec's "Home: list and revoke"
- Decision: in a scope, Home's rows are those of the account root that the wallet directory records for the signed-in `(provider, sub)` with status `active` (the member's row → its account's `root` row), else the identity's own. The path is `{scope}#{provider}#{sub}#0`, key index 0 (the only index a vault opens), hashed as `vault_shares.path_hash` and `vault_consents.path_hash` hold it; email consents use the account's User ID (`end_users.token_sub`, or `identitySub` computed for a user with no row). The list and all three stops resolve the root the same way, so whatever is listed can be stopped and nothing else can.
- Options: (a) this (no chain read; a link still in its delay, or a stale `active` row after an unlink whose sync failed, behaves as in `GET /v1/home/apps`, D500); (b) read `get_identity` on chain per scope (exact, but a subrequest per scope, which the free plan's 50 can't afford for a list). **Recommendation: (a)**, with (b) only if a stale directory row is judged worse than the app list's same exposure.
- Amended 2026-11-10 by D661 (H9's security review, medium): a member-resolved root is confirmed on chain before any stop and before addresses are shown; "the app list has the same exposure" didn't hold for personal data and writes.
- Address impact: none.

### D607. `GET /v1/home/devices`: 10 of the user's own scopes a page, 25 devices and 25 tab consents a scope, D1 only
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/home/devices.ts`
- Decision: no parameter or `?cursor=` pages the directory's scopes for this identity, 10 at a time in scope order; `?scopeId=` reads one scope (an app's page, with the identity's own path when the directory has no row). Per scope: the live shares (newest first, 25, `more: true` past that), each with its active consent, the active consents of apps that keep no share (25), the shared addresses per app (25), and the names of the apps named. One D1 read for the roots and one D1 batch of four small statements per scope; no chain read. 30/min per IP and 60/min per Home key, as the app list (the spec's table).
- Why: the spec allows 50 a page; 10 keeps the batch at 40 statements, well inside 10 ms CPU and 50 subrequests (D417).
- Address impact: none.

### D608. "Live" and "active" are judged by one function shared with the vault's status read
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/vault/consent-store.ts` (`shareLive`, `consentActive`, used by `consentStatus` and `home/devices.ts`) · Carries out D534's condition on H9
- Decision: a device is a share that unlock would still accept: not revoked, before its idle limit, before min(its end, created + the app's session TTL now), the app still keeping logins, its origin still allowed. A consent is active when not revoked, before its end, and (in 'session' mode) its share is live: never `revoked_at` alone, so a 'session'-mode logout or new login, which leaves the consent's `revoked_at` NULL, reads as not active (tested).
- Address impact: none.

### D609. The three stops: the same 404 for "gone" and "not yours", conditional writes, and nothing waits on a pause
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/home/revoke.ts`
- Decision: `POST /v1/home/consents/revoke {consentId}`, `/shares/revoke {shareId}` (ids base64url, as the list gives them) and `/email-sharing/revoke {appId}`. Each loads the row by its id, resolves the root for the row's scope (D606) and acts only when the path hash or User ID matches; otherwise `404 unknown_consent` / `unknown_share` / `unknown_email_share` with the same body as an id that doesn't exist. The write repeats the match in its `WHERE`. A repeat answers `200 {revoked: false}` (email: `revoked: 0`). Signing a device out ends its share and its consents in one batch (`revoked_by = 'share'`, as D513 left for H9). Email: every address of the account for that app → `declined`, copies cleared, exactly the session-proof route's write; `404` when this account never decided anything there; `503 email_sharing_unavailable` without IDENTITY_SUB_KEY for a user the directory doesn't hold. No chain read, so all three work through a governance pause. 30/min per IP and per Home key, one window shared by the three.
- Residual: a found-but-not-yours id costs one more D1 read than an unknown one; ids are 128 random bits, so the timing difference can't be used to find one.
- Address impact: none.

### D610. "Last used" comes from the share's idle limit; no new column
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home/devices.ts` (`lastUsedAt`)
- Decision: an unlock or an approved signature's touch sets `idle_until` to that moment plus the app's idle limit, so the last use is `idle_until − idle_ttl_ms` (never before sign-in). Where the slide was cut short by the share's end, it can't be told and the page shows no "Last used". An auto-signature doesn't touch (D539), so it is the last time the user was there, not the last signature. A changed idle limit shifts the estimate until the next use.
- Options: (a) this, no migration; (b) migration 0020 adding `vault_shares.last_used_at`, written by every unlock and touch (exact; one more column in the hot path and a deploy order). **Recommendation: (a)**; (b) if exact times are wanted.
- Address impact: none.

### D611. The vault labels a device by browser and system family only
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/web/src/vault/device-label.ts`, `boot.ts`, `vault.ts`, `api.ts` · Carries out D98 item 10 and D512 (H5 left the label out)
- Decision: `POST /v1/vault/shares` carries `deviceLabel`: "{browser} on {system}" from the User-Agent every page already sends; browsers Edge, Opera, Samsung Internet, Firefox, Chrome, Safari; systems iOS, Android, ChromeOS, Windows, macOS, Linux; "Browser on {system}" or "{browser}" when one is unknown, no label when both are. Never a version, a device model, a language or a screen size. Stored with the share and deleted with it (D178).
- Options: (a) this; (b) User-Agent Client Hints (more precise, more bits); (c) no label. **Recommendation: (a)**: a handful of bits, not a fingerprint, and enough to tell "my phone" from "my laptop".
- Address impact: none.

### D612. The devices section reads only when the user asks
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/web/src/auth/home-devices.ts`, `home-page.ts` (two mount points and `leaveApp`)
- Decision: "Devices and auto-approve" sits on the front page (after "Your apps", the two the spec's lock-in stance names) and on each app's page above "Move this wallet to another wallet app". Each starts with "Show devices" and reads `GET /v1/home/devices` on that click; "Show again" re-reads; leaving an app's page closes its section. Nothing is fetched on its own, and an answer from before a new sign-in or a sign-out shows nothing (D553, D559).
- Options: (a) this; (b) read on opening an app's page automatically (one click less, one request per page view). **Recommendation: (a)** for now; (b) is a small change if wanted.
- Address impact: none.

### D613. `/home?view=devices` is the address the "Manage in Hana Home" links will use; nothing links to it yet
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-devices.ts` (`devicesLinked`)
- Decision: exactly `?view=devices` opens the devices section after sign-in, with one read and focus on its heading. It carries no `appId`, so it never names an app whose wallet the page would then refuse to move (D600). The plan's H9 scope lists the links, but its rule ("nothing ships half-wired"; `/home` is linked from nowhere until H12) and H12's scope ("link `/home` from the consent screen and the approval popup") put the links themselves in H12: H9 built only the address.
- Address impact: none.

### D614. Wording: what each stop does and doesn't do; the app's rule as the app's own words
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-devices.ts` (`HOME_STOP_CONFIRM`, `stopDoneText`), `home-problems.ts`, `home-api.ts` (`homePolicyLabel`)
- Amended 2026-11-10 by D662 and D663 (H9's security review): the sign-out wording now says whoever has the device can still approve and sign in a tab already open there for up to about a minute (an app with a policy) or about 10 minutes (other apps); "Last used" reads "Last opened or approved here"; a 'none'-mode consent reads "A tab (may be closed)".
- Amended 2026-11-10 (the user, on the screens): "Sign out this device?" shows two short lines, "Signs that device out of this app and stops automatic signing there." and "A tab already open there can keep working for a few minutes (up to about 10).", with the full detail behind a native "More" disclosure. The other two confirmations have three lines and stay as they are. Web addresses wrap only after `://` and before `.`, `:` and `/` (`dom.ts` `originText`), on Home and on the auth pages' "at https://…" lines.
- Decision (as first built): each stop asks first, in place of its button. "Sign out this device?": auto-signing stops within about 10 seconds; the app asks to sign in again the next time it's opened or reloaded there; a tab open there now can still ask for approvals until it next checks with Hana ("don't approve anything you didn't start"); signatures and transactions already made stay valid, and signing out doesn't move funds. "Stop auto-approving on this device?": stops within about 10 seconds, the device stays signed in, signatures already made stay valid. "Stop sharing your email with this app?": new sign-ins and the dashboard lose it at once, tokens already issued keep it up to an hour, a copy the app stored is the app's own. The policy's label shows as "The app describes what it may sign without asking as: “…”", only if display-safe and at most 80 characters, else "No description"; never a heading. The user sees their own shared addresses. Refusals: one sentence per code (`unknown_share`, `unknown_consent`, `unknown_email_share`, `email_sharing_unavailable`), with the code and request id.
- Address impact: none.

### D615. D442's partner requirement is removed; Hana Home's stop replaces it
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9` (`docs/integration.md`); **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Carries out D442's amendment
- Decision: `docs/integration.md` no longer requires an app with auto-approve and email sharing to offer a "Manage email sharing" control; it says users can stop sharing in Hana Home, and that a control calling `requestEmailSharing()` is still welcome.
- Gap: Hana Home reaches users only once it is deployed and linked (H12). Until then a user of an app whose signing is all auto-approved has only the partner's control. **Recommendation:** keep the removal (the plan asks for it in H9) and deploy H9 before any partner turns on email sharing with auto-approve; or keep the requirement until H12 if that can't be promised.
- **Amended 2026-11-10 (after H9's security review); confirmed by the user 2026-11-10:** the requirement stays. `docs/integration.md` keeps "Required if you use auto-approve" (the D442 amendment) until H12 has deployed Hana Home and linked it from Hana's own surfaces: users whose signing is all auto-approved never see Hana's popup, so until then they have no route to Home. H12 removes the requirement (recorded on H12 in `docs/hana-home-build-plan.md`). The H9 branch's removal was reverted.
- Address impact: none.

### D661. A member's account is confirmed on chain before Home shows its addresses or stops anything
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/home/root.ts` (`confirmMember`, `confirmedRoot`, `ownRoot`), `devices.ts` (`checkRoots`, `canStop`), `revoke.ts`, `directory/sync.ts` and `store.ts` (`markHintedMember`) · From H9's independent security review (medium) · Amends D606
- Problem: an unlink's background `syncAccount` that fails before `markRemovedMembers` leaves the removed login `active` in the directory indefinitely (a root's plain login never re-reads members; no cron). Through D606 that login could list the account's devices and plaintext shared addresses and sign the owner's devices out, repeatedly.
- Decision: (a) every stop whose root is another identity's (a member's account) first asks the chain (`get_identity`, one uncached view; it answers through a governance pause, so D609 holds): a confirmed member acts for the root; a contradiction acts for the identity's own rows (so another's id is a 404); no answer is `503 near_unavailable` with `retry-after: 2` and nothing written. (b) `GET /v1/home/devices` confirms its member-resolved scopes the same way, at most 10 reads a request, 5 at once, stopped after the first batch with a failure: a confirmed scope is shown in full; a contradicted one becomes the identity's own; an unconfirmed one lists its devices but with `canStop: false`, no stop on the page and no addresses (they aren't read). (c) `syncAccount` marks the member a relayed cancel or unlink named `cancelled` or `unlinked` even when `get_account` fails: the API relayed it, so it knows.
- Cost: one `get_identity` per member scope listed, and per stop by a member; worst case for the list 25 fetches (5 reads × NEAR_RPC and 3 fallbacks after 5 that succeeded), D665.
- Address impact: none.

### D662. "Sign out this device" ends an already-open tab at its next `GET /v1/app` read
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10**; option (b) taken for every app by D680 (2026-11-10) · Built: `apps/api/src/handlers.ts` (`share` on `GET /v1/app`), `vault/consent-store.ts` (`shareStatus`, `SHARE_HEADER`), `packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts` (`applyServedShare`), `api.ts`, `packages/core/src/api-types.ts` · From H9's independent security review (medium) · Amends D614's wording
- Problem: an open tab learned of a revoked share only at a touch (at most once per 10 minutes, after an approved signature), so whoever held the device could keep approving there; and the confirmation's "don't approve anything you didn't start" spoke to the wrong person (the Home user never sees that popup).
- Decision: the vault's existing `GET /v1/app` reads (no new polling) send `x-hana-share` (the session's share id, from `VAULT_ORIGIN` only) and get `share: 'live' | 'revoked'`. `'revoked'` (revoked, gone, the app no longer keeping logins, its origin removed) ends that session as a touch's 410 does: the record deleted, other tabs told, the session ended. Time-based ends (idle, absolute) are not reported: they stay the vault's own timers and the next unlock or touch (D55). The read only ever ends a session; it slides and extends nothing (D539), and a missing or odd value changes nothing. An app with an auto-approve policy reads every minute (`POLICY_REFRESH_MS`), so its open tab ends within about a minute; another app reads only before particular requests, so its tab ends at a touch (within about 10 minutes of use), a read, an unlock or a reload. The confirmation now says: "Whoever has that device can still approve and sign in a tab of the app that is already open there: for up to about a minute in an app that can sign some requests by itself, for up to about 10 minutes in other apps."
- Options: (a) this; (b) a periodic read in every app (ends every tab within a minute, one more request a minute per open tab). **Recommendation: (a)**, as the review asked for no new polling.
- Address impact: none.

### D663. "Last used" reads "Last opened or approved here", never later than now
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home/devices.ts` (`lastUsedAt`), `home-devices.ts` · From H9's review (low) · Amends D610
- Decision: the value is the last unlock or approved signature there; the page names it so and says requests the app signed by itself don't count. It is clamped to now (a lowered idle limit would put it in the future).
- Address impact: none.

### D664. Bounds never make the devices list say something false
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home/devices.ts`, `home-devices.ts` · From H9's review (lows 4–6) · Amends D607
- Decision: each device's consent is read with the device (joined by its share), so no other list's bound can hide it and show "Auto-approve is off". The apps read takes only apps the rows name (at most 100), and a device whose app wasn't read is shown, never dropped. Past 25 devices the page says "others are signed in too". Each app's origins are parsed once per request. A 'none'-mode consent reads "A tab (may be closed)": Hana can't tell whether that tab is still open.
- Address impact: none.

### D665. What one devices request costs, and the key index Home sees
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h9`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · From H9's review (low 6, note 7)
- Decision: D1 counts a `batch()` as one query against its per-invocation limit (50 on the free plan), whatever its statement count (Cloudflare's D1 limits page, read 2026-11-10). A list request makes at most 3 D1 queries (the roots, the batch, and a second batch only before migration 0014), 3 Durable Object calls (`homeGate`'s limiter and marker), at most 4 fetches for `get_config` when it isn't cached, and at most 25 fetches for the member checks (D661): 35 in the worst case, inside the free plan's 50 subrequests. A stop makes at most 3 D1 queries, 3 Durable Object calls and 4 fetches for one `get_identity`. Shares and consents at a key index other than 0 are invisible to Home: the vault opens only index 0 (`KEY_INDEX`), so none exist today; a future index would need Home to read its path too.
- Address impact: none.

## Hana Home H10: email users, and signing in through the exit client (branch `feat/hana-home-h10`), 2026-11-10

Built on `feat/hana-home-h10`, not merged, not deployed. Every decision here was **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (D616–D627, and D628, D629, D666–D669 from H10's security review). None changes a path, a key rule or derivation: an email user's Home path is `{scope}#email#{sub}#0` or its account root's, exactly as in the vault, and `aud` never enters a path.

### D616. The issuer's Home route computes every nonce from typed inputs, and its gate is the chain's alone
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h10`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/email-issuer/src/handlers.ts` (`handleHomeStart`, `homeAudience`, `homeVerified`, `mint`'s `TokenAudience`), `commitment.ts` (`homeCommitmentNonce`), `chain.ts` (`homeEmailExit`) · Meets H1's review condition (the plan's H10), D463, D474, D485, D490, D494
- Decision: `POST /v1/email/home/start` takes `{email, kind, commitment}` and nothing else (no publishable key, no nonce). `kind: 'identity'` commits to the Home key, its end (at most 20 minutes away) and salt, and the issuer computes `homeNonce`; `kind: 'derive'` commits to a session of one use, key index 0, ending within 20 minutes, and the issuer computes its session nonce. The shared `resend` and `verify` carry the challenge on. `mint()` takes a typed audience of exactly two forms, `email:{scope}` or `hana-home`, never one from a request. The gate reads only the chain (no app, no `IssuerRpc` read, D434): the identity needs `("email", "hana-home")` in force on the exit list; a derive gets `email:{scope}` while the scope holds its email client (the normal route, D490), else `hana-home` while the email exit is in force (D485), else `409 not_covered`. The audience is read again at `verify`.
- Why: a route that signed a caller's nonce would let an owner get a `hana-home` token carrying `client_proof_nonce` for their own mailbox and register the client on their scope; the Home and session nonces' domains differ from the client proof's, so no such token can exist (the contract's audience-shape rule refuses the client as well). A Home identity token can never open a session for the same reason (its domain differs from the session nonce's). Gating on the chain keeps a suspended or deleted app's users their route.
- Address impact: none. The token's `sub` is the address's own `HMAC(K_sub, address)`, the same as any email login's (a test holds it equal).
- Amended 2026-11-10 by H10's security review (confirmed by the user 2026-11-10): a `derive` code needs the address's own Hana Home sign-in (D629); the chain is read before a code is spent and again at `resend` (D668); the email exit reaches any registered scope, never-email ones included, and D544 is the stop (D667).

### D617. Hana Home's email codes draw on a share of their own: 10% of the daily send budget
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `limits.ts` `HOME_BUDGET_SHARE`, `handleHomeStart`
- Decision: every Home code mail goes through the mailbox, domain and IP limits as any login's, then the general pool within a share counted under `hana-home`: the flat share of an app with no usable plan (`BUDGET_APP_SHARE`, 10% of `dailySendBudget`). There is no partner quota (there is no partner).
- Options: (a) this; (b) no share of its own (Home could use up the general pool every app shares); (c) a larger share (Home is the rescue route; to revisit with real traffic).
- Why (a): Home can't empty any app's share, and no app can empty Home's.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (H10's security review, D628, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10): the 10% is split into 6% for anyone and 4% for returning mailboxes, with Home's own per-IP and per-prefix windows and the 50% alert.

### D618. Hana Home signs in through the shared client while one is in force, else through the exit client; an app's wallet through the exit client only where its coverage is `exit`
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts` (`homeGoogleRoute`), `home-export.ts` (`homeExportRoute`, `checkRoute`), core `hana:home-params` and `hana:home-derive-params` (`exit: true`), `login-page.ts` (`exitEntry`) · Settles D550's open point and D578's proposal; applies D490 and D491
- Decision: Home's own sign-in uses the first shared Google client in force and, only when there is none, the exit client (`exitGoogleClientId`), whose answer comes back through `/home/callback`. "Sign-in isn't available" now means neither Google client is in force and email sign-in is off. To open an app's wallet, a Google account uses the exit client only where the API reports coverage `exit` naming the exit client Home's settings name, and only after the page reads it in force on NEAR (listed, or pending and due); otherwise the move isn't offered ("Hana can't open this wallet from here").
- Why: the exit counter (D487) stays a signal of real exits; everyday sign-ins stay on the ordinary route.
- Address impact: none.
- Note, 2026-11-10 (H10's security review, D666, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10): D490's preference is the page's alone. The API admits an exit token wherever the contract does (D525, the user's choice on 2026-11-09, unchanged), so a user who drives the exit client by hand (their own token and session key, no page) opens exit sessions the page wouldn't, and raises the hourly exit counter (D487) doing so: the counter is a signal, not proof of a real exit.

### D619. Hana Home neither keeps nor sends a device ticket for email
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `handleHomeStart` (no owner claim), `homeVerified` (no ticket issued)
- Decision: the Home route takes no device ticket or unlock grant, and its `verify` issues none.
- Why: Home keeps nothing in storage (D553), and a ticket issued and thrown away would push one of the user's devices' tickets out of the mailbox's five.
- Cost (to weigh): during a code drain on the mailbox (someone using up its windows), the user can't sign in to Home by email until the windows reset; the login popup's owner path doesn't help Home. Option not built: read (never write) the auth origin's stored ticket for that address.

### D620. Home's code mails name Hana Home and the action, never an app
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `mail.ts` (`purposeText` for `home` and `home_session`)
- Decision: "Your sign-in code for Hana Home" ("sign in to Hana Home"), and "Your code to open a wallet in Hana Home" ("open one of your wallets in Hana Home, where its private key can be shown to move it to another wallet app", and "Never give this code to anyone: it opens your wallet"). No app is named.
- Why: the issuer reads no app for Home (D616), and a name the page sent would let anyone put words in a Hana mail. The design's "name the action and the app" is met for the action only.

### D621. A Home code writes no user-directory row and seals no address
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `homeVerified`
- Decision: `verify` of a Home challenge answers `{idToken}` only: no `sealedEmail`, no case B, no `user_emails` row. The issuance row and the daily counts name `hana-home`.
- Why: a Home sign-in is no app's login; the directory rows are per app (D269) and email sharing is per app (D438).

### D622. Email sign-in runs on `/home` itself, not in a `/login/email` child; `/home`'s policy gains the issuer
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-email.ts`, `home-page.ts`, `pages.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/host.ts` · Deviates from the plan's "the `/login/email` mode for Home"; amends D551 and D583
- Decision: the address and code screens are part of `/home` (and of its "Move this wallet" section); the page calls the issuer directly. `/home`'s `connect-src` is the export window's list plus the issuer's origin, in an env with one.
- Why: a child window and the login relay exist for Google, which must answer a redirect URI; Hana Home is already on the auth origin, so a `/login/email` child would add a window, a message channel and a relay slot for nothing. The address and code still go to the issuer only (D230).
- Options: the `/login/email` mode the plan named (more moving parts, the same security, Home's CSP unchanged).
- Amended 2026-11-10 (D669, confirmed by the user 2026-11-10): a malformed `EMAIL_ISSUER_URL` no longer takes `/home` down.

### D623. An email account's address stays in Home's memory for its sign-in; later codes go to it without asking again
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts` (`emailAddress`), `home-export.ts` (`startEmailCode`)
- Decision: after an email sign-in the page keeps the address (memory only, dropped on sign-out or another account); "Sign in again" and the per-app code send to it with one button and no field. "Use a different email" is offered only on the first sign-in.
- Why: the per-app code must come from the same mailbox (the API also requires the same `sub`); asking again would only add a way to get it wrong.
- Note 2026-11-10 (D678): the header now shows this address ("Signed in as …").

### D624. What `/home/callback` accepts
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-callback-page.ts`, `callback-page.ts`, `login-storage.ts` (`exit`), `google.ts` (`HOME_CALLBACK_PATH`) · For D491
- Decision: the page clears the fragment first; relays only for a `state` whose entry the Home child stored for the exit client (with the client and the nonce), only an ID token whose unverified `aud` and `nonce` are those (anything else is relayed as `invalid_response`, a claim outside the allow-list as `token_has_pii`), Google's errors as they are; it refuses a framed window and one whose opener is another site's or another Hana page (a missing opener is accepted: Google's pages may cut it). `/login/callback` refuses an exit entry. Its policy is `connect-src {apiUrl}` and no logo.

### D625. `GET /v1/home/config` says whether email sign-in is open
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/home/config.ts`
- Decision: `emailSignIn` is true only with an email issuer in the env and `("email", "hana-home")` in force on the exit list (the rule `homeGate` applies). The page offers "Continue with email" only then; an older API reads as off.

### D626. H8's "can't move this wallet yet" is gone
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-export.ts` (`HOME_EXPORT_OFF_TEXT`, `homeExportRoute`) · Amends D578, D584
- Decision: coverage `exit` opens through the exit client (a Google account) or a code (an email account); coverage `email` through a code. Where neither applies the section says "Hana can't open this wallet from here. If the app still runs, use the app itself." For an email account the section's button reads "Continue with a code", its step "Get a code to open this wallet".

### D627. Wording of the sign-in for two methods
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `home-page.ts`, `home-email.ts`
- Decision: "Continue with Google" and "Continue with email"; "Sign in with the Google account or the email you use in those apps"; "Signed in with email"; sentences that named "this Google account" name "this email address" for an email account. The code screens reuse the login popup's sentences ("Check your email", "Too many attempts. Try again later.", "That code is wrong. N tries left.", …) with "Type it here, on this Hana page only".
- Amended 2026-11-10 (the user, after reviewing H10's screens): the first screen no longer says "15 minutes", which was false for email (D629's note: an email sign-in ends with its 10-minute token). It says "You stay signed in for a short time, and not after you close or reload this page." The warning two minutes before and the end use the sign-in's real end, the token's expiry where it comes first (`endsAtMs`), for both methods.

### D628. Hana Home's mail can't be used up by fresh addresses: its own IP windows, a reserve for returning mailboxes, an alert at half
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built on `feat/hana-home-h10`; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/email-issuer/src/limits.ts` (`IP_HOME_START_LIMITS`, `IP_AGGREGATE_HOME_LIMITS`, `HOME_BUDGET_SHARE`, `HOME_RESERVE_SHARE`, `RETURNING_MAILBOX_MS`), `handlers.ts` (`homeBudget`, `homeAggregateLimits`), `rate-limiter.ts` (`noteVerified`, `returning`) · From H10's security review (Medium) · Amends D617
- Problem: `home/start` needs no sign-in, each start can name a fresh address, and Home's mail is one share for every user: a few IPs could use it up and leave every user's email sign-in to Home answering 429 until the UTC day ends.
- Decision, numbers proposed:
  - (a) Home's own windows on top of `start`'s: per IP subject 3 per 10 minutes and 10 a day (dev envs 10 and 60); per aggregate prefix (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /56 and /48) 50 a day.
  - (b) Home's share of the general pool is split: 6% of `dailySendBudget` for anyone, and 4% that only a **returning mailbox** may draw on once the 6% is gone: one whose code was verified (any app's login or Home's) within 30 days. The mailbox's own limiter object (keyed by the existing `mailboxKey`) keeps the time of its last verified code and nothing else; no address is stored.
  - (c) Reaching half of either part raises the existing `email_budget` alert (`app_50`, app `hana-home` or `hana-home-returning`): a count in `email_daily` and at most one mail a day to the security alias, no address in it. A part running out raises `send_budget_exhausted` the same way. No new cron.
- What it costs a genuine first-time Home user (an address that has never verified a code): during a flood they share the 6% with the flood and may get "Too many attempts. Try again later." until the UTC day ends; behind a NAT or a campus /24, 10 Home starts a day per IP and 50 per prefix are shared with everyone there. A user who signed in to any app with that email in the last 30 days still gets a code from the 4%. A catch-all domain's owner can make returning mailboxes, but each needs a code from the 6% first and counts in the recipient domain's cap.
- Not built (an option): a challenge before `home/start` such as Cloudflare Turnstile. It would stop scripted floods at the source, but needs a site key and a secret on the issuer, a script from `challenges.cloudflare.com` in `/home`'s policy (a third party on the page that shows private keys), and a widget step for every user; free tier on Cloudflare. Not recommended before real traffic shows the windows aren't enough.

### D629. A `derive` code needs the address's own Hana Home sign-in
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `handlers.ts` (`homeIdentityHolds`), `home-email.ts`, `home-export.ts`, `home-api.ts` (`token`) · From H10's security review (Low 2) · Amends D616
- Decision: `kind: 'derive'` must carry `identity`, a live Hana Home identity token this issuer minted: its JWS verifies with a published key, `iss` the issuer's, audience `hana-home`, not expired (60 s of skew, as the API), its issuance row's purpose `home` (a derive's `hana-home` token or a scope's token is refused), and `sub` the address's own. Otherwise `401 home_identity_invalid`, nothing mailed. `kind: 'identity'` takes no `identity`. The page sends its sign-in's token; on `home_identity_invalid` it ends Hana Home's sign-in and says so.
- Why: without it anyone could mail "open one of your wallets… its private key can be shown" to any address.
- Note: an email identity token lives 10 minutes (the issuer's token lifetime), while Hana Home's sign-in lasts 15: an email user's sign-in effectively ends after about 11 minutes, at the API as here.

### D666. D490's "exit only where the normal route is gone" is the page's choice; the exit counter can be raised by hand
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: documented; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · From H10's security review (Low 3) · Notes D618; D525 unchanged
- Decision: no API change: the API keeps admitting exit tokens wherever the contract accepts them (D525, the user's decision of 2026-11-09). `docs/security.md` and D618 say that D490's preference holds in the page only, and that someone driving the exit client by hand can raise the hourly exit counter (D487).

### D667. The email exit reaches any registered scope; D544 is the stop
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: documented; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · From H10's security review (Low 4) · Notes D485, D616
- Decision: documented, not checked at the issuer: the issuer reads no `get_identity` for a `derive` today, and checking `opened` there would add a chain view to every per-app code. `POST /v1/home/login` already refuses an identity that never opened a wallet in the scope (D544, before anything is counted or relayed), where links are open.

### D668. A Home code's route is read before the code is spent, and again before a resend
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `handlers.ts` (`handleVerify`, `handleResend`), `challenge.ts` (`peek` with `purpose` and `scopeId`) · From H10's security review (Low 5) · Amends D616
- Decision: `verify` reads the Home route from the chain before comparing the code, so a refusal or a chain that can't be read never burns the single-use code (the token is minted on that reading); `resend` reads it first and mails nothing once the exit is removed or the scope is gone.

### D669. A malformed `EMAIL_ISSUER_URL` serves `/home` without the issuer's origin
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/pages/host.ts` · From H10's security review (Low 6) · Amends D622
- Decision: the auth Worker serves `/home` with the policy minus the issuer's origin (never a looser one) instead of a 503; Google sign-in works, and the email sign-in, whose request the policy blocks, says the service can't be reached. The page can't learn the Worker's settings, so it doesn't hide the email button: the build's own `emailIssuerUrl` and the API's `emailSignIn` decide that. `/login/email` still answers 503.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (the user): `GET /v1/home/config` answers `emailSignIn: false` when the API's own `EMAIL_ISSUER_URL` (from the same manifest value) isn't an http(s) URL, so the page doesn't offer email then.

## Designed HTML emails (branch `feat/html-emails`), 2026-11-10

### D670. User mail and the partner invite get a designed HTML part from one shared layout; the text part stays
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **asked for by the user 2026-11-10** ("a much better layout/design… something like HTML based email", after receiving Hana Home's sign-in code); the layout, colours and wording below decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (after reviewing the screenshots) · Built: `packages/brand/src/email.ts` (`@hana-id/brand/email`: `mailHtml`, `mailText`, `mailUrlProblem`, `MAIL_COLOURS`), `apps/email-issuer/src/mail.ts` (`mailEnvNotice`), `labels.ts`, `env.ts`, `scripts/gen-wrangler.ts`; tests `apps/email-issuer/test/mail-html.test.ts`, `packages/brand/test/email.test.ts` · Amends D419's "Not the email issuer"
- Decision:
  - **One layout, one place:** `@hana-id/brand/email`, a string template (no rendering library, no runtime dependency; about 8 KB a mail, far under Gmail's 102 KB clip). The issuer and the admin Worker import it; the mail texts stay in their Workers.
  - **Every mail stays `multipart/alternative`** (it already was: the HTML part was a few bare paragraphs): the text part unchanged word for word; the HTML part says the same sentences in the same order (a test checks every text line is in the HTML), plus a heading (the subject) and a small footer ("Sent automatically by Hana ID.").
  - **Built for mail clients:** tables and inline styles, at most 560 px, the system font stack, a text wordmark ("Hana ID") and Hana's gradient as a 4 px rule, no image, script, form, style sheet or remote resource, so the mail is the same with images blocked; one `<style>` in the head only adds the dark colours, a narrow-screen padding and neutral styling for links a client invents. `lang="en"`, `color-scheme` and `supported-color-schemes` metas; every text/surface pair AA in both schemes (a test).
  - **The code:** large, monospaced, letter-spaced, one text node with no space or cell between digits (a double-click or long press takes all six), `user-select: all`, the expiry under it; the anti-phishing sentence in a callout with the auth host as text, each dot in its own element so clients don't link it; "if you didn't…" as a normal paragraph.
  - **Applied to:** every code mail (each purpose: app login, the link flows, Hana Home's sign-in and "move a wallet" codes), the issuer's link notice, unlock and confirm mails (D675), and the partner invite (D672). Not to the operational mails (D674).
  - **The env banner:** on testnet the HTML part opens with D419's sentence ("[SANDBOX] Not production: this email is from Hana ID sandbox-dev (testnet), for testing."). The issuer gets `ENV_LABEL` and `NEAR_NETWORK` from `gen` and shows it only for a known label with `testnet`. Subjects and the text part stay as D419 left them for user mail (the sender's name says "(testnet)").
  - **Unchanged:** the sender, every subject, SendGrid's settings (click, open and subscription tracking off for every message, `@hana-id/sendgrid`), SPF and DKIM.
- Security: every string is escaped in the layout, which also drops control, bidi and invisible characters, and refuses a button URL that isn't https (http only on a loopback host) and a code that isn't 4–12 digits or capitals; app names still pass `displayAppName` first; Hana Home's mails name no app (D620). Tests use hostile names (tags, quotes, `javascript:` URLs, bidi and invisible characters, CR/LF, over-long names).
- Deliverability notes: the HTML part is small and text-heavy with one link at most; the hidden preview line and its padding (D671) are common practice but are hidden text, which some filters weigh slightly; the first sends after deploy are worth watching in SendGrid's stats.
- Not verified: real mail clients (Gmail web and apps, Apple Mail, Outlook). The screenshots are a browser's rendering, with dark mode simulated two ways (the media query, and an inversion filter for Gmail-style forced dark).
- Amended 2026-11-10 (the security review, D687, D688; the user's D685): the heading, the title and the preview line are fixed words per purpose, never the app's name; the app's name is written as unlinked text; the logo is a hosted image (D685), so "no image" now reads "one image, the logo"; text is stripped by the display-safety rule's classes (D688).
- Address impact: none.

### D671. The code is not in the preview line
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10**
- Decision: the hidden preview line (preheader) says what the code is for and that it expires ("Your code to sign in to Hana Home. It expires in 10 minutes."), never the code, and is padded so a client doesn't fill the rest of the preview from the body (where the code is). The subject already never holds it (Q8).
- Why: the preview shows on lock screens and in notification banners to anyone near the phone; the plain mail used to put the code in that preview (its first lines). Keeping it out matches the subject rule.
- Cost: a user can't read the code off a notification; they open the mail (iOS and macOS can still offer the code from the mail's body for AutoFill).
- Option: put the code in the preview (faster, as many services do); recommended against.
- Amended 2026-11-10 (the security review, Low 3): this is **best effort**. What it covers: clients that build the preview from the HTML part and show up to about 300 characters (the preheader, padded with about 300 invisible characters since this amendment, up from 120), which is Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook's usual preview. What it doesn't: a client that previews the text part (it opens "Your code to … :" and then the code, on purpose: the text part stays as users know it), a client that shows a longer preview than the padding, and a notification that shows the body. The subject never holds the code in any client.

### D672. The partner invite: designed, one button and its URL as text, who invited and what accepting does
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **asked for by the user 2026-11-10** (the invite is a partner's first contact with Hana); the wording **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/admin/src/email/messages.ts` `inviteLink`, `render.ts` (`design`); tests `apps/admin/test/email.test.ts`
- Decision: the invite's HTML part is the shared layout (D670): heading "You're invited to {org} on Hana ID", one "Accept the invitation" button and the same URL as unlinked text (the only `href`), D419's banner on testnet, the security footer. Both parts gain three sentences: who invited, by role only ("by Hana staff" or "by an owner of the organisation": no member id or staff address, which would be new disclosure), what accepting does (a new organisation: created with you as its first owner; an owner invite: owners change apps, keys and members, and with an existing owner you are a viewer until a waiting period ends, which its owners can cancel; a viewer: sees and changes nothing), and "The link works once, for this address only." The preview line names the organisation and the expiry, never the link.

### D673. No hosted logo in mail; the wordmark is text (superseded by D685)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10**, then **superseded the same day by D685** (the user chose a hosted logo with the wordmark as its fallback)
- Decision: no image in any mail: "Hana ID" as styled text.
- Why: a remote image is a request at open time, the shape of a tracking pixel (it tells the host when and roughly where a mail was opened); many clients block remote images by default (the logo would show as a broken box or alt text), and Gmail proxies them. An inline (`cid:`) or `data:` image adds size and is unevenly supported. SVG isn't supported in most clients.
- Option (if the user wants the mark): a 2x PNG of the mark hosted on a Hana origin with no cookies and no logging of requests (e.g. the files Worker), with `alt="Hana"`, width and height set, and a test that it's the only remote resource. Trade-off: brand recognition and a little phishing resistance against an open-time request per mail and a broken image where blocked.

### D674. Operational mails keep their plain form (a follow-up)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10**
- Decision: the admin Worker's change notices (guarded changes, owner grants, login methods), digests, on-chain watcher mails, ledger and settlement alerts, statement notices, retention and directory alerts; the issuer's own alert mails (`daily.ts`); and the watchdog's alerts (text only) stay as they are.
- Why: an alert must reach and read in any client, including terminals, forwarding rules and paging bridges; their content is key-value tables, lists and JSON (a policy up to 20 KB) that the plain HTML already shows faithfully; a staff alert gains nothing from branding. The partner-facing change notices are the best candidates: `render(..., design)` already maps every block kind (a warning to a callout, a link to a button with the URL as text), so moving one is a one-line change plus its snapshot.
- Follow-up: decide per mail after reviewing the invite in real clients; the watchdog's mail would need an HTML part first.
- Amended by D700 (2026-11-11, asked for by the user): the security notices partners receive get the designed layout.

### D675. The issuer's link notice, unlock and confirm mails get the layout, their link as one button
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10**
- Decision: these user mails already carried one link (to `authOrigin`); in the layout it is a button ("Open the cancel page", "Open the sign-in link", "Receive codes again") with the URL again as text. Code mails still have none.

### D679. Showing a Google account's address in Home's header (proposed, not built)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** as recommended: **not built** for now · Would amend D25 (as amended by D119 and D270) for Hana Home, and D551 if the read goes to another origin
- Today: Hana Home's Google sign-in (`/login?mode=home`, and `/home/callback` for the exit client) asks Google for `response_type=id_token`, `scope=openid` only. The token carries no `email` claim by design, and the claim allow-list (D271) and Home's verifier (D473) refuse one that does (`token_has_pii`): the page never learns the address, so it can't show it.
- What it would take: D270's pattern on Home's child: first a Google access token with `scope=openid email` (Google's sign-in screen then also asks to "see your primary email address" for the shared or exit client), read once in the page from Google's userinfo endpoint (`https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo`, a new `connect-src` for `/home`; `www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo` is already in it), kept in memory like an email account's address, and the access token dropped; then the silent `prompt=none` openid-only ID-token request as today, so the token Hana's API and the chain see stays exactly as now. One more Google round trip and one more screen element on every Google sign-in to Home.
- Trade-off: the user sees which Google account they used (useful with several), but Google's screen adds an email permission to Hana Home's sign-in, the address enters a page that shows private keys (only in memory, never sent to Hana), the consent screen's scopes change for the shared and exit clients (their OAuth verification and Testing-mode lists), and the step that can fail (`prompt=none` after the access token) is one more place a sign-in can break. Recommendation: not now; reconsider if users report signing in with the wrong Google account.
- Address impact: none (the ID token, its `sub` and every path are unchanged).

### D685. The designed mails show Hana's logo, hosted on the env's files origin, with "Hana ID" as its fallback
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-10** ("yes, add a hosted logo image to the designed emails, with the wordmark as its fallback"), reversing D673; the mechanics below built on the user's instructions · Built: `packages/brand/scripts/mail-logo.ts` (draws `mail/hana-mail-logo.png` and `src/mail-logo.ts` from `logo/`), `packages/brand/src/email.ts` (`header`, `mailLogoUrl`), `apps/files/src/index.ts`, `rules.ts` (`MAIL_LOGO_HEADERS`), `apps/files/scripts/gen-wrangler.ts`, `apps/email-issuer/src/mail.ts` (`mailLook`), `env.ts`, `scripts/gen-wrangler.ts` (`FILES_ORIGIN`), `apps/admin/src/email/` (`filesOrigin`); tests `apps/files/test/files.test.ts`, `packages/brand/test/email.test.ts`, `apps/email-issuer/test/mail-html.test.ts`, `apps/admin/test/email.test.ts` · Supersedes D673
- Decision:
  - **The image:** Hana's mark and wordmark (the auth pages' bar, from `packages/brand/logo/`) on a white rounded plate, so it reads on light, dark and inverted backgrounds; a 240 × 80 PNG (about 4 KB) shown at 120 × 40 with `width` and `height` set. `alt="Hana ID"`, styled on the `<img>` as the text wordmark was (font, size, weight, colour), so a client that blocks images shows "Hana ID" as before and no broken-image box. Without a files origin, or with a URL that isn't https (http only on a loopback host), the header is the text wordmark. One function draws the header (`header` in `email.ts`).
  - **Where:** the env's files Worker (`files.origin`, the origin of app logos), at `/brand/hana-mail-logo-<first 16 hex of its sha256>.png`: the bytes are built into the Worker (no R2), so the path changes with the image. Headers: `image/png`, `nosniff`, a `sandbox` CSP, `cross-origin-resource-policy: cross-origin` (mail clients' image proxies may fetch it), inline disposition, `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `no-referrer`; no cookie. Only `GET` and `HEAD` on the files origin.
  - **Not a tracker:** the URL is the same for every recipient and every mail (no query, no token; a query string is ignored); the Worker writes no log line for it, and the files Worker's platform invocation logs are now off (`logs.invocation_logs: false`), so no IP, user agent or URL is kept. What an open can reveal: Cloudflare's own edge sees the request like any request (its usual analytics, counts only in the dashboard, nothing per recipient that Hana can read); clients that proxy images (Gmail, Apple Mail Privacy Protection, Outlook) fetch it from their proxy, often once per message or ahead of opening, and many cache it for a year. Hana can't tell which mail, or which address, was opened.
  - **Only in the designed mails** (the issuer's user mail and the partner invite); code mails still have no link.
  - **The URL comes from the manifest** (`files.origin`, through `FILES_ORIGIN`): a different env or the move to company domains changes it in one place. Mails already delivered keep the old URL and show their "Hana ID" fallback once the old origin stops answering, as do mails sent before a logo change (only the current hash is served).
- Deploy order: the files Worker first (it must serve the path before any mail names it), then `gen` and deploy the email issuer and the admin Worker.
- Address impact: none.

### D686. An app's name may not look like a web address or contain "Hana"
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: from the security review (Medium, item 1), **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/console-core/src/names.ts` (`appNameProblem`, `normalisePartnerAppName`, `nameSkeleton`, `hanaWordIn`, `looksLikeAddress`), `apps/api/src/changes/settings.ts` (`appName`: create and every rename, from staff's "Create an app" and the partner console's Branding tab alike), `scripts/lib/admin-sql.ts` (`assertAppName`, the CLI), `apps/email-issuer/src/mail.ts` (`displayAppName`); tests `packages/console-core/test/names.test.ts`, `apps/email-issuer/test/mail-html.test.ts`
- The rule, in plain words: an app's name is refused when (1) it contains "://", or "www." at the start of a word, or a dot (also a full-width or ideographic one) between a letter or digit and a letter, as in "example.com" or "Sign in at evil.example"; or (2) one of its words starts with "Hana", in any case, with accents, in full-width or styled letters, with look-alike letters from other alphabets (Cyrillic а, А, Н, н, һ; Greek α, Α, Η, Ν, η; Armenian հ, ո, ռ; Latin ɑ; "@" and "4" for a; Cyrillic п for n), or with its letters split by spaces or punctuation ("H a n a", "H.A.N.A"). "Hana" inside a word ("Johana", "Ethan Apps") is allowed; a word that merely starts with it ("Hanami") is refused.
- Why: an app's name appears in Hana's own mails and pages beside Hana's words. "Hana Home" made an app's code mail read like Hana Home's own, and a name like "evil.com" can be turned into a link by Gmail or Outlook right above the code, in a mail that must carry none.
- Confirmed 2026-11-10 as proposed, the strict form: "Hanami" and other words starting with "Hana" are refused. A genuine case is an exception Hana grants by hand, and **today that needs a code change**: there is no staff override in the API, the console or the CLI (each applies `appNameProblem`); the change would be an allow-list of exact names in `packages/console-core/src/names.ts`, reviewed like any rule change, and the mail check (`displayAppName`) reads the same rule, so an allowed name would show in mails too.
- What it misses: look-alikes outside that table (Unicode's full confusables list is not in the repo; adding it is the stronger option), other brands' names, and words like "Hanna" that read close to Hana. Org names keep their old rule (they are set by Hana staff), but the designed invite writes them as unlinked text.
- Existing names: an app whose stored name breaks the rule keeps working; the API refuses only a new name or a rename. Mails apply the rule again (`displayAppName`), so such an app's code mail says "an app" and its subject names no app, as for any name that isn't display-safe; the auth pages still show the stored name until it is changed. The fixtures and seeds (`Smoke A`, `Smoke B (shared only)`, `Sodax Demo`, `Test Wallet`, `Email Home App`, …) pass.
- Address impact: none (names don't enter any path).
