## Sign-out reach: every app's vault checks its share each minute (branch `feat/signout-reach`), 2026-11-10

Built on `feat/signout-reach` (from `develop` 0882d71b), not merged, not deployed. D680 was **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10**;
after the branch's independent security review (no Critical or High) the user confirmed D681 and D683 as built, amended D682
(a 3-minute grace) and had D684's idle slow-down built (2026-11-10). D690–D694 are the review's fixes, built as asked, with the
choices made inside them **proposed, awaiting the user's confirmation**. No path, key rule or derivation changes; no migration,
secret or cron. The API gains `POST /v1/vault/share-status` and two Rate Limiting bindings (D690): the API deploys first (D693).

### D680. Every app's vault makes the one-minute check, so a sign-out from Hana Home reaches any open tab within about a minute
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts` (`armStatusRead`, `statusRead`, `checkShare`, `statusReadWanted`, `applyServedShare`, `STATUS_READ_MS`), `boot.ts` (visibility), `packages/web/src/auth/home-devices.ts` (the wording) · Amends D465 ("no new polling": this is a new periodic read for apps with no policy), D662 (its option (b), now taken for every app) and D614's wording
- Problem, verified live by the user on sandbox-dev: "Sign out this device" revoked the share at once, but in an app with no auto-approve policy the open tab learned of it only at a touch (at most every 10 minutes, after an approved signature) or a reload; the user signed a personal message there after signing the device out.
- Decision: the vault asks about its share about once a minute while a session with a share is live in that tab, in every app (every 5 minutes once the tab is idle, D684), and ends the session on `'revoked'` exactly as before (record deleted, other tabs told, nothing left in memory, `disconnect` 4900). In an app with a policy it is the policy's existing minute read, `GET /v1/app` with `x-hana-share` (one request a minute, never two); in other apps the light `POST /v1/vault/share-status` (D690). Any other read made in the minute counts, so the timer waits out the rest of the minute. Nothing is read while logged out, while dormant (D112), past the session's limits, or for a session with no share. The read only ever ends a session: it counts as no activity for the idle limit and slides nothing (D55, D539).
- Hana Home's confirmation says "A tab already open there can keep signing for up to about a minute."; under "More" "…for up to about a minute, or for up to about 3 minutes while that device can't reach Hana." (D682) and "A tab nobody is using may still look signed in for a few minutes, but it can't sign anything." (D684, D681); after the stop, "a tab already open there can't sign after about a minute".
- `'none'` mode: a session with no share has no row Hana Home lists as a device, so there is no "Sign out this device" for it and nothing to check; its consent can still be stopped from Home (D465, within 10 s). Unchanged.
- Address impact: none.

### D681. A hidden tab pauses the share check and checks at once when shown again
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (as built) · Built: `onVisibilityChange`, `statusReadWanted`, `VaultHost.visibility`
- Decision: the share check runs only while the tab is shown (`document.visibilityState`, which a frame takes from its tab). Hidden: no share reads. Shown again (a page restored from the back/forward cache included): one read at once if the interval has passed since the last answer, else the timer goes on; being shown counts as activity (D694). A policy app's background read keeps running while hidden, as before, at the idle pace once nothing happens (D684).
- Why: a hidden tab can't start an approval (the launcher or the partner's button needs a click in the shown tab), browsers throttle hidden timers anyway, and D682 and D692 check before every approval signature and cached identity token, so "about a minute for a tab someone is using" holds at no cost for hidden tabs.
- Residual: after a sign-out, a hidden tab keeps the key in memory and reports `logged_in` until it is shown, its idle limit, a reload or its next signature or identity-token request (which end it); it can complete no signature and hand out no cached token meanwhile.
- Amended 2026-11-10 after the re-review (Low 6): a `pageshow` with `persisted` (a back/forward-cache restore) is handled as the tab being shown, beside `visibilitychange`.

### D682. An approval-popup signature needs a fresh `'live'` answer, with a 3-minute grace when the API can't answer
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10, amended: the grace is 3 minutes** (built with 10, changed the same day) · Built: `confirmHolder`, `shareConfirmed`, `sign()`, `SHARE_FRESH_MS`, `SHARE_GRACE_MS`, `SHARE_WAIT_MS`
- Decision: before the approval popup, and again after Approve, a session with a share needs the API to have said "live" within 60 s (its create, an unlock, a touch, or a share read); older, it checks first (the light read, then `GET /v1/app`, waited for at most 8 s), and `'revoked'` ends the session (4900, no popup, nothing signed). With no answer (a failure, a 429 or 5xx, a timeout, a missing `share`), the signature still completes when the last "live" is under 3 minutes old; past that it is refused with `api_unavailable`, `data.reason: 'share_unconfirmed'`, before any popup, the session stays, and signing resumes with the API's next answer. Both ages are taken on the larger of the corrected clock and a monotonic one (a device clock set back or a device that slept doesn't stretch them). Auto-signing is unchanged: it already needs an `'active'` consent answer within 10 s, which a revoked share fails.
- Trade-off: an outage longer than 3 minutes blocks approval signatures in tabs already open; in such an outage new sign-ins and reloads already fail. Someone holding the device who blocks Hana's API gets at most 3 minutes after the last "live" answer. The review's correction: before this branch a blocked API meant signing without limit (a touch's and the policy read's failures were ignored), so the grace is a strict improvement.
- Address impact: none.
- Amended 2026-11-10 after the re-review (Low 4): a share's create and an unlock count as "live" from when they were sent, as every other answer does, so a slow answer leaves less of the minute and the grace, never more.

### D683. Failed reads back off to 8 minutes; a failed or slow read neither ends nor extends a session
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** (as built) · Built: `statusInterval`, `statusFailures`, `STATUS_READ_BACKOFF_MAX_MS`, `STATUS_READ_MIN_MS`
- Decision: after each background check that gets no answer, the interval doubles: 1, 2, 4, 8 minutes, then 8 (never shorter than the idle pace, D684); any answer to any read resets it. One check at a time: a slow one is waited for, never stacked. A failure, a 429, a missing `share` field or another value ends nothing and changes no time. The timer never re-arms for less than 10 s.
- Amended 2026-11-10 after the re-review (Low 1, an availability bug): `GET /v1/app` and the light read are aborted after 15 s (`STATUS_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`, on the vault's own timers, and they settle at that deadline even if a fetch ignores the abort), so a fetch that never settles can't hold the one check in flight, and with it every later check, the background timer and, after the grace, every signature, until a reload. The check in flight is per share: a new session never joins the previous session's check. Other vault fetches still have no timeout of their own (the login relays, `createShare`, `unlock`, `touch`, `revoke`, `revoke-all`, the consent and identity-token calls, the email-sharing calls, the mainnet-demo event, `relayWrite`); none is on the share check's path (a touch is fire-and-forget).

### D684. What the check costs; an idle tab checks every 5 minutes
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10: build the idle slow-down** · Built: `statusIdle`, `noteStatusActivity`, `STATUS_IDLE_AFTER_MS`, `STATUS_IDLE_READ_MS` · Measured: `apps/api/test/home-devices.test.ts` "one minute read costs…", "share-status: no chain call…"
- Decision: after 5 minutes with no activity in a tab (D694), the background check runs every 5 minutes instead of every minute; any activity brings the minute back at once. The checks before a signature and a cached identity token (D682, D692) are unchanged, so a sign-out is still caught when it matters: an idle tab may look signed in for up to about 5 minutes but can't sign or hand out a token meanwhile.
- Requests per open tab with a live session, per hour: before this branch, 0 in an app with no policy (a touch, at most 6 an hour, only while approving) and 60 in an app with a policy. Now: an active shown tab 60 (light reads, or the policy's `GET /v1/app`); an idle one 12; a hidden one 0 with no policy, and a policy app's hidden tab 60 while active, 12 idle. A tab stops reading at its idle limit (2 h by default), when it goes dormant.
- Against the Workers free plan's 100 000 requests a day (account-wide, every Worker; past it requests fail), tabs shown around the clock: 50 active make 72 000 (72%), 50 idle 14 400 (14%); 500 active make 720 000 (7.2 times the limit), 500 idle 144 000 (1.4 times). Shown 8 hours a day, a third of that. On Workers Paid the cost is small: 500 active tabs around the clock are about 22 million requests a month, a few dollars beyond the included 10 million.
- Per light read (D690): 1 D1 statement and 2 rows read once the app is in the isolate's 30-second cache (a miss adds the app's 2 statements), no Durable Object request (its limits are Rate Limiting bindings), no chain call; 50 active tabs around the clock read about 0.14 million rows a day of the free 5 million (3%), 500 about 1.4 million (29%). A policy app's `GET /v1/app` stays as measured before: 8 statements, 14 rows, one Durable Object request (the per-IP limiter).
- CPU: GET /v1/app's own computing measured about 0.03 ms in Node; the light read does less (one JSON body, one statement). Estimated well under 1 ms of the 10 ms limit; not measured on Workers (check Workers Observability after the deploy).

### D690. A light, vault-only share-status endpoint, limited per share
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built from the security review's Medium 1 and 2 (asked for by the user 2026-11-10); the auth and limit choices **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `apps/api/src/vault/share-status.ts`, `vault/limits.ts` (`VAULT_STATUS_IP_LIMIT` 600, `VAULT_STATUS_SHARE_LIMIT` 30 a minute, namespaces `95005`, `95006`), `packages/web/src/vault/api.ts` (`shareStatus`), `vault.ts` (`checkShare`)
- Problem: `GET /v1/app` shares the per-IP config window (20 a minute on the free plan), so about 20 shown tabs behind one IP (or a neighbour there) got 429s and, after the grace, every approval failed; and it carries `share` only on a 200, so a NEAR outage (502), a settings failure or a misconfiguration (409) dropped the answer, although Stellar and EVM signing need no NEAR.
- Decision: `POST /v1/vault/share-status` `{shareId}` answers `{share: 'live' | 'revoked', serverTimeMs}`, `no-store`: the vault gate (vault origin, an allowed parent, the app from the isolate cache), a per-IP ceiling high enough for a NAT, then a per-share window, then one D1 statement (`shareStatus`). No chain call, no app quota, no usage event; it reads and slides nothing. Every refusal (429, 503, 4xx) is no answer to the vault, never `revoked`.
- Authentication: the share id alone (128 random bits that only the vault, the API and the account's own Hana Home hold), for a one-bit answer about that share. A session proof was rejected: it would cost a signature check on every read and prove nothing more (without a counter it replays; with one it is a D1 write).
- Policy apps: the policy's minute read keeps carrying the share, and the light read is only its fallback when that read gives no answer; a separate light read beside the policy read would be two requests a minute. The checks before a signature or a cached token use the light read first, `GET /v1/app` as the fallback.
- Amended 2026-11-10 after the re-review (its Lows 2, 3 and 7): the per-IP ceiling names no app (one ceiling per IP subject across apps) and is asked before the app lookup, so one IP causes at most about 600 D1 statements a minute per Cloudflare location (up to 1 800 with made-up keys); a neighbour behind the same IP and location can use it up, as with the unlock's per-IP window, which is no answer, never a sign-out. The caller's `x-hana-parent-origin` is no longer checked here: the answer depends only on the share's own recorded origin, so a tab on an origin the partner removed reads `revoked` and ends (it got a 403 before, a no-answer, and could sign for the 3-minute grace), and the header can't make it answer about another origin. The Origin check binds browsers only; the share id is the secret.

### D691. A check that got no answer is reused for 5 seconds
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built from the review's Low 2 (asked for by the user 2026-11-10) · Built: `SHARE_NO_ANSWER_REUSE_MS`, `shareNoAnswer`
- Decision: while reads fail, sign requests in a row within 5 s of a check that got no answer reuse it (the grace decides) instead of each sending a new one.

### D692. A cached identity token is handed out only after the same share check (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built from the review's Low 3; **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `checkedCachedIdentity`
- Decision: `hana_identityToken` answers from its cache only after D682's check (a `'live'` answer within a minute, else a check, else the 3-minute grace, else `share_unconfirmed`); `'revoked'` ends the session and the answer is nulls, as logged out. A dormant session is checked with the light read, which never unlocks it (D112). A mint needs no check (the API checks the share).
- Why: the token is a server-verifiable sign-in a partner's backend trusts for up to an hour; a hidden tab signed out from Home kept serving it. Cost: at most one light read a minute per tab, only when the page asks for a token.
- Limit: a token already handed out, or pushed to the page by `identityTokenChanged`, stays valid until it expires (as before).

### D693. The API deploys before the vault; a vault ahead of it degrades to the old read
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: built from the review's Low 4 (asked for by the user 2026-11-10) · Built: `checkShare` (`shareStatusMissing`), `docs/operations.md`
- Decision: deploy the API (the endpoint and its bindings) before the vault. A vault ahead of it gets a 404 `not_found` (or, in a browser, a failed preflight): never `revoked`; it falls back to `GET /v1/app` for the share, which every deployed API answers since H9, and after a readable 404 uses only that.
- Amended 2026-11-10 after the re-review (Low 5): a real older API answers the unknown route without CORS headers, so a browser sees a failed preflight, not the 404. When the light read fails as a network error and `GET /v1/app` then answers, or the 404 is readable, the vault uses `GET /v1/app` alone for 30 minutes (`SHARE_STATUS_REPROBE_MS`), then tries the light read again; a network error with `GET /v1/app` failing too (offline) isn't remembered. The fake API in the vault tests fails the preflight the same way.

### D694. What counts as activity for the check's pace (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-10 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-10** · Built: `noteStatusActivity`
- Decision: activity is any request from the partner page on the port (reads such as `hana_status` included), any `hana:` message from a Hana window on the auth origin (the approval, consent, login, export and sharing popups: a person at work), and the tab being shown. It only sets the pace of the background check; it never extends a session (the idle limit counts key requests only, D55).
- Abuse: a hostile page can keep the pace at a minute by asking anything (costing requests, gaining nothing) or stay silent to slow it to 5 minutes, which doesn't help it: it can't get a signature or a cached token without D682's fresh answer.

## A sign-out tells the page so (branch `fix/signed-out-reason`), 2026-11-11

Built on `fix/signed-out-reason` (from `develop` 0867313a), not merged, not deployed. Found in live testing on sandbox-dev:
a device signed out from Hana Home while its demo tab was open; the next approved signature there was refused (as it
should be) but the demo said "The connection to the Hana vault was lost. Reload the page.", which is wrong: the vault was
fine and only a new login was needed. A page could not tell a sign-out from a lost vault (both a bare 4900). No path, key
rule or derivation changes; no API, migration, secret or cron change.

### D695. A session ended because its share was revoked tells the page so: `disconnect` and the refused request carry `reason: 'signed_out'` (code stays 4900) (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built: `packages/core/src/protocol.ts` (`disconnectReason`, `DISCONNECT_REASONS`, the `signedOut` broadcast), `packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts` (`shareRevokedRefusal`, `sessionEnded`, `announceEnd`, `endSession`'s `reason`, `broadcastRevoked`'s `signedOut`), `packages/web/src/client/client.ts` (`HanaDisconnect`), `apps/demo/src/errors.ts`, `page.ts` · Extends D680, D682, D692
- Decision: when the API says a session's share was revoked (a status read's `'revoked'`, from the minute's check or the one before a signature or a cached identity token; `410 share_revoked`, or `410 session_ended` with reason `share_revoked`, on a touch, `revoke-all` or a consent register), when a newer login on this device replaces it, and when another tab says so, the session ends as before and the page is told: the vault sends `disconnectReason {reason: 'signed_out'}` just before `disconnect {code: 4900}`, the SDK passes `reason: 'signed_out'` on the page's `disconnect`, and every request the session refuses then (a signature waiting for approval or after it, a consent screen, an export waiting for its window) gets 4900 with `data.reason: 'signed_out'`. An identity mint refused with `share_revoked` keeps its `session_ended` and `sessionExpired` and adds `data.reason: 'signed_out'`.
- Not on a guess: every other end says nothing more. This tab's own logout (no `disconnect` at all, as before; its waiting requests get a plain 4900), another tab's logout (a `disconnect` with no reason: a page may want its own wording later), expiry and the idle limit (`sessionExpired`), a share the API reports expired or unknown (`410 share_expired`, `404 unknown_share`), a mint refused for any other reason, a dormant session whose unlock fails (`sessionExpired`, as before: the unlock's answer isn't read), a record that fails to open, and a lost vault connection (the SDK's own 4900).
- Compatibility: `disconnect` keeps exactly `{code}` on the port, which shipped SDKs (0.2.0, 0.3.0) validate strictly: a field there would make them drop the whole event. A new event is dropped harmlessly by them, as with `launcherKind` (D572), so no version gate and no SDK version bump. A vault older than this sends no `disconnectReason`, and the SDK sends no `reason`. The SDK keeps a reason only for the event right after it; a lost connection never has one. The refused request's `data.reason` reaches every SDK release (error `data` is free-form). EIP-1193 is unchanged: a session's end is `accountsChanged []`, and the provider's own `disconnect` (4900, the vault connection) has no reason; wagmi, viem and ethers see the same codes.
- Other tabs: a tab that ends a share because it was revoked broadcasts `signedOut {shareId}` just before `revoked {shareId}`. A tab of this build ends on `signedOut` with the reason, and the `revoked` after it finds nothing left to end; a tab of an older build ignores `signedOut` and ends on `revoked`, as before (so a deploy never leaves a tab running on a revoked share). An expired or unknown share is broadcast as `revoked` alone.
- `signed_out` means "Hana revoked this device's session", which the API's `'revoked'` doesn't break down further: Hana Home's "Sign out this device", `revokeOtherDevices()` on another device of the same user (`revokeAllFrom` revokes every other live share of the app and path), a newer login of the app in another tab of this device, or the partner's settings (persistence turned off, the origin removed). A sign-in on another device does not sign this one out. The demo says "You were signed out on this device (from Hana Home, another tab or another device). Log in again." as a notice, never the reload text, and the refused signature that arrives in the same moment shows the same notice instead of overwriting it; a 4900 without the reason keeps "The connection to the Hana vault was lost. Reload the page.".
- Exposure: the reason is one bit about this app's own share on this device, which the page could mostly infer already (a `disconnect` while its vault answers and `hana.status` is `'logged_out'`); it says nothing about which device or page revoked it, or about other apps.
- Rejected: a field on `disconnect` behind an SDK version gate (needs a version bump and still leaves 0.3.0 pages without it; the separate event costs nothing); a new error code (wagmi, viem and ethers key on 4900); a `reason` on the `revoked` broadcast (older tabs validate it exactly and would ignore the revocation); telling the page "signed out" for every 4900 or every share end (a guess for expiries and lost vaults).
## Admin pending invites, the onboarding dry run's fixes, the one-partner gate on testnet (branch `feat/admin-pending-invites`), 2026-11-11

### D696. Staff see invites to new organisations on the Organisations page
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: proposed 2026-11-11, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built on `feat/admin-pending-invites` (not merged, not deployed): `StaffRpc.newOrgInvites` (`apps/console/src/invites.ts` `newOrgInvites`), the admin's `GET /api/invites/new-orgs`, `apps/admin/public/app.js` `pendingInvitesPanel`; `docs/operations.md` "Onboarding a partner on testnet" step 1
- Problem: an invite from "Invite a new partner" has no organisation until its first owner accepts (`invites.org_id` NULL), so after the one-off "Invite sent…" message nothing showed it: staff couldn't see who was invited, whether the email had gone out, when it expires, or revoke it without the API (found in an onboarding dry run, 2026-11-11).
- Decision: a staff-only read, `StaffRpc.newOrgInvites({limit ≤ 100})` (Hana actor only; not audited, as `getOrg` and the other staff reads), answers the invites with `org_id` NULL that are open, or ended (accepted, else revoked, else expired: that time) less than 30 days ago (`NEW_ORG_INVITES_WINDOW_MS`, inside the 90 days the cron keeps ended invites), open ones first, then newest first, with `truncated` when more matched. The admin BFF serves it as `GET /api/invites/new-orgs` (behind the same Access and staff-list check as every route; nothing in the URL); the Organisations page shows it as "Pending invites" above the list whenever there is a row, re-read with the page (so it appears at once after sending), with the state in words (Waiting for the email to go out, Email sent, waiting for them to accept, Accepted, Revoked, Expired) and Revoke (the existing route) on open rows. The invite view gains an optional `newOrgKind` (`partner` | `internal`, from `invites.new_org_kind`) on new-org invites: additive, so older readers ignore it. No migration: the list uses the existing `invites_org_open` index's leading `org_id`.
- Rejected: a separate page (the Organisations page is where staff start onboarding and where the organisation appears once accepted); listing every ended invite (unbounded; 30 days covers a dry run's follow-up and the 7-day expiry); auditing the read (no staff read of org data is audited; the invitee's address is shown only to staff, never logged).
- Not done: an accepted row doesn't link to the organisation it created (the invite row keeps `org_id` NULL and nothing ties the two without reading the audit log, which has no index on `target`); the organisation is in the list below.

### D697. Times in email sentences read as dates; tables keep the ISO time (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built on `feat/admin-pending-invites` (not merged, not deployed): `apps/admin/src/email/render.ts` `readableTime`, `messages.ts` `inviteLink`, `ledger-messages.ts` `retentionFailed`
- Problem: the partner invite said "The invitation expires on 2026-11-18T04:54:59.777Z" (found in the onboarding dry run, 2026-11-11).
- Decision: a time inside a sentence is written for a person, in UTC to the minute: "18 November 2026, 04:54 UTC". Today that is the invite's expiry (its body and preview line) and the retention job's "was due at" (staff). Times in tables (`kv` rows) and in digest lists stay the exact ISO time (`isoTime`), in partner and staff mails alike: they are copied into tickets and compared with logs and the audit view, which use it.
- Rejected: a reader's local time zone (an email has no reliable one; staff and partners work across zones, and the admin console shows UTC too); changing the tables as well (wider diff for no reader's gain; ISO there is what support compares).
- Amended the same day by D699 and D700 (asked for by the user): in the designed security notices partners receive, table times read in words too (the pending change's "Proposed at", the invite notice's "Invited at" and "Expires", the owner grant's "Requested at", the login-methods notice's "Changed at", the on-chain proposal's "Can execute from"). Staff mails and the digests keep ISO.
- Also from the same dry run, on the same branch (UI copy and behaviour, no decision of their own): the admin's "Create an app" redraws the Apps table in place and keeps the publishable key on screen; the organisation page's Invites panel offers Revoke on open invites only; `passkeys_required` names D242's one-partner gate ("Only one partner organisation for now") instead of asking for a passkey that can't be added.

### D698. The one-partner gate is lifted on testnet only; it stays on mainnet (amends D242)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** ("yes lift the limit on testnet only. Rule stays on mainnet.") · Built on `feat/admin-pending-invites` (not merged, not deployed): `apps/console/src/config.ts` `onePartnerGate`, `apps/console/src/invites.ts` `issueInvite` and `whyNotIssued`
- Problem: D242's gate (no second `partner` org, counting open new-partner invites, while `PASSKEYS_SHIPPED` is false) stopped a second external partner from being onboarded on testnet, where partners are to test end to end now and mainnet is months away.
- Decision: the gate applies while passkeys haven't shipped on every network **but testnet**. The network is the env manifest's `network` (`envs/<env>.json`; the schema allows only `testnet` today), written into the console's config by `gen` as `NETWORK` (`apps/console/scripts/gen-wrangler.ts`), the same var and the same exact comparison as the API's mainnet-demo rule (`mainnetDemoEnv`, D428). It fails closed: `NETWORK` missing, empty or anything but exactly `testnet` (`Testnet`, `testnet `, `mainnet`) keeps the gate. On a gated network nothing changed: the check is still inside the invite's insert batch, so concurrent issues can't race past it. On testnet a refused new-partner invite is never answered `passkeys_required`. No manifest schema change: the field and the var existed.
- Where it is enforced (checked 2026-11-11): at issue (`issueInvite`: staff's `StaffRpc.issueInvite`, and an owner's `member.invite`, which can't create an org) and, after the branch's review, at acceptance (`acceptInvite`): on a gated network the acceptance batch's commit row also requires that no partner org other than `org_legacy` exists for a new-partner-org invite, so open partner invites collected while `NETWORK` was `testnet` and later accepted under a non-testnet config add at most one partner org; a refused one writes nothing, leaves the invite open and ends the sign-in with `passkeys_required` ("This invite would create a second partner organisation, which Hana can’t allow here until passkeys are available. Contact Hana."). Nothing else creates an org (the migration's `org_legacy` only) or changes an org's kind; moving a legacy scope (`assignScopeOrg`) creates none.
- Why: partners test end to end on testnet first; their console accounts there rely on Google sign-in alone (no second factor), and every wallet holds test funds only, so a hijacked partner console account on testnet costs no real money. On mainnet the reason for D34's deferral stands: passkeys (or an explicit new decision) before a second partner (`docs/mainnet-readiness.md` 7.8).
- Rejected: flipping `PASSKEYS_SHIPPED` (it would lift the gate on mainnet too); a separate opt-out var (a var someone could set by mistake on mainnet; `NETWORK` comes from the manifest's network, which a mainnet env can't declare as testnet without its whole config being testnet's); deciding by env name (`isDevEnv`: would keep the gate on a testnet staging env, where partners test too).

## The console's app page after a partner dry run (branch `fix/console-getting-started`), 2026-11-11

Built on `fix/console-getting-started` (from `develop` 670ad2d8), not merged, not deployed. Found in a live dry run of
onboarding a new partner on sandbox-dev: a staff-created test app's first origin (`http://localhost:5173`, the
`no_session` waiver) was in force from its announcement (13:05) and sign-in from it worked, but 20 minutes later the
app page still listed it under "Changes waiting" with Cancel and every timeline step reached, while "Getting started"
said "1 origin is active"; the client snippet asked for an environment name a new partner can't know; the Audit page
showed epoch times, `null` fields and raw JSON. No path, key rule or derivation changes; no migration, secret or cron
change.

### D701. An app's read reports a guarded change in force as `active`; the console never offers Cancel on it (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built: `apps/api/src/changes/views.ts` (`changeView(r, now)`), `apps/api/src/changes/apps.ts`
  (`COUNTS`, `detailView`), `apps/console/web/src/pages/app/Changes.tsx` (`isWaiting`), `pages/Apps.tsx`
  (`nextEffectAt`, `useReloadAtNextEffect`), `pages/app/Overview.tsx`, `pages/app/Signing.tsx`
- Cause: a change is in force by the API's own predicate once `active_from <= now` (cas.ts `IN_FORCE`: the gate, the
  preflight, Cancel's refusal, removals), but its stored `status` stays `pending` until the hourly job (the API's cron
  run at :00, `guarded/cron.ts`) records it `active` and writes `<kind>.activated`. `getApp` and `listApps` answered the
  stored status, so for up to an hour a change already in force read as waiting: the console listed it with Cancel (which
  the API refuses, `not_pending` "already in force: remove it instead"), and the apps list counted it as waiting. Nothing
  was stuck: the next hourly run records it.
- Decision: `getApp` (ConsoleRpc and AdminRpc) answers a pending change whose `active_from` has passed as `active`
  (`changeView` with `now`), and `listApps`' `pendingChanges` counts only changes not yet in force (cas.ts `NOT_YET`).
  The stored row and the hourly job are unchanged (it still records the activation and the ledger row, so the Audit page
  shows `origin.activated` after the next :00 run). A write's answer (cancel, ack, expedite) still carries the stored
  status. The SPA judges "waiting" against the server's clock, not the reader's: the console's app read answers `now`,
  the SPA keeps the offset to its own clock and judges `isWaiting` (pending and not announced, or announced with its
  time ahead), the timeline's steps and the re-read timer by it, so a laptop running fast never hides a Cancel the
  server would still accept, and a page read before the time never shows a change in force as waiting. While the page
  is open, one timer to the next effective time (plus 1 s) re-reads the app once; the answer sets the next timer, if
  any. Of two `policy_set` changes in force before the hourly job (after a waiver or an expedite), the read shows only
  the latest by `active_from` as `active` and the older as `ended`, as the job will record.
- Rejected: running the guarded job every 15 minutes (shortens the window, doesn't close it); polling the app page.

should the words fail, the row's JSON stands in (and unreadable details read "(details unreadable)" in both parts), so no row can stop a digest. **Titles and details come from one place**, `@hana-id/console-core` `audit-words.ts`, which the console's Audit page now imports too (through the subpath `@hana-id/console-core/audit-words`, so the SPA bundles only these functions): `actionLabel` (a title from `ACTION_TITLES`, else the code's words, so an unknown code is never hidden), `securityEventLabel`, `keyLabel`, `detailValue` and `detailFields` (the caller passes its time form: the browser's local time on the console, UTC words in mail). **Every code has a past-tense title** in `ACTION_TITLES` (68 codes): every `app_changes.kind` the API writes (`APP_CHANGE_KINDS` in console-core; the API's `CommitRow.kind` and the cron's ledger rows are typed by it, so a new kind can't be written without being listed, and a console-core test wants a title for each), every console audit action (`AUDIT_DETAIL_KEYS`; a console test wants a title for each), and the admin SPA's `LOG_KIND` kinds (that SPA has no build step and keeps a copy; `test-spa/log-kind.test.ts` holds each of its words equal to the shared ones; it now says "Change announced by email" and "Scope moved to this organisation" as the console and the mail do). Writing the list found two kinds no title or list knew: `mainnet_demo.on` and `mainnet_demo.off`. The console's Audit page reads every code the new way too. The titles: `app.created` "App created"; `app.deleted` "App deleted"; `app.renamed` "App renamed"; `app.logo_set` "App logo set"; `app.logo_removed` "App logo removed"; `app.settings_changed` "Settings changed"; `app.turned_off` "App setting turned off"; `app.suspended` "App suspended"; `app.resumed` "Suspension lifted"; `settings.changed` "Settings changed"; `email.off` "Email login turned off"; `suspension.set` "App suspended"; `change.proposed` "Change proposed"; `change.announced` "Change announced by email"; `change.cancelled` "Change cancelled"; `change.expedited` "Change put in force early"; `change.link_cancel` "Change cancelled from an emailed link"; `origin.proposed` "Origin proposed"; `origin.activated` "Origin in force"; `origin.removed` "Origin removed"; `origins.removed` "Origins removed"; `policy.proposed` "Policy proposed"; `policy.activated` "Policy in force"; `policy.ended` "Policy ended"; `policy.pending_dropped` "Waiting policy dropped"; `policy.removed` "Policy removed"; `raw_sign.proposed` "Raw signing proposed"; `raw_sign.activated` "Raw signing in force"; `raw_sign.off` "Raw signing turned off"; `key.created` "Key created"; `key.revoked` "Key revoked"; `key.rotated` "Key rotated"; `org.security_contacts` "Security contacts replaced"; `org.policy` "Organisation policy changed"; `org.frozen` "Organisation frozen"; `org.unfrozen` "Organisation unfrozen"; `scope.assigned` "Scope moved to this organisation"; `migration.baseline` "Migration baseline recorded"; `owner_action.relayed` "On-chain owner action sent"; `owner_action.executed` "On-chain owner action executed"; `invite.issued` "Invite sent"; `invite.revoked` "Invite revoked"; `invite.notified` "Invite notice emailed"; `invite.expired` "Invite expired"; `invite.accepted` "Invite accepted"; `owner_grant.created` "Owner rights requested"; `owner_grant.notified` "Owner rights notice emailed"; `owner_grant.cancelled` "Owner rights request cancelled"; `member.added` "Member added"; `member.role` "Member role changed"; `member.removed` "Member removed"; `member.owner_granted` "Member became an owner"; `user.disabled` "User disabled"; `user.enabled` "User enabled"; `session.signed_in` "Signed in"; `session.signed_out` "Signed out"; `signin.refused` "Sign-in refused"; `step_up.failed` "Fresh sign-in failed"; `statement.issued` "Statement issued"; `ledger.exported` "Ledger exported"; `rate.overridden` "Rate overridden"; `support.lookup` "Support ID looked up"; `users.find` "Wallet directory searched". The security kinds: `drift` "App setting in force without a notice", `breaker` "Too many destructive changes in an hour", `owner_cap` "On-chain owner action limit reached", `owner_allowance_low` "Owner action allowance running low", `home_budget_high` "Hana Home daily budget running high". **The text part is unchanged**: each row one line with the codes, the ISO time and the JSON. How a row reads is three small functions in `messages.ts` (`changeRow`, `auditLogRow`, `eventRow`).
- **The row count is said** before and after the rows, in both parts: the intro ("4 changes were made to the apps of org_….", "4 console events: members, invites and organisation settings changed in org_…:", "The API recorded these 3 security events:", singular forms for one) and a line after the rows, "End of the 4 rows." The security digest's last line, which named an internal file (`docs/playbooks.md`, also a host name a text client may link), now reads "Hana security receives every security event too and has a recovery playbook for each kind. To ask about one, reply to this email or write to your Hana contact.": it goes to the org's contacts and the alias (the alias alone for an event with no org), and suits both.
- **Row times:** the text part keeps the exact ISO time (`2026-11-11T05:01:36.861Z`), as D697 and D700 said for digests: it is what support copies into tickets and compares with the API's rows and the logs. The HTML part reads it in words as the notices do ("11 November 2026, 05:01 UTC", seconds dropped), with the plain-word rows chosen by the user; a time inside the details too (one that isn't a valid time there shows its raw number). Amends D697's rule for digest lists, for the HTML part only.
- **A row whose time isn't a valid one** (NaN, past the Date range; `ms` is any non-negative safe integer, up to about 9.007e15 against the Date limit of 8.64e15) no longer makes the render throw. It is shown raw and flagged ("not a valid time: 8700000000000000") in both parts, the rest of the row and the other rows as usual, and the admin logs `digest_bad_time` at error level (keys `level`, `at`, `event`, `step` (the source), `orgId` when there is one, `count`; never the value), as loud as the throw it replaces, which the feed step logged as an error every run. Not added: a count in the feed step's own log line (the digests are built inside `feed.ts`'s generic walk, which knows only sent or not; it would need the walk's plumbing changed). Why not fail closed as the notices do (D700's amendment): a digest is after the fact and blocks nothing, but a throw stops its whole source: the `app_changes` and `audit_log` cursors never pass that row and the security events (the first 50 unnotified, re-read each run) are never marked, so every later row for every organisation would go unmailed. Skipping the row was rejected too: the row would never be mailed at all and only the log would show it. The blocking notices still refuse a bad time (`readableTime`).
- **Size and completeness: the HTML part has a budget, `DIGEST_HTML_BUDGET` = 90 000 bytes as rendered.** The `entries` block sets the font and colours once per row (under 1 KB of markup a row besides its text), but a row's text can cost far more than its length in HTML: the unlinked form writes each `.`, `/`, `#`, `?`, `=` as 19 bytes and the escaping writes each `"` as 5 (`&#34;`, and JSON doubles them as `\"`), in the details (400 characters) and in any value of up to 500 (an audit target such as a partner-chosen invitee address, an actor or scope id). Before the budget, 50 such rows measured up to about 1.3 MB (targets), 420 KB (details of dots) and 107 KB (details of quotes, with no delimiter), past Gmail's 102 KB clip, which hides the rest of a mail without saying what: a member who can write those values could pad rows so the row that matters lands past it. Now the HTML part holds as many rows as fit (oldest first; a binary search over the rows shown, a handful of renders), then "{M} more rows are not shown here: see the plain-text part of this email or the console's Audit page." (for security events: "… or ask Hana security (reply to this email)."), no link; the text part always holds every row. Measured with the plain-word rows (the code line and the details in words; the code and detail lines are not monospaced, which keeps the markup small): a few rows 10.7–11.6 KB; 50 ordinary rows with details at the cap and URLs in them 82.4–89.1 KB, all shown; 50 rows of details of dots 82.7 KB (9 shown, 41 left out); of quotes 87.5 KB (29 shown); audit rows with 490-character delimiter-heavy targets 87.2 KB (6 shown). Tests pin each of these under the budget with the note and the end line.
- **Cuts are well-formed** (`cut` in `render.ts`): the details' 400-character cut, `oneLine`'s and the notices' JSON cuts drop a surrogate pair they would split (and any lone surrogate), so neither part ever holds half an emoji, which a strict provider could refuse (and a refused digest holds its cursor). Text the cut doesn't split comes out as before.
- Unchanged: purposes and message keys (`feed:app_changes:…`, `feed:audit_log:…`, `feed:security_events:…`), recipients (contacts, old and new contacts on a contacts change, the alias for events, the alias when an org has none), the suppression rule (the audit digest is routine and keeps SendGrid's lists; the others bypass them, D401 as amended), subjects, the batching, cursors, budget and marking in `feed.ts`.
- Still plain: the statement notice (`statementIssued`: to the contacts, the billing address and the alias; one table and no rows, it would convert with the notices' `notice` design alone, left for the user to decide) and the staff alerts (D700's list).
- Not covered: the text part (a plain-text client may still link an origin or URL in a details value, D687); not tried in real mail clients (browser screenshots, light and dark, a phone width).
- Address impact: none.

## Auto-approved Sodax swaps: deferred, with what it would take (no branch, no code), 2026-11-11

### D708. Auto-approving Sodax swaps is not built now; revisit once there is a commercial agreement with Sodax to build on
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-11** (leave it for now, and note what implementing auto-approved swaps would take so it is remembered; it will likely be needed later, once there is a commercial agreement with Sodax to build on; the current demo is enough for now); reworded 2026-11-13 before the repository went public (the user's request); the decision is unchanged · Built: nothing · Relates to D428, D429, D476, D492 and the auto-approve policy rules (`docs/integration.md` section 9)
- Decision: the Sodax demo keeps the approval popup on every swap. Auto-approve stays as it is: testnet contract calls a policy names (`apps/smoke/policies/demo-auto-approve.json` is the worked example). An auto-approve step on a testnet call in the sample app was offered and not taken up.
- What is in the way today (checked in code on 2026-11-11):
  1. A mainnet demo request is never auto-approved: `packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts` `sign` (`eligible = !demo && …`). The real-funds banner lives in the approval popup.
  2. No policy can cover a Sodax swap, on any network: calls whose instructions travel in opaque bytes (routers, multicall, bridges, Sodax's `AssetManager.transfer` and `sendMessage`) always get the popup until a protocol decoder ships (integration guide section 9, "Not covered in the pilot"). The mainnet demo already decodes Sodax calls to bind delivery to the user's own wallets (D476, D492), but that decoder is not wired into policy matching.
  3. A policy caps native value and fees, not token amounts; `limits.perDayCount` (1 to 500 per user per UTC day, per device) is the only brake on token moves.
  4. Nothing was found that checks a swap's minimum output against a fair price (no such check by name in `packages/web`, `packages/core`, `packages/sodax`; to confirm when this is picked up). The page writes that number, so without the popup a script could set it near zero and a filler could keep the difference: a loss that looks like slippage even though the output goes to the user's own wallet.
- What building it would take: (a) a new decision amending D428/D429's "always the popup" for the mainnet demo, or doing it for a live app instead; (b) a Sodax decoder in policy matching, so a policy can say "swaps and their deposits and approvals, delivered to the user's own wallets" and the vault checks each request; (c) a fair-price bound on the minimum output, from the live prices the demo already reads (D436), e.g. within 1 to 2 percent; (d) a per-day count as the ceiling on repeats. With (b) to (d), the worst daily loss per user is about count × (fee + allowed slippage × the per-transaction cap): 20 a day at 1 percent of 9.99 USD is about 3 USD, so no separate dollar budget is needed (the user's point: with delivery bound to the user's own wallets, a swap can only lose fees and slippage, once slippage is bounded); (e) the consent screen saying plainly that it covers real funds, with the limits and how to stop it, and a notice on each auto-signed swap, since the popup's banner is no longer seen; (f) the policy set on the app as a guarded change; (g) the sample site's switch, status and stop; (h) tests, docs and a security review. Size: large, mostly (b) and (c).
- Why deferred: it helps only the swap demo, not a partner integrating or testing on testnet (the current priority), and the current demo is enough for now; it is revisited once there is a commercial agreement with Sodax to build on.
- Address impact: none.

## A Google account's address changes: two open items (no branch, no code), 2026-11-11

### D709. A new Google address can't sign in by email while the account already has an email member (open)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **open**, logged at the user's request; nothing decided · Built: nothing · Relates to
  D119, D122, D139, D199
- The case: a user's Google identity G is the account root and an old address E1 is already its email member. The
  user changes the Google account's address to E2 and logs in with Google, so the issuer records a hint `G ↔ E2`. An
  email login with E2 then finds the hint: G has the wallet and E2 has none (case B), but the account already has a
  sign-in method of the email kind (one per provider, `links.rs`), so the join isn't linkable
  (`apps/email-issuer/src/decide.ts` `linkable`). `verify` returns `googleWallet: true` with no `idToken` and no
  `linkTicket` (`apps/email-issuer/src/handlers.ts`, the case B lookup), and the popup shows only "This email belongs
  to a wallet you created by signing in with Google. Continue with Google to open it." (`packages/web/src/auth/email-page.ts`).
- Effect: E2 can't sign in by email in that scope until E1 is unlinked and E2 linked (explicit link, 24 h), and
  nothing tells the user why or how. E1 keeps working while the user still reads that mailbox (a changed Gmail address
  stays as an alternate).
- To decide: the popup's wording for this case (say an older email is already linked, point to unlink and link);
  whether Hana Home or the partner's UI should offer "replace the email sign-in" in one step; whether anything should
  change on the server. Any change to who can join or when needs a security review (it is the email issuer's power
  over Google wallets, D119).
- Address impact: none.

### D710. An email login with a changed address before the next Google login makes a second wallet (open)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **open**, logged at the user's request; nothing decided · Built: nothing · Relates to
  D122 ("no case D"), D132, `docs/email-login-spec.md` "The four cases"
- The case: a user changes the Google account's address to E2 and, before any Google login records a hint for E2,
  signs in by email with E2. No hint exists, so E2 is case C and opens its own wallet as a root. At the next Google
  login both identities have a wallet (`both_wallets`): nothing links or merges them (the contract refuses `Both
  sign-in methods already have a wallet`), and each method keeps opening its own wallet. This is the known way to end
  up with two wallets in one scope (the spec's "address changes between logins").
- Effect: the user may fund the wrong wallet or think funds are missing, and no screen tells them a second wallet
  exists or which method opens which.
- To decide: whether to tell the user (a notice at the Google login when google-match answers `both_wallets`, or in
  Hana Home's app list); whether to offer a way to move funds from one to the other (through Home's export or a send),
  never a merge of two funded wallets (rejected in D122); whether the issuer could catch it earlier (it only learns
  Google's current address at a Google login).
- Address impact: none.

## Tests that don't depend on the clock or on another checkout (branch `test/flaky-pass-1111`), 2026-11-11

### D712. Each linked worktree gets its own e2e ports; window tests start inside their window
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: decided while building (the user asked for the flaky-test pass on 2026-11-11: "yes start 1, 2 and the flaky test pass in parallel"), **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built: `apps/e2e/src/checkout-port.ts`, `ports.ts`, `port-env.ts`; `apps/api/test/helpers.ts` (`startOfMinuteClock`, `minuteStartFor`, `minuteHeadroom`), `apps/console/test/helpers.ts` (`minuteHeadroom`), `apps/email-issuer/test/helpers.ts`; `packages/web/scripts/gen-envs.ts` (`writeAtomically`); tests only otherwise
- Decision: with CI off (D387), `pnpm verify` on one machine is the gate, often from several worktrees at once. (1) The e2e stack's port base: the main checkout keeps 4410; a linked git worktree takes 4510 to 48910 in steps of 100 from a hash of its path; `HANA_E2E_PORT_BASE` still overrides. Two worktrees that draw the same base (about 1 in 440) are refused by the existing fingerprint check. (2) A test of a per-minute, per-hour or per-day limit starts its clock just inside a window (or waits for headroom where the counter runs on the real clock in another isolate), instead of hoping no boundary passes. (3) A wait for something to happen waits for that thing, not for a fixed real time. (4) `envs.generated.ts` is written atomically and only when it changes, since four packages generate it in one run.
- Left as they are, listed in the branch's report: the console tests' real-time waits for the API's token buckets, exact read counts after 25 ms in `share-check.test.ts`, `vi.waitFor`'s 1 s default around WebCrypto, day and month keys compared across isolates at UTC midnight.
- No production code path changes behaviour. Address impact: none.

## Partner console: the way back from a fresh sign-in, the Email login tab's live state (branch `fix/console-email-login-flow`), 2026-11-11

### D711. A fresh sign-in returns to the page that started it, a page from an allowlist built server-side (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** (asked for by the user: the two Email login traps of the partner guide fixed in
  the product; where actions return to, and how, decided while building, to confirm) · Built:
  `apps/console/src/actions.ts` (`RETURN_PAGES`, `returnPath`, `defaultReturn`), `web/src/api.ts` (`ReturnTo`),
  `web/src/lib.tsx` (`useStepUp(org, from)`), `web/src/pages/Action.tsx` (`safeReturn`), each page's `useStepUp`
- Cause: the action page's back link was guessed in the SPA from the action's kind (an `app.settings` went to Login &
  sessions, an `owner_action` to the scope's page), and only for a member of one organisation. The Email login tab
  starts both kinds, so after Google's redirect its partner landed on another page and had to find the tab again (the
  partner guide warned about it). The page that started an action wasn't known after the redirect: the SPA's history
  state doesn't survive it.
- Decision: `POST /api/orgs/:org/actions` takes `returnTo: {page, appId?}`, a page name from the kind's allowlist
  (`origin.add` origins; `policy.set`, `raw_sign.on` signing; `app.resume` suspend; `app.settings` sessions or email;
  `owner_action` scope or email; `member.*`, `org.policy` members; the first is the default). An app's page is the
  action's own app, or, for an `owner_action` from the Email login tab, an app of the org on the action's scope (read
  with `getApp`). The console builds the path from the org, those ids and the page name, stores it in the action's
  `action_json` (outside the hashed action) and answers it on `GET /api/actions/:id`; an older action gets the kind's
  default page. Every page that starts a fresh sign-in names itself (Origins, Signing, Login & sessions, Email login,
  Suspend, the scope page, Members; Keys and Branding have none). The SPA uses the answer only when it is one of its
  own action pages (`/orgs/<id>/apps/<id>/<tab>`, `/orgs/<id>/scopes/<id>`, `/orgs/<id>/members`, ids of
  `[A-Za-z0-9_]`), else the kind's own page as before. Link text: "Back to Email login", "Back to Origins", "Back to
  Signing", "Back to Login & sessions", "Back to Suspend", "Back to the scope", "Back to members".
- Security: no open redirect. No URL or path from the request reaches the link: the console refuses anything but an
  allowlisted page name and a checked app id (`400 bad_request`, or `404` for an app that isn't the org's; nothing
  stored), and the SPA ignores an answer that isn't one of its pages. Tests with hostile values on both sides: the
  console's (`apps/console/test/stepup.test.ts`) a URL or `//host` as `returnTo` (any string fails the object schema),
  a URL or `..` as the page, an id with a path, an unknown key, a page the kind has no use for, an app of another scope
  or org; the SPA's (`web/test/email.test.tsx`) another origin, `//host`, `javascript:`, `..`, a query, a fragment, an
  unknown tab, a leading space, a backslash, non-strings. The link is a client-side route; the callback's own redirect
  is unchanged (`/actions/:id#`).
- Rejected: a `?next=` on the callback (a request value in a redirect); the SPA's history state or browser storage
  (lost at the redirect, or against the SPA's no-storage rule); guessing from the decoded action (the Email login tab
  shares kinds with other pages).
- Address impact: none.

### D713. The Email login tab and the scope page re-read once when a waiting on-chain change unlocks (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** (asked for by the user, reusing D701's approach; details decided while
  building, to confirm) · Built: `apps/console/src/email.ts` and `scopes.ts` (`now` in the answers),
  `packages/console-core/src/email-views.ts` (`AppEmailAnswer.now`), `web/src/pages/Apps.tsx` (`useReloadAt`),
  `web/src/pages/app/EmailLogin.tsx`, `web/src/pages/Scope.tsx`, `web/src/lib.tsx` (`clockTime`)
- Cause: both pages read the scope's pending changes once. After the timelock (1 minute on sandbox-dev, 24 h in
  production) they still said waiting and offered no Execute until the partner reloaded.
- Decision: the Email login and scope reads answer `now`, the Worker's clock that judged each change's `executable`.
  The page measures its own clock against it (D701's `clockOffset`) and sets one timer to the waiting change's unlock
  time (on the scope page, the earliest one) plus 1 s, then re-reads once; the answer, now `executable`, shows **Ready to
  execute** and **Execute the change** (scope page: **Execute**), and sets no further timer. Coming back to a hidden tab
  after that time (a sleeping laptop's timers fire late) re-reads at once. The shared hook (`useReloadAt`) also serves
  D701's app re-read, which gains the same visibility check. While waiting, the Email login tab says "You can execute
  this from HH:MM." (the reader's local time, the day added when it isn't today on the server's clock) and "This page
  checks again at that time: you don't need to reload it." Execute is offered only when the server says the timelock
  has passed, never by the reader's clock alone; an answer saying "not yet" for a time already past on its own clock
  sets no timer, so no loop of re-reads. Who can execute reads the same everywhere: "any owner" (in the console only an
  owner of an unfrozen organisation can; the contract itself lets anyone). After Execute the Email login tab says
  "Executed: users of this app can now sign in with email." only when this app's email login is on; otherwise
  "Executed: the scope now accepts email sign-in. This app still needs step 1 before its users are offered email."
  (another app of the scope proposed it, or this app turned email off while it waited).
- Rejected: polling while waiting; showing Execute from the client's clock (a fast clock would offer a call the chain
  refuses).
- Address impact: none.

## NEAR as a third wallet chain, core (branch `feat/near-core`), 2026-11-11

Built on `feat/near-core` (from `develop` @ 9854fb97), not merged, not deployed. Asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR
support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12. The shared interface of the parallel
builds is the main session's spec (relayer build D730–D739, contract build D740–D744, docs build D745–D749).

### D720. The NEAR key: derivation v1's additive tuple ("near", "ed25519", account); the address is the implicit account
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/derivation.ts` (`DERIVATION_V1_NEAR`, `nearSeed`, `chainPrivateKey`/`chainAddress` for `near`, `WalletAddresses`, `deriveWalletAddresses`, `nearPublicKey`), `addresses.ts` (`nearImplicitAccountId`, `isNearImplicitAccountId`, `isNearAccountId` moved here from `protocol.ts`, `nearPublicKeyString`, `parseNearPublicKey`), `scripts/gen-derivation-near-vectors.mjs`, `test/vectors/derivation-v1-near.json`, `test/derivation-near.test.ts`
- **This adds a derivation tuple; no existing address changes; it must be final before the address freeze.**
- Decision: `seed = HKDF-Expand(PRK, info("near", "ed25519", account), 32)`, the RFC 8032 seed, under derivation v1's own salt and expand label; the account is the NEAR implicit account (lowercase hex of the 32-byte public key), the key `ed25519:<base58>`. The tuple lives in its own frozen constant, not in `DERIVATION_V1`, so the Stellar and EVM guard (its vectors file and the SHA-256 of `DERIVATION_V1`) stays byte for byte as it was; NEAR has its own vectors (the same six S inputs, from an independent generator: node:crypto HKDF and Ed25519) and its own SHA-256 guard, and `@near-js/crypto` imports each exported key at the vector's key. The vectors file holds the export strings without their `ed25519:` prefix, so the secret scan's NEAR rule stays strict for it. `deriveAddresses` keeps returning exactly `{stellar, evm}` (the wallet proofs, the wallet record and the frozen tests use it); `deriveWalletAddresses` adds `near`.
- Rejected: adding `near` to `DERIVATION_V1` (it would change the frozen constants' hash, read as an address-changing edit); a named account (needs a registrar and an on-chain account per user).
- Address impact: a new NEAR account per user and scope; no Stellar or EVM address changes.

### D721. The NEAR codec: strict borsh, current transactions only, every action decoded or refused
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/near/borsh.ts`, `codec.ts`, `sign.ts`, `index.ts` (`@hana-id/core/near`, also in the root entry), `test/near-codec.test.ts`
- Decision: decode and encode `Transaction` (nearcore's V0: signer_id, public_key, nonce, receiver_id, block_hash, actions), `SignedTransaction`, every action through `UseGlobalContract` (tag 10; a nested delegate inside a delegate is refused), NEP-366 `DelegateAction` and `SignedDelegateAction`, and NEP-413's tagged payload. `TransactionV1` (a leading 0x01 and a priority fee, not accepted by the protocol yet), actions from tag 11 on (deterministic state init, gas keys) and access-key permissions other than FunctionCall and FullAccess are refused as `unsupported`; trailing bytes, lengths past the end, option tags other than 0/1 and invalid UTF-8 as `malformed`; invalid account ids as `invalid_value`; over 192 KiB, over 100 actions and method names over 256 bytes as `too_large`. Hashes: a transaction's sha256 (its hash and what is signed), NEP-461's `u32le(2^30 + 366) ‖ borsh(DelegateAction)`, NEP-413's `u32le(2^31 + 413) ‖ borsh(Payload)`. Every kind round-trips byte for byte against `@near-js/transactions` 2.5.1, and the signatures equal near-api-js's `KeyPairSigner`'s (test-only dependencies).
- Rejected: depending on near-api-js at runtime (size, and its looser decoding).
- Address impact: none.

### D722. Three NEAR requests, approval kinds `near_tx`, `near_message`, `near_delegate`, none ever auto-approved
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/approval.ts` (kinds, `ApprovalChain` `near`, context `{nearNetwork}` → `near:testnet` / `near:mainnet` in the digest), `protocol.ts` (`near_signTransaction`, `near_signMessage`, `near_signDelegateAction`; `WalletChain`; `hana_export {chain: 'near'}`), `packages/web/src/vault/signing.ts`, `test/near-approval.test.ts`
- Decision: as the spec says. The vault refuses (4100, "The request names another address") a transaction or delegate action whose signer or sender isn't the user's implicit account or whose key isn't its key; the popup's decoder refuses the same (`invalid_value`). The three kinds are in `NEVER_AUTO_APPROVED_KINDS`: no policy format covers NEAR, so every NEAR request opens the approval window. NEP-413's approval bytes are the tagged payload, rebuilt from the request's fields (a message that can't encode, e.g. a lone surrogate, is refused at the port).
- Address impact: none.

### D723. What the NEAR approval shows; account-control actions under the red warning (D110's rule)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/decode/near.ts`, `decode/request.ts`, `packages/web/src/auth/render-approval.ts` (`NEAR_ACCOUNT_CONTROL_BANNER`, `nearControlWarnings`, `NEAR_DELEGATE_NOTES`, `nearMessageWarning`, `nearNetworkLine`), `test/auth/render-approval-near.test.ts`
- Decision: built only from the popup's own decode: network (with what Hana checked, D726), sender, receiver, nonce, block hash and transaction hash; each action in plain words (Transfer in NEAR, FunctionCall with its method, attached deposit, gas in Tgas and its arguments as JSON re-indented in their own key order with unsafe characters `\u`-escaped, or hex when not strict JSON, shown in full behind a disclosure past 1,500 characters); the NEAR leaving the account (Transfer and FunctionCall deposits; Stake shown apart; DeleteAccount as "all of it"). Mirroring D110 (shown, not refused): AddKey (any permission), DeleteKey (removing the Hana key says the user loses control), DeleteAccount, DeployContract and UseGlobalContract of the user's own transaction or delegate action get the red banner and a warning each; DeployGlobalContract only publishes code and gets none; a relayed delegate inside the user's transaction acts on its own sender and gets none. A delegate action says a relayer pays the fee and that it names no network, with its expiry (`max_block_height`). A NEP-413 message names its recipient first and prominently, then the message (text, or hex when not display-safe) and the no-network note.
- Address impact: none.

### D724. The NEAR key export: `ed25519:` + base58(seed ‖ public key); the API's `exportChain` left out for NEAR
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/export.ts` (`nearSecretKey`, `exportStringOf`, `addressOfExport('near', …)` checks the two halves agree), `packages/web/src/auth/export-page.ts`, `key-reveal.ts`
- Decision: the export window shows and copies the NEAR key in the form near-cli, near-api-js and NEAR wallets import, with the safeguards unchanged (fresh login, typed confirmation, guarded buttons, auto-hide, erase). The API takes `exportChain` `'stellar'` or `'evm'` only (`apps/api/src/login.ts`), so a NEAR export sends none and its `key_exported` event is recorded with no chain until the API accepts `'near'` (D728).

### D725. Compatibility: `near` in the addresses only for SDK 0.4.0 or later; the record and the API shapes unchanged
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/protocol.ts` (`PortAddresses.near?`, `NEAR_SDK_MIN`), `packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts` (`sdkTakesNear`, `portAddresses`, the unlock's derivation), `test/vault/near.test.ts`
- Cause: SDKs 0.3.0 and 0.3.1 check the address object's exact keys (`isPortAddresses`), in `ready`, `hana_status`, `hana_login` and `accountsChanged`: an extra `near` would make them drop the whole message, stranding the tab.
- Decision: the vault adds `near` only for an SDK whose hello names `NEAR_SDK_MIN` (0.4.0) or later; older SDKs get exactly `{stellar, evm}`. A new SDK takes addresses with or without `near` (an older vault sends none) and then refuses `hana.near` requests and `exportKey('near')` locally (an older vault would drop them unanswered). The NEAR account is derived from PRK at login and at every unlock, never stored: the record keeps exactly `{stellar, evm}`, so an open tab of an older vault bundle reading a newer record sees what it always did, and a record written before NEAR unlocks with NEAR. The identity token's wallet proofs and `POST /v1/wallets/record` stay exactly Stellar and EVM (the API's shapes); NEAR in either is the API change of D728.
- Address impact: none.

### D726. NEAR networks: the claim checked on the env's RPC; test apps testnet only; delegate actions bound by key, nonce and expiry
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, and after the branch's automated security review (two medium findings), confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/networks.ts` (`mainnetOfRequest` for NEAR, `isTestNearNetwork`, `TEST_APP_NETWORK_RULE` names NEAR), `packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts` (`checkNearBlock`, `checkNearDelegate`, `NEAR_DELEGATE_MAX_BLOCKS`), `vault/near.ts` (`blockExists`, `accessKey`), `vault/signing.ts`, `auth/render-approval.ts` (`nearNetworkLine`)
- Cause: NEAR's bytes name no network. A transaction is tied to one by its block hash (it runs only with a recent block of the network it is sent to); a delegate action has no block hash; a NEP-413 message has nothing.
- Amended by D729 (the nonce floor, both providers for test apps, relayed delegates refused). Decision: (1) every app's `near_signTransaction`: on the env's RPC (testnet), a `testnet` claim's block hash must be a known block (4100 `near_block_unknown`; RPC unreachable: `api_unavailable` `near_rpc_unavailable`, fail closed), a `mainnet` claim's must not be (4100 `near_network_mismatch`; unchecked when the RPC is down). (2) A test app's `mainnet` request is refused at once (`mainnet_not_allowed`); the mainnet demo never covers NEAR. (3) A test app's delegate action, on testnet's RPC at final finality: the sender's access key exists with this public key (`near_key_unknown`), nonce > the key's (`near_delegate_nonce_used`) and < height × 10^6 (`near_delegate_nonce_too_large`), height < `max_block_height` ≤ height + 10,000 (`near_delegate_expiry`); fail closed. On mainnet nearcore refuses a nonce ≥ height × 10^6 and an expired action, so it could run there only while mainnet's height is between nonce / 10^6 (≥ the testnet height the key was added at, ≥ 277 M for any Hana NEAR key) and `max_block_height`. Measured 2026-11-11: testnet 277.2 M, mainnet 224.0 M, testnet at ~1.7 blocks/s; the ranges don't overlap and a gap of ~53 M blocks closes only if mainnet's block rate exceeds testnet's (years at best). A window on `max_block_height` alone would not bind (testnet is ahead, so a testnet-height expiry lies in mainnet's future). (4) NEP-413 messages, like SEP-53 and EIP-191 (D35), name no network and are not refused for test apps; the popup says so. (5) The popup labels the network: a transaction on the env's network "Hana found its block hash on testnet", a test app's delegate action "Hana checked your key, nonce and expiry on testnet", anything else "as the app says: Hana can’t check this".
- Rejected: refusing test apps' delegate actions (the hackathon's gasless demo needs them); trusting the claimed network (the review's finding 2).
- Open: a live app's delegate action and any NEP-413 message stay valid wherever the account has the key (`docs/security.md` "Known open issues").
- Address impact: none.

Until then the vault sends today's shapes.
- Address impact: none.

### D729. The NEAR review's fixes: relayed delegates refused, who pays in a delegate action, the nonce tied to the height
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: from the branch's full security review (one high, three medium, eight low findings), decided while fixing, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Amends D723 and D726 · Built: `packages/core/src/near/codec.ts` (`nearRelaysDelegate`), `near/delegate.ts` (`nearDelegateNonce`, `nearDelegateNonceFloor`, `NEAR_DELEGATE_MAX_BLOCKS`, `NEAR_NONCE_PER_BLOCK`), `near/sign.ts`, `decode/near.ts` (`nearDeposits`' burn and inner deposits, `NEAR_GLOBAL_CONTRACT_YOCTO_PER_BYTE`, `ignoreBOM`), `decode/request.ts`, `export.ts`, `packages/web/src/vault/signing.ts` (`NEAR_RELAYED_DELEGATE_RULE`), `vault/vault.ts`, `vault/near.ts` (both providers for test apps), `auth/render-approval.ts`, `auth/approve-page.ts`, `client/near.ts`; tests `core/test/near-review.test.ts`, `web/test/vault/near-signing.test.ts` and additions to the NEAR suites
- H1, a transaction relaying a delegate action: nearcore's `total_deposit` counts a Delegate action's inner deposits, so the transaction's signer prepays them; the popup showed 0 leaving. Hana now refuses such a transaction outright, in the popup's decoder (`unsupported`), at the port (4100 `near_relayed_delegate`) and in the signer: a wallet user is not a relayer.
- Who pays in a relayed delegate action (nearcore `apply_delegate_action`, read 2026-11-11): the relayer's transaction pays the gas and prepays every deposit and transfer of the delegate's actions; the actions then run as a receipt whose predecessor is the user's account. On success the deposits reach their receivers; on failure they are refunded to the predecessor (the user), and unused gas to the relayer. The user's balance goes down only for actions on the account itself: DeleteAccount (everything), Stake (locked), DeployGlobalContract (burnt). The popup's relayer note and the guide say exactly that (D723's "still comes from your account" was wrong).
- M1, the nonce: D726 bounded only nonce > the key's nonce, about (the height the key was added at) × 10^6, so once mainnet passed that height a kept action would have been valid there for good. The nonce must now also be above (testnet's height − NEAR_DELEGATE_MAX_BLOCKS) × 10^6 (4100 `near_delegate_nonce_stale`). Corrected after the re-review: that does not stop a replay, it dates it. nearcore runs a delegate action on any network whose own height H has nonce < H × 10^6 and H ≤ max_block_height; the bounds pin H to a fixed window of at most 20,000 blocks around testnet's height h at signing (about 700 with `nearDelegateNonce` and a 600-block expiry). Mainnet (224.0 M vs testnet's 277.2 M on 2026-11-11, both ~1.7 blocks/s) passes through that window about 361 days later, when a kept signature could run there if the user's implicit account exists on mainnet with that key and a lower nonce. Hence the test-app rule below, which makes such a replay call nothing.
- Test apps' delegate actions (after the re-review): only FunctionCall and Transfer (4100 `near_delegate_test_app_action` for AddKey, DeleteKey, DeleteAccount, DeployContract, DeployGlobalContract, UseGlobalContract, Stake, CreateAccount), and the receiver a `*.testnet` account other than the user's own (`near_delegate_test_app_receiver`), checked before any RPC read (`nearTestAppDelegateProblem`, `@hana-id/core/near`). On mainnet `testnet` doesn't exist (checked 2026-11-11), a top-level account under 32 characters can be created only by `registrar`, and `x.testnet` only by `testnet`: a replayed call or transfer reaches a missing account and fails, its NEAR (the relayer's) refunded to the user. Residual: a zero-deposit call in the user's name if `registrar` ever created `testnet` there; accepted for test apps, whose addresses must never hold mainnet funds (the guide and `partner-start-here.md` say so). Live apps are not restricted; their binding is mainnet-readiness row 1.21. Considered, not built: a mainnet RPC read that the key doesn't exist there (TOCTOU, and no mainnet RPC in the vault's CSP). For a test app the NEAR reads need two providers outside local* envs (`near_rpc_single_provider`, `api_unavailable`, fail closed; sandbox-dev has `rpc` fastnear and `rpcFallback` rpc.testnet.near.org).
- Popup (after the re-review): a box that holds more than it shows (`scrollHeight > clientHeight` after layout, again on resize) gets an always-visible scrollbar and "This box holds more than it shows (N characters): scroll through all of it before you approve." (`markOverflowing`, shared by every request kind's `pre.message`, Stellar and EVM messages included; their inline hex was never height-capped); a call to a contract on the user's own account raises the red banner and its total reads "Unknown: the contract on your account decides"; a delegate action that takes none of the user's NEAR reads "None of your NEAR (the relayer pays the fee and the NEAR attached). Tokens the calls move are yours."; a NEP-413 recipient that is not exactly the page's host or origin gets one factual line in the warning style, whatever its shape (a page picks the recipient, so no shape softens it; an automated review undid a pattern exemption); operation and action lists number once (their headings), `ol.ops` has no list numbers. `nearDelegateNonce` takes an optional `lastUsed`.
- Final check: the approval page watches each box with a ResizeObserver (the window's resize event where there is none; `watchOverflowing`), tested; an env counts as local for the two-provider rule only with a `local*` name AND a loopback vault origin (`nearLocalEnv`); `independentEndpoints` compares normalised URLs, so one provider spelled two ways is one. nearcore accepts it (below height × 10^6) and sets the key's nonce to it after use; later transactions and delegate actions continue from it (the bound only grows with the height). `nearDelegateNonce({ keyNonce, blockHeight })` returns max(keyNonce + 1, (blockHeight − 100) × 10^6) and throws at the bound.
- M2: DeployGlobalContract burns `global_contract_storage_amount_per_byte` (10^20 yoctoNEAR, 0.0001 NEAR, per byte) from the account it runs on; it is now counted ("NEAR burnt") and warned about. UseGlobalContract burns nothing (only storage for the identifier).
- M3: arguments and NEP-413 messages are shown whole in the popup's scrolling box (never folded), with "Long: N characters. Scroll through all of it before you approve." past 1,500 characters.
- Lows: a BOM keeps arguments as hex (L1); a call to a contract on the user's own account is warned about (L2); the export check zeroes its decoded key buffer (L3); for test apps the block, key and height reads go to both of the env's providers when it has two, every answer must pass (L4); `relay`'s deadline covers reading the body (L5); the guide says the relay is available where the environment runs one (L6); the popup flags a NEP-413 recipient that isn't the page's host and writes out non-ASCII ones with \u escapes (L7); unit tests pin the NEAR mainnet guard and the NEP-413 account check (L8).
- New refusal reasons: `near_relayed_delegate`, `near_delegate_nonce_stale`.
- Address impact: none.

Unknown keys in `near` are refused (`.strict()`). sandbox-dev: `hana-id-guestbook-dev1.testnet`, named like its other accounts (`hana-id-<role>-dev1.testnet`). Nothing else hard-codes the name.
