### D741. The guestbook contract: 50 latest messages in a ring, newest first, no owner and no upgrade path
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built: `contracts/hana-guestbook` (`src/lib.rs`, unit tests in `src/tests.rs`, `README.md`), near-sdk 5.24 like `hana-signer`
- Decision: `add_message({text})` stores `{account_id: predecessor, text, block_timestamp_ms}` and returns it with `index` (its position in the full history, 0 for the first message: added to the spec's three fields so a page can key a list). The text is trimmed (`str::trim`, Unicode White_Space) and must then be 1 to 200 characters, counted as Unicode scalar values, not bytes or UTF-16 units. The method is not payable: a deposit is refused, so a caller never loses NEAR to it. Only the latest 50 messages are kept, in a ring (slot `index % 50`), with a running `total_messages` counter. `get_messages({from_index?, limit?})` lists the kept messages newest first (`from_index` 0 = the newest; `limit` defaults to 50 and is capped at 50, a larger value is clamped, not refused; past the end, `[]`). `total_messages()` counts every message. `new()` runs in the deploy transaction; there is no owner, admin method, upgrade or migration.
- Why: the contract account pays for storage (the caller is a zero-balance account), so storage must be bounded: 50 of the largest messages take 46 250 bytes (under 0.5 NEAR), measured in the unit tests, and storage stops growing once the ring is full (unit and sandbox tests). Newest first suits a guestbook page. No owner means no key on chain decides anything but the account's own (D743).
- Security: the text and the account id are attacker-controlled bytes; a page renders them as text, never HTML (the README says so for the UI builders). Anyone can write and 50 messages push the rest out; spam control is the relayer's.
- Rejected: refusing `limit > 50` (clamping is the usual NEAR paging behaviour); a storage deposit from the caller (a zero-balance account can't pay); filtering control or markup characters in the contract (the page's job; the contract stays a byte store).
- Address impact: none.

### D742. Under a meta transaction the predecessor is the user; what the relayer must know
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built: `contracts/integration-tests/tests/guestbook.rs` (NEP-366 delegate actions built with `near-primitives` and sent over the sandbox's JSON-RPC with `near-jsonrpc-client`: near-workspaces has no Delegate action; the four crates are the versions near-workspaces already uses)
- Findings on near-sandbox 2.13.4, each an assertion in the test: (1) `add_message`'s predecessor under a relayed delegate action is the **user's account**, not the relayer's. (2) The user's implicit account must exist before its delegate action can run (`AccountDoesNotExist` otherwise); a transfer of **0 yoctoNEAR** creates it with the user's key as its full-access key and a balance of 0 (182 bytes, a NEP-448 zero-balance account). (3) The user's balance stays 0 after the relayed call: unused gas is refunded to the relayer. (4) The relayer's transaction reports `SuccessValue` even when `add_message` fails (it ran only the Delegate action): the relayer must look for a failure in every receipt outcome. (5) A replayed signed delegate action fails with `DelegateActionInvalidNonce`. (6) Gas: the `add_message` receipt burns about 1.40 Tgas for the largest message (1.45 Tgas once the ring is full and it replaces the oldest), the whole relayed transaction about 2.94 Tgas; the test attaches 30 Tgas and fails above 10 Tgas burnt.
- For the relayer build (D730–D739, theirs to decide): 30 Tgas on the delegate action's `FunctionCall` is ample; `/v1/near/activate` can be a 0-yoctoNEAR transfer; the guestbook account to allow is `near.demoGuestbook`.
- Address impact: none.

### D743. `deploy-guestbook`: a dry run by default, deploy and `new()` in one transaction, never a redeploy, `--lock` to drop the key
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: **asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-11** · Built: `scripts/deploy-guestbook.ts`, `scripts/lib/guestbook-deploy.ts`, `scripts/test/guestbook-deploy.test.ts`, `docs/operations.md` "Hackathon demo guestbook (NEAR)"
- Decision: a tool of its own beside `deploy-contract` (which stays hana-signer's alone), in its style: it reads the chain, prints the plan and changes nothing without `--yes`. It builds the wasm as hana-signer's is built for deploys (`cargo near build non-reproducible-wasm --no-abi`; `--wasm`, `--skip-build`), checks the balance (storage for the account's bytes, the code and 50 000 bytes of messages, plus 0.1 NEAR of gas), and sends one transaction from the account's own full-access key (the near CLI legacy keychain): `DeployContract` and `new()`, so no one can initialise the contract in between; then it checks the code hash and `total_messages() = 0`. It never redeploys: a deployed guestbook is "done", other code or another guestbook build is a blocker, and a new version goes to a new account. It blocks, printing the command that fixes it, on a missing or underfunded account, a keychain key that isn't a full-access key there, an account without keys, or an RPC on another chain. `--lock` deletes every access key on the account, in the deploy transaction or on its own once deployed.
- The key left after a deploy: the full-access key `near` CLI created with the account. It is the only power over the guestbook (it can deploy other code and rewrite every message and author). Recommended: lock once the demo has worked on testnet, then delete the key file. After the lock the account can never change or be deleted; its ≈ 2 testnet NEAR stay staked.
- Not done by the build (the user runs it): the account creation and the deploy (`docs/operations.md`).
- Address impact: none.

`docs/api.md` "NEAR relay", `docs/security.md` "The NEAR meta-transaction relay", `docs/operations.md` "NEAR relay".

### D730. A Hana NEAR wallet's first transactions go through NEP-366 meta transactions that Hana's relay pays for (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided
  while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/api/src/near/` (`relay.ts`, `delegate.ts`, `relay-chain.ts`,
  `relay-config.ts`, `relay-funds.ts`), `relayer-key.ts` (`relayNear`), `rate-limiter.ts` (`spend`, `giveBack`)
- Decision: a user's NEAR implicit account (64 hex, zero NEAR) acts by signing a `DelegateAction`; `POST /v1/near/relay`
  wraps it in a transaction of Hana's relay account (receiver = the user's account, one `Delegate` action) and sends
  it; the user pays nothing. Testnet only.
- Rejected: funding each user's account (gives users NEAR to spend elsewhere and costs more per user); relaying
  arbitrary signed transactions (a user's own transaction needs the user's NEAR).
- Address impact: none (no derivation changes; the address is the core build's, D720–D729).

### D731. Activation is its own route: a zero Transfer creates the implicit account (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `POST /v1/near/activate`; `test-sandbox/meta-tx.test.ts`
- Facts (near-sandbox 2.13.4, protocol 86): a delegate from an account that doesn't exist fails `AccountDoesNotExist`; a
  0-yocto Transfer creates the implicit account (balance 0, 182 bytes, its key the full-access key, a zero-balance
  account under NEP-448's 770-byte allowance) and costs the relayer ≈ 0.0071 NEAR (70 Tgas burnt on the new account);
  `[Transfer, Delegate]` in one transaction still fails `AccountDoesNotExist`, and the new key's nonce (block height ×
  10^6) can't be known when the user signs. So the client activates, reads the nonce (the answer carries
  `accessKeyNonce` and `blockHeight`), then signs. Testnet (nearcore 2.14.0-rc.5, protocol 88 on 2026-11-11) is not
  measured: the amount is a manifest setting (`near.relay.activationYocto`, default "0", at most 0.01 NEAR) in case a
  network needs one.
- Rejected: folding activation into relay (fails on chain, above); funding with a minimum balance (not needed: zero
  balance works).
- Address impact: none.

### D732. Only zero-deposit FunctionCalls to allowlisted receivers, with bounded gas and expiry, are relayed (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `near/delegate.ts` (`decodeSignedDelegate`, `policyRefusal`), `relay.ts`
- Fact (measured): the relayer pays every deposit the inner actions attach (a delegated 1 NEAR Transfer from a
  zero-balance account moved the relayer's NEAR), and all their gas. A delegate action can make the relayer pay anyone.
- Decision: a strict borsh decoder (exact length, ≤ 4096 bytes, ≤ 4 actions, Ed25519 only, account-id rules); only
  `FunctionCall`, zero deposit, receiver in `near.relay.receivers` (sandbox-dev: the guestbook), inner gas together ≤
  `near.relay.maxGasTgas` (default 50, sandbox-dev 30); the sender is hex of the delegate's own key and the signature
  verifies; from the chain: the account and key exist, the nonce is unused and below (height + 1) × 10^6, and
  `max_block_height` is 3 to 1000 blocks ahead (NEAR accepts any height ahead). The relayed `Delegate` carries the
  exact bytes decoded. A failed inner call is answered `contract_rejected` (the transaction's own status is
  `SuccessValue`; every receipt is read).
- Rejected: per-method allowlists (receivers are Hana-chosen contracts; revisit with partner receivers, readiness 1.21).
- Address impact: none.

### D733. Configuration: manifest `near.relay` beside `near.demoGuestbook`, the var NEAR_RELAY, testnet only, fail closed (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `packages/env` `nearSchema`, `gen-wrangler` `NEAR_RELAY`, `relay-config.ts`
- Decision: `near: { demoGuestbook?, relay?: { account, receivers, maxGasTgas?, dailyBudgetNear?, perSenderPerDay?,
  perAppPerDay?, lowBalanceNear?, activationYocto? } }`; the relay account is its own (not the signer, relayer, owner,
  MPC, a watchdog or the guestbook), receivers never the signer, relayer or relay account. Absent, unreadable, without
  receivers or keys, or with `NETWORK` other than `testnet`: `503 relayer_unconfigured`. The request's `network` must be
  `testnet` (`mainnet` → `403 mainnet_not_allowed`), and the key object checks `NETWORK` again.
- Address impact: none.

### D734. A separate relay account with full-access keys, in the RelayerKey objects (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `relayer-key.ts` (`relayNear`, the role, `near-relay-key-<i>`),
  `NEAR_RELAY_KEYS`, `scripts/near-relay-keys.ts`
- Decision: a function-call key can't sign a `Delegate` action, so the pools can't be reused; the relay has its own
  account (`near.relay.account`) whose full-access keys are the Worker secret `NEAR_RELAY_KEYS`. Each key is one
  RelayerKey object (the same nonce reservations and retries as the pools; an object serves one role for its life; its
  stored reservation names account and key), picked by sha256(sender) so a request's copies meet (claims, D455). A key
  also in a pool turns the relay off. The account's balance is all a stolen key can take: keep it small.
- Rejected: a full-access key on `relayer` (would put the pools' account balance and keys at a full-access key's
  mercy); a new Durable Object class (a wrangler migration for the same nonce logic).
- Address impact: none.

### D735. Who may call: the app gate only (the SDK from the partner's page), for a directory-listed account (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `relay.ts` (`knownAccount`, `nearDirectory`; the session proof's
  `nearRelayPayload` / `provenUser` were removed after the re-review of 8b6fbdf5)
- Decision: the core build's SDK (`hana.near.relay`, `hana.near.activate`) calls both routes from the partner's page
  with the publishable key and no session credential, so both take the app gate (`appGate` kinds `near` and
  `near-activate`: an origin in force for the app, or the vault; their own per-IP windows) and require nothing more.
  Bodies: relay `{network?, signedDelegateAction}`, activate `{accountId, network?}`. The spend is bounded by the
  policy (D732), the limits and the budget (D736). A body may add the vault's session proof (the session key signs
  `identityMessage` with payload `"near-relay" ‖ borsh(network) ‖ sha256(signed delegate bytes)`, activate
  `"near-activate" ‖ borsh(network) ‖ borsh(accountId)`; within 60 s, the session live in the app's scope, once); when
  present it is checked and the request counts per user. Open (security.md (s)): anyone with a publishable key can use
  the relay within the limits; before mainnet the vault sends the proof and the routes require it, then the wallet
  directory's NEAR record binds `sender_id` to the user.
- Amended the same day after the security review: with `near.relay.requireKnownAccount` (default true) both routes
  act only for a NEAR account the wallet directory holds for a user of the app's scope (the `feat/near-directory`
  build records it at login, signed by the NEAR key), through one seam, `nearAccountKnown`; an unknown account is
  `409 near_account_unrecorded` (activate: `retryable`, `retry-after: 2`, since the record can lag the login); per-user
  limits key on the directory's user. `false` is testnet only (the schema); sandbox-dev runs `true` (the directory build is
  merged into this branch; the seam calls its `nearAccountUser`). The session proof was later removed (below).
- Rejected for this round: requiring the session proof (the SDK built in parallel calls from the partner page, D720–D729);
  a wallet proof by the NEAR key over the session key (any key the caller holds can sign it, so it proves nothing more).
- Address impact: none.

### D736. Limits and a daily NEAR budget, in the RateLimiter objects; two security event kinds (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `relay.ts` (`quota`, `reserveBudget`, `settleBudget`), `relay-funds.ts`,
  migration 0020, `console-core` `SECURITY_EVENT_KINDS`
- Decision: per IP 30 relays / 10 activations a minute (the app gate's window); per sender `perSenderPerDay` (100;
  sandbox-dev 50); per user 200 relays and 5 activations a day (later 2, the directory's user); per app 120 a minute and
  `perAppPerDay` (5000; sandbox-dev 2000) and `activationsPerAppPerDay` (200) a day; across the env `relaysPerDay`
  (20000; sandbox-dev 10000) and `activationsPerDay` (1000); the per-IP windows hold across every app (window names
  without the app id); each per-app cap and the per-app budget `appDailyBudgetNear` (1) must be below the env's (the
  schema and the parser refuse otherwise; after the security review of 2026-11-11); a later window's refusal gives the earlier back. The env's budget `dailyBudgetNear` (5) is an
  amount counter (`RateLimiter.spend`): a relay reserves (inner gas + 5 Tgas) × gas price, an activation 100 Tgas × gas
  price + its amount, then gives back the difference to what burnt (all of it when nothing executed). Past 80%:
  `near_relay_budget_high` (one a day); hourly, the account below `lowBalanceNear` (2) or missing:
  `near_relay_balance_low`. No D1 counter; 0020 only adds the two kinds. Not in the app's relay quota or the usage
  ledger (not billed).
- Address impact: none.

### D737. Answers: `{transactionHash, status}`, waiting up to 30 s for every receipt (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `relay.ts` `relayAnswer`, `relayer-key.ts` `NEAR_RELAY_OUTCOME_MS`
- Decision: `200 {transactionHash, status: "executed"}`; `422 contract_rejected` / `delegate_rejected` (`reason`) with
  `status: "failed"`; `504 timeout` with `status: "pending"` (poll the hash, never resend blind); the other relay codes
  as the pools'. The wait is `EXECUTED_OPTIMISTIC`, 30 s (a meta transaction settles in about three blocks).
- Address impact: none.

### D738. The sandbox lane runs the relay's own code against a real node (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `apps/api/test-sandbox/`, `vitest.sandbox.config.ts`, `pnpm verify`'s
  sandbox step

### D739a. After the review of 2026-11-11 (round 2): in-flight cap, gas-only settlement, reads counted first (proposed)
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: as D730 · Built: `relay-config.ts` (`inFlightCapPerKey`, `inFlightNear`, `relaysPerMinute`),
  `relayer-key.ts` (`maxInFlight`, `not_enough_balance`), `relay.ts` (`budgetSettlement`, `cachedHead`, the pre-chain
  windows), `rate-limiter.ts` (`charge`), `test/near-mock.ts` (keys and transactions bound to their account)
- Decision: each key object takes at most `inFlightNear ÷ (keys × (maxGas + 5 Tgas) × gas price × 12)` relays in flight
  (`503 relayer_busy` beyond); a `NotEnoughBalance` refusal keeps its reservation; an env-wide minute window; sandbox-dev
  `maxGasTgas` 10, `inFlightNear` 3, `relaysPerMinute` 200. A settlement gives back the reservation less what burnt
  less what an activation transferred, and charges a spend above it. The sender's day and the app's and env's minute
  (activate: 60 a minute per app, 300 across the env, existing accounts included) count before any chain read; the head
  block is cached a second. Per directory user: 2 activations and 200 relays a day. Amended after the next review the
  same day: a counter aimed at the sender (its day, the user's day) counts only a delegate that passed the nonce, expiry
  and already-relayed checks; before the chain reads only the sender's minute (10), the app's and the env's minute; a
  delegate's hash is remembered 20 minutes (refused `already_relayed` before any count), forgotten if nothing ran.
  Amended again (the review after): no sender-scoped window before the delegate is known fresh: a durable per-sender
  nonce floor (the highest nonce sent; only grows) drops anything at or below it with no chain read; the sender's
  minute window is gone; the daily windows are given back when nothing is sent or created. And once more: the sender's
  minute window comes back, after the floor (only the key's holder reaches it); a chain answer of a used nonce raises
  the floor to the chain's nonce and gives the app's and env's minute hits back; a failed floor write fails closed.
  Last, after the re-review of 8b6fbdf5: the optional session proof is removed from both routes (it cost chain reads
  before any counted window; the directory gives the user); a chain-stale delegate gives the sender's minute back too;
  activate counts an account's own minute (5) before the shared minutes; three explicit states: certainly not sent
  (the key object's `notSent`, before any broadcast) forgets the request, anything else (sent or unknown) raises the
  floor and keeps the copy mark; a `delegate_nonce_used` answer's `accessKeyNonce` is the lowest nonce Hana won't take (the larger of its floor and the chain's), which the SDK and the demo read; no field or code renamed. A concurrent copy of one activation
  answers `created: false`. The key-in-a-pool check compares public keys; the relay account is never `RELAYER_ACCOUNT`
  or `SIGNER_ACCOUNT`.
- Address impact: none.

### D755. The NEAR wallet record: Ed25519 over the record statement with chain "near", under a v2 proofs domain; only for SDK 0.4.0+ and an API that lists it
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/core/src/wallet-record.ts` (`WALLET_RECORD_PROOFS_DOMAIN_V2`, `WALLET_RECORD_CHAINS_V2`, `WALLET_RECORD_SIGNATURE_BYTES`, NEAR in `walletRecordStatement`, `verifyWalletRecord`, `walletRecordProofsHash`), `identity.ts` (`ProofChain`; `canonicalWalletAddress`, `signWalletProof`, `verifyWalletProof` take `near`), `api-types.ts` (`AppConfig.walletChains`, `apiTakesNear`), `apps/api/src/directory/record.ts`, `apps/api/src/handlers.ts`, `packages/web/src/vault/wallet-record.ts`, `vault.ts`; tests `packages/core/test/wallet-record.test.ts` ("the NEAR record", "the session signature with a NEAR record"), `apps/api/test/wallet-directory.test.ts` ("NEAR in the wallet directory"), `packages/web/test/vault/near.test.ts` ("the NEAR wallet record")
- Decision: the body's `wallets` may be `{stellar, evm, near}`. The NEAR entry is the implicit account id (64 lowercase hex, the only accepted form) and the NEAR key's Ed25519 signature (strict RFC 8032) over the existing record statement `"hana-id/wallet-record/v1" ‖ 0x00 ‖ env ‖ signer ‖ app ‖ scope ‖ path ‖ borsh("near") ‖ borsh(account) ‖ session_pk ‖ issued_at_ms`. With it, the session signature covers `sha256("hana-id/wallet-record-proofs/v2" ‖ 0x00 ‖ stellar, evm, near triples)` instead of v1's two: the domains differ, so a two-chain signature never covers a three-chain body (an attacker's NEAR record added to a victim's) nor the other way round. A two-chain body is unchanged (v1), so every older vault keeps working.
- Why it can't collide: every NEAR signature the vault's NEAR key makes besides this one is Ed25519 over a 32-byte sha256: a transaction's (nearcore checks `sha256(borsh(Transaction))`), NEP-366's (`sha256(u32le(2^30 + 366) ‖ borsh(DelegateAction))`), NEP-413's (`sha256(u32le(2^31 + 413) ‖ borsh(Payload))`); there is no raw NEAR request. Ed25519 binds the exact message bytes and the statement is always longer than 32 bytes (its domain alone is 24), so a record signature verifies as none of them and none of them as a record; its domain is no other Hana message's, and the NEAR key is its own (D720), so it is never a Stellar or EVM proof either. Tested both ways, including a NEP-413 message whose text is the statement.
- When the vault sends it: for an SDK whose hello names 0.4.0 or later (D725: the partner sees in its console what its SDK hands out) and only when the API's `GET /v1/app` lists `near` in `walletChains` (an older API refuses a three-chain body with `400`, which would also lose Stellar and EVM). The API always lists `["stellar", "evm", "near"]`.
- Rejected: a NEP-413-shaped proof with a Hana-only recipient (a partner page chooses NEP-413's message, recipient and nonce: the proof would be one approved message from a forgery unless the vault also refused that recipient, a second rule to keep right); a separate statement domain for NEAR (the chain is already in the statement); a retry with two chains after a 400 (D317's one call; the capability field says it beforehand).
- Address impact: none.

### D756. Migration 0019 widens two CHECKs; the NEAR row is written apart; the vault records NEAR once at an unlock until the API says it did
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/api/migrations/0019_near_wallets.sql`, `apps/api/src/directory/record.ts`, `store.ts`, `packages/web/src/vault/record.ts` (`NearRecordedMark`, `nearRecordedKey`, `parseNearRecorded`), `vault.ts` (`recordWallets(s, unlock)`, `nearRecorded`, `markNearRecorded`), `api.ts`
- Decision: 0019 rebuilds `end_user_wallets` (`chain` ∈ stellar, evm, near; `address` 42 to 64 characters) and `user_events` (`chain` may be `near`, never on a mainnet demo signature), as 0018 rebuilt `user_events`: same columns, rows, keys and indexes; expand-only. The API writes the NEAR wallet after the Stellar/EVM batch, as its own statement: before 0019 its CHECK refuses it and the rest stays written (`directory_near_unrecorded`, `no_migration_0019`); the answer adds `near: true | false`. So nothing breaks whichever deploys first; D763 still makes the migration first a rule. The vault sends the record at every login as before and, at an unlock, only when NEAR should be recorded and the IndexedDB entry `near|<record id>` doesn't hold this session's public key; it writes that entry when an answer says `near: true` ('session' mode only, and only while that session is still the vault's) and deletes it wherever the record is deleted (a logout, a dead record): what a logout leaves is still only the root pins. A user from before NEAR, or with a missed record, so gets the row at their next page load without a call at every load.
- Rejected: a new table for NEAR (every reader, the erasure and the retention job would need a second join); writing NEAR in the same batch (one refused row would lose all); a call at every unlock (one more API call and chain read per page load); a field in the session record (older vault bundles read it).
- Address impact: none.

### D757. `nearAccountUser(db, scopeId, accountId)` for the relayer; a missing row may be a record still on its way
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/api/src/directory/near.ts`, tests in `apps/api/test/wallet-directory.test.ts`
- Decision (as amended by D762 after the branch's security review): one indexed SELECT of at most two rows on `end_user_wallets` (`chain = 'near'`, `address`) joined to `end_users` (`scope_id`), ordered by `first_seen_at`, then `user_id`; it returns the internal id (`hu_…`) for the relayer's per-user limits (never to be put in an answer) when exactly one user of the scope lists the account, null when none does or two do (ambiguous, logged `near_account_ambiguous`: no honest pair of users of one scope derives one account, so the client never chooses whose limits are charged; the first version ordered by `last_used_at`, the client's `issuedAtMs`, which let it choose), and throws on a failed read (unavailable, not unknown).
- What "listed" means: a session of that user's account root, live on chain on that path when the record arrived, sent a record whose NEAR entry that account's key signed (D755). It proves the session's holder also held the key, not that Hana derived it: the API can't derive keys, so a client of the user's own can list a key it holds. D762's two rules bound that. The record is not part of the login's answer (D317): it normally lands within a second, can lag up to the vault's 15 s abort, or be missing (an outage, 0019 not applied, an SDK before 0.4.0), so null shortly after a login is retryable; for a session from before NEAR, the next page load records it (D756).
- Address impact: none.

### D758. Every screen that lists a user's wallets shows NEAR, under the other chains' rules; "No NEAR account yet" where there is none
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/console-core/src/users.ts` (`WalletChain`, `parseUserSearch`: 64 hex characters, any case, is a NEAR account), `apps/api/src/directory/read.ts` (order Stellar, EVM, NEAR; the export event's chain), `apps/console/src/users.ts` (the allowlist), `apps/console/web/src/pages/Users.tsx`, `apps/console/preview/fixtures.ts`, `apps/admin/public/app.js`, `apps/admin/src/users.ts`, `apps/api/src/home/apps.ts`, `packages/web/src/auth/home-api.ts`, `home-page.ts`, `home-export.ts`, `scripts/lib/admin-users.ts`, `scripts/admin.ts`; tests in each package
- Decision: the partner console's Users list shows the NEAR account shortened with its copy button like the others, its detail in full; a detail without one says "No NEAR account yet" (the list says nothing, to keep the row short). The console Worker's allowlist takes `near` (64 lowercase hex) and now leaves out a wallet of a chain it doesn't know instead of dropping the user (a known chain of the wrong form still drops the row). Partners see a NEAR account exactly as Stellar and EVM addresses (D310, D346, D411 unchanged): only their own scopes' users, and, from an honest vault, only an account their SDK 0.4.0 session recorded (the SDK gate is the vault's: the API takes a three-chain body from any holder of a live session, within D762's rules; amended after the security review). The admin's Users search and Support ID lookup find and show it ("NEAR"; a NEAR export says NEAR; a Home derive's export says "every chain"), with a hint where none is recorded. Hana Home lists it after Stellar and EVM with a NearBlocks (testnet) link, or a plain line saying none is on record; Home's export now compares each recorded address with its own chain's (a NEAR address was compared with the EVM one, which would have refused every move of a user with a NEAR row). The admin CLI's `user:find --address` takes a NEAR account. Search inputs name it.

- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/api/src/login.ts` (`EXPORT_CHAINS`), `apps/api/src/mainnet-demo.ts` (`recordKeyExport`'s fallback), `packages/web/src/auth/export-page.ts`, `apps/e2e/src/server/api.ts`; tests `apps/api/test/mainnet-demo.test.ts`, `packages/web/test/auth/export-page.test.ts`

### D760. The identity token's `wallets` stay Stellar and EVM: the spec promises a closed shape
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: nothing (docs only: `docs/architecture.md` "Partner identity token", `docs/integration.md` section 2)

Until then a partner reads `hana.near.accountId` and proves it with `hana.near.signMessage` (NEP-413). (`canonicalWalletAddress`, `signWalletProof`, `verifyWalletProof` and `walletProofMessage` take `near` already, for that later change; `IDENTITY_CHAINS` and the proofs hash stay exactly Stellar then EVM.)

### D761. Where a third chain shows up in text: what was updated, what was left

### D762. One NEAR account per user and key index; one user per NEAR account in a scope; the lookup never picks
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: from the branch's security review (M1: a directory row proves only that the session's holder holds the key), decided while fixing, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Amends D756, D757 · Built: `apps/api/src/directory/record.ts` (`nearConflict`, `NearRefusal`), `apps/api/src/directory/near.ts`, `apps/api/migrations/0019_near_wallets.sql` (`end_user_wallets_one_near`), tests in `apps/api/test/wallet-directory.test.ts` ("NEAR accounts: what a client can list") and `migration-0019.test.ts`
- Cause: with the user's own login and a client of its own, anyone can sign a record with any NEAR key they hold. Before this, (A) one user could list any number of NEAR accounts (the key is `(user_id, chain, address)`), each then a candidate for the relayer's paid activation, and (B) one account could be listed under several users, the lookup choosing by `last_used_at`, a time the client sets (±5 min), so the client chose whose per-user limits were charged.
- Decision: (a) a record whose NEAR account differs from the one this user already lists at this key index is refused whole: `409 near_account_mismatch`, nothing written, logged `directory_near_conflict` (error); migration 0019's partial unique index (`user_id`, `key_index`) where `chain = 'near'` makes it hold under concurrent writes (the loser's NEAR row is skipped, `nearCode: near_account_mismatch`). (b) A record of an account another user of the scope already lists writes the user's other rows but not the NEAR one (`near: false`, `nearCode: near_account_taken`, logged `directory_near_conflict`): the first lister keeps it. Not refused whole, because with an exported key a stranger could list someone's account first, and that must not cost the owner their directory rows. (c) `nearAccountUser` answers null when two users of a scope list one account. Scopes stay apart: the same account in two scopes (only possible with an exported key) is each scope's own row.
- Legitimate change: none. The account is derived from the path's PRK, so an honest vault sends the same one at every login for that user and key index. Only a derivation change (allowed before the address freeze, and called out then) would change it; the operator then deletes the old NEAR rows (`docs/operations.md`, "NEAR in the wallet directory"), and each user's next login records the new one.
- Stellar and EVM, reviewed and left unchanged: they have the same property today. A Stellar or EVM row also proves only that the session's holder held the key, the key is `(user_id, chain, address)`, so a client of the user's own can list any number of Stellar or EVM addresses under its own user, and an address may be under several users (shown as `sharedWith`, D311's residual). Nothing hands out value on those rows today (no relayer reads them), so this branch doesn't change them; the same rule for them would be a separate decision (an honest vault also derives one each per key index).
- Rejected: a unique index on (scope, account) (`end_user_wallets` has no scope column; adding one is a larger change than the write-path check); refusing a `near_account_taken` record whole (above); overwriting the first NEAR account with the second (it would let a client move a user's listed account at will).
- Address impact: none.

### D763. Migration 0019 before the API (a rule); the vault waits 30 minutes after `near: false` before an unlock resends
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: from the branch's security review (L3), decided while fixing, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Amends D756 · Built: `packages/web/src/vault/record.ts` (`near-deferred`, `NEAR_RECORD_DEFER_MS`, `NEAR_RECORD_CONFLICT_DEFER_MS`), `wallet-record.ts` (`nearRefusedIn`), `vault.ts`, `docs/operations.md`; tests in `packages/web/test/vault/near.test.ts`
- Cause: without 0019 every NEAR record is refused, and the unlock backfill (D756) resent it at every page load of every SDK 0.4.0 session.
- Decision: operations makes "0019 before the API" a rule (an API ahead of it still works). The vault keeps, beside the record, `near-deferred` with `untilMs` when the API answers `near: false`: no unlock resends before then, 30 minutes for `no_migration_0019` or `internal`, 24 hours for `near_account_taken` or `near_account_mismatch` (only a new login changes those). A login always sends the record, as before. The entry holds the session public key and a time, nothing else, and is deleted with the record.
- Address impact: none.

### D750. `hana.near.activate()`: the SDK creates the user's own account on testnet before its first gasless call
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/web/src/client/near.ts` (`activate`, `NearActivateResult`, the shared `#post` of `relay` and `activate`), `src/index.ts`, `test/client/near.test.ts`; `docs/integration.md` section 8 ("A new account: activate it first"), `packages/core/test/integration-doc.test.ts`.
- Decision: `hana.near.activate()` takes no argument and posts `{ accountId }` (the session's own implicit account) to `POST {apiUrl}/v1/near/activate` with `x-hana-key`, `credentials: 'omit'`, no referrer, `NEAR_RELAY_TIMEOUT_MS`; it resolves `{ created, accountId, accessKeyNonce?, blockHeight?, transactionHash? }` (the relayer build's answer; each optional field only in its exact shape, an answer for another account refused) and maps refusals exactly as `relay` does (with the relayer's `accessKeyNonce` and `retryable` in `data` when it sends them) (4100 with the API's code in `data.reason` and the HTTP status in `data.status`, `rate_limited`, `origin_not_allowed`, `app_suspended`, `api_unavailable`). Logged out, or with a vault without a NEAR account: 4100 before any request. The timeout stays armed until the body is read, for `relay` too.
- Why: a test app's delegate action is refused by the vault until the user's key exists on testnet (`near_key_unknown`), and a new implicit account exists only after a first transfer; no popup is needed (it moves no user funds), and a partner should not have to pass the account id it already has.
- Rejected: activating inside `relay` (two answers in one call, and the vault's check runs before relay); taking an account id argument (a page could ask the relayer to create anyone's account).
- Address impact: none.

### D751. The click signs at once: NEAR is read before the click, `prepareApproval` only when it couldn't be
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/demo/src/near-card.ts`, `src/near.ts` (`delegateNonce`, `transactionNonce`, `DELEGATE_TTL_BLOCKS`), `test/page.test.ts`, `apps/e2e/tests/demo.spec.ts`.
- Decision: the card reads the user's access key (nonce), the latest final block and the balance from the env's NEAR RPC when it appears, when the message box is focused or typed in (which also calls `activate` for a new account, once per account and page session; its answer's key nonce and height serve as the read, since the RPC can lag the new key) and every 30 s while the user is interested (5 minutes after the last focus or key, tab visible). A click with a read under 60 s old builds the borsh bytes and calls `signDelegateAction` synchronously, so the approval popup opens in the click; otherwise the click calls `hana.prepareApproval()` first, then reads (activating if needed), then signs into that window, and cancels the ticket if the read fails. The delegate expires at the final height + 600 blocks (inside the relayer's + 1000 and the vault's + 10,000). The nonce comes from one function (`delegateNonce`): core's `nearDelegateNonce` (D729: the key's nonce + 1, or (height − 100) × 10^6 if higher) counted from the highest of the key's nonce and any this page signed since its last read; at nearcore's bound the card says to wait a block. `activate` and `relay` are retried for about 20 s while the API answers `near_account_unrecorded` or `near_account_unknown` (the vault records the account in the wallet directory just after login), and twice more on `relayer_busy`. When the relayer answers `delegate_nonce_used` after signing (it holds the key at a higher nonce: another tab, or a chain read the page hadn't seen; the SDK passes on its `accessKeyNonce`), the card reads again, builds above that nonce and asks once more, which needs the user's Approve again (NEAR requests are never signed without it); a second refusal is shown. Any nonce or expiry refusal drops the read the page holds, so the next click reads fresh. The `add_message` call attaches 10 Tgas (it burns about 1.45; the relayer caps a delegate at 10 Tgas on sandbox-dev).
- Why: Safari and Firefox open a popup only within the click's activation; reading on focus covers the usual path (type, then click) with no extra click, and `prepareApproval` is section 8's documented fallback.
- Rejected: reading in the click and relying on the launcher's "Review in Hana" (an extra click on every first write); activating at login for every visitor (spends the relayer's activations on people who never write).
- Address impact: none.

### D752. The demo's NEAR settings come from the manifest; its CSP connects to the NEAR RPCs and the API, nothing else new
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/demo/src/config.ts` (`DemoNear`, `apiUrl`, `NEAR_TESTNET_EXPLORER`), `src/csp.ts` (`connectOrigins`), `test/config.test.ts`, `test/csp.test.ts`, `apps/e2e/src/build.ts`.
- Decision: the build reads `rpc`, `rpcFallback`, `apiUrl` and `near.demoGuestbook` from `envs/<env>.json` (as it reads `vaultOrigin`), validates them (https or loopback, a `.testnet` guestbook) and bakes them into the bundle; no host is hard-coded except NearBlocks' testnet explorer, as for Stellar and EVM. The page's `connect-src` is the EVM RPC, the NEAR RPC, the NEAR fallback and the API, as origins, each once. Without `near.demoGuestbook` the card shows the account, NEP-413 and export only.
- Why: the page now calls the API itself (`relay`, `activate` run in the partner's page) and reads NEAR directly; everything else stays in the vault frame.
- Rejected: exporting the SDK's generated envs (`HANA_ENVS`) to the page (it isn't public API, and the demo already reads the manifest at build time).
- Address impact: none.

### D753. The guestbook is attacker-controlled: parsed strictly, shown as text, invisible and direction-changing characters replaced
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/demo/src/near.ts` (`parseMessages`, `displayText`, `shortAccount`, `checkGuestbookText`), `src/near-card.ts`, `test/near.test.ts`, `test/page.test.ts`.
- Decision: `get_messages` is read with a 20-message limit; entries without a valid NEAR account id, integer index and time, or with a text over 800 UTF-16 units are dropped. Text goes into text nodes only (`textContent`, `dir="auto"`, `unicode-bidi: isolate`), never HTML, never auto-linked; tab, LF and CR become spaces; every other Cc, Cf, Co, Cs, Zl and Zp code point becomes U+FFFD, except a zero-width joiner between two pictographs (emoji sequences); text is cut to 200 characters. Authors show shortened, with the full id as a tooltip and "you" on the user's own. The input is checked as the contract checks it: Rust's `trim` (Unicode White_Space) and 1 to 200 Unicode scalar values, and a lone surrogate is refused.
- Why: anyone can write anything to the guestbook; a right-to-left override or a zero-width character could disguise a message or an author.
- Rejected: dropping unsafe messages entirely (hides that something was there); core's `isDisplaySafeText` as a filter (it would turn most emoji, which carry U+FE0F, into hex).
- Address impact: none.

### D754. Borsh from `@hana-id/core/near`, no NEAR SDK in the page; "Sign a transaction" sends only with NEAR for its fee
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user 2026-11-11 (NEAR support for the NEAR hackathon); details decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/demo/src/near.ts` (`addMessageDelegate`, `addMessageTransaction`, `NearRpc`, `TX_FEE_RESERVE`), `apps/demo/package.json` (`@scure/base`, already in the bundle through core), `src/near-card.ts`.
- Decision: the page encodes the `DelegateAction` and the `Transaction` with core's codec (the one the vault decodes with), so partners reading the demo see one implementation; `@near-js/*` isn't added. The built script grew from 93.12 kB (30.86 kB gzip) to 117.41 kB (38.75 kB gzip), the card and the codec together (+24.3 kB, +7.9 kB gzip). "Sign a transaction" builds a real `add_message` call (the message box's text, or a fixed one) with the key's next nonce and the latest final block hash; it sends it (`send_tx`) only when the account exists and holds at least 0.01 NEAR, else it shows the signed transaction and its hash and says it wasn't sent because the account has no NEAR for the fee, pointing to the gasless write.
- Why: a zero-balance account can't pay gas; broadcasting would only fail.
- Rejected: `@near-js/transactions` (a second borsh implementation and more bundle for the same bytes).
- Address impact: none.


## Profile names: set in Hana Home, shared per app (branch `feat/profile-names`), 2026-11-11

### D714. Users set an optional first and last name in Hana Home and share it per app; partners read it in identity tokens, the SDK and the console; staff see it in the admin
- Date 2026-11-11 · Status: asked for by the user ("a way for users to set their own name (i.e. first/last names) in
  Hana Home portal, and partners can read the names via SDK … this is an optional field"; "admins will see these names
  in the users list in admin portal, partners can also see in the users list in partner portal"). The user chose:
  sharing per app, turned on in Home, off by default; identity token claims plus a page method; a Name column on the
  partner console's Users screen. Details decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-12** · Built: hot-DB migration 0021
  (`home_profiles`, `name_shares`), `packages/core/src/identity.ts` (`normalizeProfileName`, `PROFILE_NAME_MAX`, the
  claims), `apps/api/src/home/profile.ts`, `identity/name.ts`, `identity/token.ts`, `directory/read.ts`,
  `rpc/admin.ts` (`profileNames`), `changes/retention.ts`, `scripts/lib/uid-erase.ts`; the Home page
  (`packages/web/src/auth`), the SDK (`getProfile`, `profile`, `profileChanged`; React `useProfile`), the console's and
  the admin's Users screens
- Decision:
  1. **Whose name.** The name belongs to the sign-in identity Home is signed in as (`home_profiles`, keyed by
     `(provider, sub)` as the wallet directory keys identities): one name per Google or email login, used in every
     scope. Both parts are optional, at least one set; each is NFC, trimmed, runs of spaces folded, 1–50 code points,
     one display-safe line (`normalizeProfileName`: no control, format, bidi, zero-width, private-use or variation
     character, refused rather than stripped). "Remove my name" deletes it and every share of it.
  2. **Sharing.** Per app × account (`name_shares`, keyed by the app and the account's User ID in its scope, as
     `email_consents`), turned on from the app's page in Home, off by default. Only for an app Home lists to anyone (not
     deleted, has had a login) and only once a name is set. The share holds no copy: the name is read through the
     identity that shared it, so an edit reaches every app at its next token and a removal ends them all. Any identity of
     the account may stop the account's share. A member-resolved account is confirmed on chain before a share or a stop
     (D661), as Home's other writes.
  3. **A linked login's share** (`via = 'member'`) counts only while the wallet directory lists that identity as a
     live member of the account and the share is no older than its link (`LIVE_NAME_SHARE`): an unlink stops the name
     at once, and linking again doesn't bring it back. A root's own share (`via = 'own'`) can't outlive its place,
     since the User ID is computed from it. Residual: an unlink whose directory sync failed leaves the row `active`
     (D661's case) until the account's next login sync; and a member row the directory wrote with no `effective_at`
     (a sync from `get_identity` alone) can't tell a relink, so an old share would count again after one.
  4. **Partners.** Identity tokens carry the OIDC claims `given_name` and `family_name`, each only when set and shared
     (after `email`). The SDK reads them from the token in the page: `hana.getProfile({maxAgeMs?})`, `hana.profile`,
     the `profileChanged` event (only when the name changes), React `useProfile()`. No vault or protocol change, so it
     works with every vault; a change in Home reaches an open page at its next mint (up to about 55 minutes with the
     vault's cache, sooner with `maxAgeMs`). The partner console's Users screen shows the name shared with one of the
     org's live apps in the user's scope (a Name column, "Not shared" otherwise).
  5. **Staff.** The admin's Users screen shows each identity's name whatever the user shared (staff see the address
     too): the issuer directory's rows get their names from the API through a new staff-only
     `AdminRpc.profileNames` (≤ 50 identities a call, one SELECT), and the wallet directory's users carry the account
     name (the root's, else the first identity's that has one) and each identity's.
  6. **Erasure and retention.** `uid-erase` deletes the account's name shares of the scope's apps, and each identity's
     name, with every share of it, once the wallet directory sees that identity in no other scope (the issuer's
     `user_emails` rule). The monthly retention job deletes the name shares of apps deleted 30+ days ago.
  7. **The screens.** Home's front page has a collapsed "Your name" section ("Show my name": the two optional inputs,
     Save, "Remove my name" after a confirmation, and the apps the name is shared with, each with "Stop sharing"); each
     app's page has a collapsed name-sharing part ("Share my name with {App}" / "Stop sharing my name"). A share or a
     stop acts at once, with no confirmation (it can be undone; the sentence after it says tokens already issued keep
     the name up to an hour); only removing the name asks first. An app's state is the account's share, whichever of its
     logins made it, so any login can see and stop it. The partner console's Users list and detail have a Name column
     ("Not shared"); a malformed name drops the row, as a malformed address does. The admin's Users list, detail, wallet
     users and Support ID lookup matches show names; its search now asks the issuer for at most 50 rows a page (was 100;
     the screen already sent 50) so one `profileNames` call covers a page.
- Security: the name is personal data the user typed. It leaves Hana only to an app the user shared it with, and is
  never logged by the API, the CLI or the admin. Every Home read and write is keyed by the verified Home identity or
  the User ID computed from it (root.ts), so a request can't name another user's rows. Names are shown as text only
  everywhere (and are display-safe by construction). The claims are unverified data in the page: a partner backend
  verifies the token.
- Rejected: a copy of the name per share (an edit would have to reach every copy, a removal could miss one); sharing
  with every app automatically, and a partner-triggered sheet like email's (the user chose per-app sharing in Home); a
  live push of a Home change to open partner pages (it would need the vault's status read to carry it; the next token
  is enough for an optional display name); keying the name by account (an account is per scope, and Home signs in as
  one identity).
- Address impact: none. Nothing here reaches the contract, a path, a key or the session nonce.

## The Journear Passport rebrand and redesign (branch `feat/journear-design`), 2026-11-12

Built on `feat/journear-design` (from `develop` 6ab570b1) and its area branches; merged as PR 46 (`develop` b37ebb51) and deployed to sandbox-dev on 2026-11-12 by the user (checked by hand). No path, key
rule, protocol string or address changes: only what users read and how pages look.

### D765. Every Hana ID frontend follows the Journear Passport design system; the product is renamed for users
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: **asked for by the user 2026-11-12** ("can we update so that all our frontends follow this design system?", the Journear Passport design system v0.5, https://claude.ai/artifact/Ub6zWLCFWbyB4R6Z6Rukco); the scope, names, depth and fonts **decided by the user 2026-11-12** in answers; the token fixes below decided while building, for the user to confirm · Built: `packages/brand` (`tokens.css`, `components.css` (new), `fonts.css`, `fonts/`, `logo/`, `src/index.ts` (`BRAND`, `FONT_FILES`, `markSvg`), `src/check.ts`, `test/brand.test.ts`) · Amends D426 (its token set, typefaces and mark are replaced; its rules stand: one token set, fonts self-hosted on each origin, `font-src 'self'`, AA tested in both schemes)
- Decision (the user's):
  - **Full rebrand.** What users, partners and staff read: "Hana ID" → **Journear Passport**, "Hana" on its own (the company or service) → **Journear**, "Hana Home" → **Passport Home**. Code identifiers don't change: package names (`@hana-id/*`), SDK symbols (`createHana`, `HanaError`, `hana.*`), env and account names, origins, storage keys, message types, error codes, and every signed, hashed or domain-separation string.
  - **Scope:** everything in hana-id (both consoles, the sign-in, approval, export, email and share popups, Passport Home, the vault launcher, the demo and the smoke pages, the designed emails, and SDK and API messages), and in the sample partner repo only the elements that show Journear Passport itself. The sample keeps its Sodax styling.
  - **Depth:** the restyle, plus the system's behavioural patterns (the save bar, toasts, setting rows, choice cards, validate on blur, the confirm-and-sign layout, the 3-step export with its checkbox), plus its voice (plain and short, no crypto jargon for users).
  - **Fonts self-hosted:** Archivo 500/700/900, IBM Plex Sans 400/500/600 and IBM Plex Mono 400/500, all OFL 1.1, from Fontsource's npm builds (`@fontsource/*@5.3.0`), Latin subset, each licence beside them. Never Google Fonts, so no font request leaves our origins.
  - **App-name guard:** partner app names are also refused when they contain "Journear" or a look-alike; "Hana" stays refused; "Passport" alone is allowed (amends D686).
- Decided while building:
  - The system's `tokens.css` is taken as published (`--jp-*`), with three WCAG AA fixes: the light warning text is #935F12 (the system's #B7791F is 3.3:1 on its own warning background); the dark pressed primary is #2A9488 (#248578 gave its label 3.8:1); and `--jp-on-danger` is new (light text on the dark scheme's danger fill was 2.7:1). `--hana-*` is gone, with no aliases.
  - `components.css` is the system page's `.jp-*` rules as published, minus the page's own chrome. Its danger button reads `--jp-on-danger`, and a reduced-motion rule is scoped to `.jp-*`.
  - The mark in code has a 106 × 100 viewBox, so the chevron's round tail isn't clipped.
  - Fontsource's Latin subset (U+0000–00FF and the usual punctuation) replaces Montserrat's wider U+0000–017F. Latin Extended-A characters (such as "Ł" or "ő") are drawn by the system fallback.
- Why: the user is moving the product to the Journear Passport brand. One token set and one component file keep every page consistent and make the next change a one-place change.
- Address impact: none.

### D769. Partner app names may not hold "Journear" or "Passport Home", besides "Hana"
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: "Journear" **decided by the user 2026-11-12**; "Passport Home" proposed while building and **confirmed by the user 2026-11-12** ("Keep it") · Built: `packages/console-core/src/names.ts` (`brandNameIn`, `journearWordIn`; `hanaWordIn` kept), `apps/api/src/changes/settings.ts`, `scripts/lib/admin-sql.ts` (`assertAppName`), `apps/email-issuer/src/mail.ts` (`displayAppName`); tests in console-core, the API, scripts and the issuer · Amends D686
- Decision: an app name is refused when its skeleton holds "Hana", "Journear" or "Passport Home", in any case, accent, look-alike (Cyrillic, Greek, Armenian, digits, `$`, `ø`), or split into separate letters. "Journear" is matched inside words ("MyJournear"); letters split by spaces or punctuation count only from the start of a word, so "Bonjour nearby" is allowed. "Passport", "Passport Travel" and "Passport Homes" are allowed. The refusal names the word that matched.
- Why: an app called "Passport Home" would get the subject "Your sign-in code for Passport Home", identical to the real Passport Home mail (what D620 and D686 closed for "Hana Home").

### D779. Passport Home's "Move this wallet" shows the NEAR key: a third address and a third choice, under the same safeguards
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/web/src/auth/home-export.ts` (`CHAIN_NAMES`, `HomeExportChain`, `addressRows`, the `unlocked` screen, `chainSecret`, `choose`), `home-page.ts` (`moving.chain`); tests `packages/web/test/auth/home-export.test.ts` ("NEAR: the third key of the opened wallet"), `apps/e2e/tests/home-export.spec.ts` · Amends D575, D582, D584; closes D761's first "Left" item

The sentence above them gains "the NEAR key for a NEAR wallet app". NEAR's steps 2 and 3 are titled "Your NEAR key" and show the account in the `.jp-kv` row; the key is NEAR's export form (`ed25519:` + base58(seed ‖ public key), D724), made inside one Show or Copy from PRK with `chainPrivateKey(prk, 'near', 0)` and zeroed in the same call, exactly as the other two. Everything else is the shared path, unchanged: one derive opens all three keys (no new request, no new sign-in), the typed `EXPORT`, the checkbox (D770), the guard on Continue, Show key and Copy key, the 60 s hide, the clipboard blank, the 5-minute erase, and nothing in the page's address can pick a chain. The Stellar and EVM screens are develop's, unchanged, except the shared "Your wallet is open" screen (the third row, the third button, the sentence).

- Address impact: none (key index 0, the same PRK and the frozen NEAR tuple; the golden test holds Passport Home to `derivation-v1-near.json` for an own path and a member's root).

### D780. NEAR's own notes on its key screens: the key is the account, it may not exist yet, Journear pays only for its approved calls
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 (the wording) · Built: `home-export.ts` (`homeExportNearNotes`, `HOME_EXPORT_NEAR_NOTES_TITLE`, `NEAR_NETWORK_NAME`, `nearNotes`), `css/export.css` (`.home-export-notes`, tokens only); tests "the NEAR screens say what is true of NEAR alone …"
- Decision: on NEAR's step 2 (under the danger alert every chain gets, D430's `EXPORT_WARNING`, above the typed word) and step 3 (above the key's box), an info alert (`.jp-alert-info`, `#home-export-near-notes`) headed "Before you move a NEAR account" lists three fixed sentences: (1) "This key is the NEAR account itself: the account's name above is made from the key. Whoever imports it into a NEAR wallet app has full control of the account. If that app removes this key from the account, this app loses the wallet too." (2) "Choose NEAR testnet in the other wallet app. An account that was never sent any NEAR doesn't exist on NEAR yet: until it gets its first NEAR, a wallet app may show it as not found or not import it." (3) "Journear pays NEAR fees only for a few calls it has approved, such as its demo's, and only in apps that use Journear Passport. In another wallet app, every transaction's fee is paid from this account's own NEAR." The names come from `BRAND`; the network's name from the env's `network` (a table typed by it, as the NearBlocks link is), so a later network can't silently keep "testnet". The Stellar and EVM screens show none of it. Info, not warning or danger: the danger alert above is the one that says what the key can do, and the system keeps one danger per view.
- Why: on NEAR the key is the account (an implicit account named after its public key), so removing it elsewhere cuts off the app; an implicit account exists only after a first transfer (D731) and some wallets can't import one that doesn't; and Journear's relayer pays only for zero-deposit calls to allowlisted receivers (D732), so a user moving out must not expect free transactions.
- Rejected: adding these to the shared warning (Stellar and EVM users would read things that aren't true of their chains); a link to a NEAR wallet (a fixed third-party link on the key screen is an endorsement Journear hasn't made).
- Address impact: none.

### D781. No API, audit or migration change: the Passport Home derive stays one `key_exported` row with no chain, "every chain (Passport Home)"
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: nothing in `apps/api` but a comment (`home/login.ts`); tests "writes nothing … no message or request carries the NEAR key or its seed" (the derive body still has no `exportChain`)
- Decision: as for Stellar and EVM, the event is attempted once per derive the API answers with a key, before the user picks one, with `chain` NULL and `app_id` NULL (D520, D98 item 6); the admin's Users page already reads it as "every chain (Passport Home)" and "one sign-in opens every chain", which now includes NEAR. `POST /v1/home/login` still refuses `exportChain` (`REFUSED_FIELDS`). No CHECK constraint is involved (NULL passes before and after migration 0019), so no migration.
- What the row is (corrected 2026-11-12 after the branch's security review, L1; the code is older than this branch and the same for every chain and for the export window's `/v1/login`): best effort. `recordKeyExport` runs after the answer is built, in the background (`inBackground`: `waitUntil`, errors swallowed), so the key can reach the page before the row exists, and the row isn't retried: a failed insert, or an env without `USER_ID_KEY` / `IDENTITY_SUB_KEY`, is logged `key_export_unrecorded` (warn, the request id only) and the user still gets the key. A derive the page recovers from NEAR (the API's answer was lost or the API failed after the relay, D581) can have no row: the API returns its error before the event. A derive by an identity with no directory row is still recorded (the user id is computed, not looked up; `home-login.test.ts` "a stranger's derive records key_exported"). Whether the insert should be awaited before the 200 is readiness row 1.23 and security.md open issue (t).
- Rejected: recording which key was shown (a second request after the derive, from a page that holds the key: a new endpoint and a new way to fail for a label the derive's row already covers).
- Address impact: none.

### D778. The pack check type-checks the partner guide's NEAR samples against the packed tarballs
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `scripts/lib/pack-check.ts` (`codeBlocks`, `sampleModule`), `scripts/pack-check.ts` (`guide-near.ts`, `GUIDE_NEAR_JS`), `scripts/test/sdk-pack.test.ts`; `docs/operations.md` "Releasing the SDK packages"; the samples in `docs/integration.md` section 8 ("NEAR"), whose figures `packages/core/test/integration-doc.test.ts` checks against `envs/sandbox-dev.json` and the API's `NEAR_RELAY_LIMITS`
- Cause: the guide's NEAR section is the code partners copy for a flow with several steps (activate, the nonce, the delegate action's bytes, sign, relay, NEP-413 verification); a sample that doesn't compile against the SDK they install fails them at the first step, and nothing checked the guide's code before.
- Decision: `pnpm run pack:check` takes every `ts` block between `### NEAR` and `### Raw signing` of `docs/integration.md`, merges their one-line named imports per module, puts them after a prelude that declares what earlier sections set up (`hana` from `createHana`, `button`, `onSent`, `onError`) and type-checks the result as `guide-near.ts` in its throwaway project, with the installed tarballs, NodeNext and Bundler resolution and `skipLibCheck` off, beside `pack-smoke/`. The samples form one module in page order (a later one may use an earlier one's declarations), never run. The transaction sample's `@near-js/crypto`, `transactions` and `utils` are installed in that project at `scripts/package.json`'s exact versions. A guide whose NEAR section can't be extracted fails the check before anything is packed.
- Why: the tarballs' `.d.ts` are what a partner compiles against; the workspace's sources are not. Extracting from the guide means no second copy of the samples to keep in step.
- Rejected: a hand-kept copy of the samples in `scripts/pack-smoke/` (it drifts from the guide); a temporary file checked once (nothing would stop the next edit breaking a sample); checking every section's samples now (most predate this and use undeclared placeholders such as `xdr` and `tx`; a later change can widen the range).
- Address impact: none.

## The NEAR relay on the admin's System status page (branch `feat/admin-near-relay-tile`), 2026-11-12

From `develop` @ 1464a744. The staff System status page (D425, D772) gains a "NEAR relay" tile in Relayer funds, so
staff see the gasless relay (D730–D739) without a block explorer. No migration, no new var or secret, no route.

### D784. The NEAR relay's facts come through `AdminRpc.systemStatus`, read live by the API at each cold read
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/api/src/near/relay-status.ts` (`nearRelayStatus`), `apps/api/src/system-status.ts` (`nearRelay`), `packages/console-core/src/health.ts` (`NearRelayStatus`), `apps/admin/src/status.ts` (`nearRelayTile`); tests `apps/api/test/near-relay-status.test.ts`, `apps/admin/test/status.test.ts`, `apps/admin/test-spa/status.test.ts`
- Cause: the relay raised only two security events (`near_relay_balance_low` hourly, `near_relay_budget_high` at 80%); its balance, keys and spend were visible only on an explorer. The relayer tile's facts come from the watchdog's stored 5-minute reading of the relayer account plus the API's pool keys in `systemStatus`; the watchdog doesn't know the relay account, its keys or its spend, and the API holds all three.
- Decision: the API answers `nearRelay` in the same `systemStatus` call the page already makes: its state (off, `bad_config`, `no_keys`, `bad_keys`, on), the manifest's account and lines, `view_account` and `view_access_key_list` of the relay account (in parallel, 5 s per endpoint through its failover), the API's relay keys compared with the account's full-access keys by public key inside the API (`nearRelayKeys`, shared with `nearRelayReady`), and the day's spend (D785). The admin judges it as it judges the others: each part fails on its own (Unknown, with an issue unless the NEAR RPC tile already says every endpoint is down), the 30 s isolate cache, and the relayer tile's staleness rule on the reading's `readAt` (never stale today: the read is live).
- Calls: none added to the admin's page budget (still 20 on sandbox-dev, 22 at most) or to any cron; inside the API's status invocation two NEAR reads and one RateLimiter call when a relay config is set, none without.
- Rejected: a watchdog reading of the relay account like `relayer_funds` (a watchdog change and deploy on its own account, 576 more NEAR reads a day whether anyone looks or not, and the keys and spend would still have to come from the API); storing the hourly check's reading (a store to add, an hour old at worst).
- Address impact: none.

### D785. Today's spend is read from the budget's own RateLimiter, read only, env-wide, amounts only
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/api/src/rate-limiter.ts` (`spent`), `apps/api/src/near/relay.ts` (`nearRelaySpent`)

### D786. How the tile judges: the manifest's lines, a fifth for red, the API's 80%
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `apps/admin/src/status.ts` (`NEAR_RELAY_CRITICAL_DIVISOR`, `nearRelayTile`)
- Decision: balance (available: amount less storage, as the watchdog's) amber below `lowBalanceNear`, red below a fifth of it (every default pair of the watchdog's `relayerFunds` has its critical line at a fifth of its warning line: 5/1, 0.5/0.1, 0.1/0.02, 1/0.2), red with the account missing. Three lines: Balance, Today's spend, Keys.

- Note 2026-11-12, after the security review: the tile doesn't show the per-app budgets (one app can hit `app_budget_exhausted` while the tile is OK); the relay refuses slightly before the tile says "used up" (it reserves a worst case first); the spend includes in-flight reservations; a changed `near.relay.account` isn't caught (a key object still live refuses to relay until it is evicted, `relayer-key.ts` `loadNearKey`); a failing wallet-directory lookup with `requireKnownAccount` isn't covered. The review's three low findings were fixed: a missing key the admin can't show still counts (severity and count from the raw list), a balance or line that doesn't parse is Unknown, never OK, and the spend read has a 2.5 s deadline (`rate_limiter_unavailable` past it). `docs/operations.md` "System status (D425)" lists the gaps.
- Address impact: none.

## NEAR relay refusals: what the SDK passes on (branch `fix/sdk-near-relay-error-details`), 2026-11-12

From `develop` @ 1464a744, not merged, not deployed. Found while writing the partner guide's NEAR section (D778), which
documented it as a limitation. No API, vault or contract change. Numbered D788: D784–D787 are another branch's.

### D788. `relay` and `activate` refusals carry the sent transaction, NEAR's reason and `retry-after`, each only in its exact shape
- Date 2026-11-12 · Status: decided while building 2026-11-12, confirmed by the user 2026-11-12 · Built: `packages/web/src/client/near.ts` (`relayError`, `sentTransaction`, `retryAfterHeader`, the exported type `NearRelayErrorData`), `packages/web/src/index.ts`; `apps/demo/src/near-card.ts` (`sentPending`, the write's timeout branch, `UNRECORDED_REASON`), `src/errors.ts` (`relayTransaction`), `index.html` (`#near-pending`), `src/near.ts` (`DELEGATE_TTL_BLOCKS`'s comment); tests `packages/web/test/client/near.test.ts` ("the sent transaction, NEAR’s reason, retry-after"), `apps/demo/test/page.test.ts`, `test/errors.test.ts`; docs `docs/integration.md` section 8 ("Errors", the table, a sample the pack check type-checks) and its release notes ("After 0.4.0"), `docs/api.md` "NEAR relay", `docs/architecture.md` "NEAR", `apps/demo/README.md`
- Cause: the SDK turned the API's refusals into a `HanaError` with `data.status`, `data.reason` (the API's code), `data.requestId`, `data.accessKeyNonce` and `data.retryable`, and dropped the rest. The API (`apps/api/src/near/relay.ts` `relayAnswer`, `quota`, `reserveBudget`, `knownAccount`; `relayer-key.ts` `relayNear`) sends `transactionHash` and `nearTx` (one base58 hash) on every failure after the broadcast (the 504 `timeout`, both 422s, `near_rejected`, `near_error`, a `relayer_busy` whose transaction was dropped or got no valid nonce), `reason` on a 422 `delegate_rejected` (NEAR's own: `expired`, `invalid_nonce`, …), and a `retry-after` header (exposed by the CORS, `http.ts`) on 429s, the budgets, `near_account_unrecorded` (2), `relayer_busy` and `relayer_unavailable` (1). Without the hash a partner can't look up a relay that timed out and may still land; only Journear could, from the request id. `/v1/near/activate`'s failures past the relay are the same `relayAnswer`.
- Decision: additive, on `data` of the same error (no code, field or message changed; SDK stays 0.4.0, release notes "After 0.4.0"): `transactionHash` from `transactionHash`, else `nearTx`, only when base58 of 32 to 44 characters (the SDK's existing `isBase58Hash`), and dropped when the two are both valid and differ; `nearReason` from `reason` only on `delegate_rejected`, only lowercase letters, digits and `_`, at most 64 characters (another code's `reason`, `bad_delegate`'s decode error, is not passed on); `retryAfterS` from the `retry-after` header only as whole seconds 0 to 86,400 (a day: the daily budgets' reset), never an HTTP date. Nothing else of the body is copied (`executor`, the body's `status` word, any nested object). The hosted demo shows a timed-out relay that has a hash as an info note, "Sent, still confirming: view the transaction ↗" (NearBlocks, the hash checked as base58 again and URL-encoded, text nodes only as D753 asks), rereads the guestbook as before, and no longer shows it as an error; a timeout without a hash, or with a malformed one, stays the existing error text.
- Also, two small corrections found on the way: `DELEGATE_TTL_BLOCKS`'s comment said 600 blocks is about 10 minutes; at testnet's ~1.7 blocks a second it is about 6 (the guide already said 6; D751's own text names only the 600 blocks, so it is unchanged). The demo retried, and had a message for, `near_account_unknown`, which nothing sends: no file outside the demo names it (`git grep`), and the API's only directory refusal is `409 near_account_unrecorded` (`knownAccount`). Both removed; that code now gets the default "refused this request" text and no retry.
- Why: the hash is what a partner needs to tell the user "sent" rather than "failed" and to check before asking for a second approval; the other two are the API's own words, already sent and exposed. Strict shapes because the answer is a network response the page renders.
- Rejected: `data.reason` for NEAR's reason (it already holds the API's code); copying `nearTx` as a second field (the same value); clamping an over-long `retry-after` (an out-of-range value is not the API's, so it is dropped); a helper method on `HanaError` (the exported type is enough, and the guide shows the check); showing the demo's pending note for `contract_rejected` or `delegate_rejected` too (they ran and failed: an error is right).
- Address impact: none.
